# Reviewer Response — R. Decision after P4/P5 (2026-05-01)

I agree with the main direction of P4/P5, with two important qualifications.

The high-level conclusion is now much clearer than it was at 7500 iters:

```text
1. The "why can't we even reach 26 dB?" question was mostly a metric/protocol question.
2. v9.1a failed for a real technical reason, not because it was under-trained.
3. The next useful experiment should return to v9.0_best, not continue the v9.1 family.
```

## R1. P4 changes the interpretation of the 26 dB problem

P4 is a strong result. The audit shows:

```text
v9.0_best:
  RGB-256 = 24.524
  Y-256   = 25.687
  RGB-512 = 25.229
  Y-512   = 26.843
```

So the earlier worry that the architecture was fundamentally capped below 26 dB is not supported. Under the stronger Y-512 protocol, v9.0 already reaches 26.84 dB.

This does not mean the model is now "solved". It means the local training-time metric was too pessimistic for comparison against published LLVE numbers. The gap should now be discussed as:

```text
not: "model cannot reach 26 dB"
but: "model reaches 26.84 Y-512, still about 2 dB below 28.9-style reports"
```

That is a materially different research problem.

However, I would not state too strongly that the model is already fully protocol-comparable to every published method. Before using 26.84 as a paper-style headline number, we should freeze the exact audit protocol:

```text
Y conversion:        RGB-to-Y formula, full-range vs limited-range
crop rule:           center-512 vs full-resolution vs border shave
sequence averaging:  per-frame vs per-sequence
input resizing:      whether 512 is native crop or resized crop
checkpoint choice:   best selected by which validation metric
```

P4 is enough to resolve the internal "25 dB ceiling" confusion. It is not yet enough to claim a final external benchmark number unless those details match the target papers.

## R2. P5 is strong enough to kill RAFT-warp loss on SDSD-indoor

P5 is even more decisive than the v9.1a training curve.

The critical observation is not merely that LQ-flow is bad. It is that even HQ-flow on HQ-pairs worsens masked L1:

```text
HQ-flow oracle on HQ-pair:
  unwarped L1 = 0.0056
  warped L1   = 0.0074
  reduction   = -32.0%
```

This rules out the simplest rescue arguments:

```text
"RAFT-small is weak"        -> no, oracle-HQ flow also fails.
"LQ is too noisy"           -> no, HQ-to-HQ also fails.
"self target is wrong"      -> no, HQ target also shows the same sign.
"mask threshold is bad"     -> not the primary issue; mask coverage is high but the warp signal is still negative.
```

My reading is:

```text
SDSD-indoor adjacent frames contain too little exploitable motion.
The interpolation error introduced by bilinear warping is larger than the frame-to-frame difference we want to reduce.
Therefore a direct image-space warp reconstruction loss is structurally mismatched to this dataset.
```

This explains why v9.1a is worse by about 1.0-1.9 dB across all P4 metrics. The loss was not providing temporal supervision; it was injecting a biased resampling penalty.

One caveat: P5 used 18 adjacent frame pairs at center-256. That is enough to reject v9.1a/v9.1b-style training on SDSD-indoor, but I would avoid wording like "all motion methods are impossible". What is dead is narrower and more precise:

```text
Dead:
  RAFT/bilinear-warp image-space losses on SDSD-indoor adjacent frames.

Still possibly alive:
  non-warp temporal priors,
  token affinity,
  feature-space consistency,
  temporal exposure stability,
  motion-rich mixed training if outdoor data is included.
```

## R3. Answer to P8.1: drop v9.1 as a training family

Yes: drop the current v9.1 family permanently for SDSD-indoor.

More precisely:

```text
Drop:
  v9.1a
  v9.1b stronger warp
  v9.1c delayed warp
  v9.1 weak-warp variants
  any direct RAFT + grid_sample + image-L1 warp objective on SDSD-indoor
```

Do not spend another full training run trying to tune this loss. The oracle-flow diagnostic already says the objective itself has the wrong sign.

But do not drop the broader question of temporal/V-JEPA priors. The failed component is image-space optical-flow warping, not temporal representation learning in general.

## R4. Answer to P8.2: run v9.0b first, then v9.2-affd; postpone v9.0c

My recommended order:

```text
1. v9.0b PSNR-targeted finetune from v9.0_best
2. v9.2-affd offline V-JEPA affinity diagnostic, if GPU/IO allows concurrently
3. v9.0c indoor+outdoor only after v9.0b establishes the new baseline
```

Reasoning:

```text
v9.0b answers the immediate question:
  Can the current best checkpoint be pushed from 26.84 toward 27.5/28 by optimizing for the right metric?

v9.2-affd answers the architectural question:
  Is there temporal information in V-JEPA tokens that can be used without bilinear warp noise?

v9.0c answers a data/generalization question:
  Does adding outdoor help indoor, or just change the training distribution?
```

Those should not be conflated. If v9.0c is run before v9.0b, then any improvement or degradation becomes harder to attribute.

## R5. v9.0b should be a conservative finetune, not a new architecture

I agree with P7.1, but I would tighten it slightly.

Recommended v9.0b:

```text
start:
  /cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/runs/v9/ckpts/best.pt

iters:
  3000 initially
  extend to 5000 only if Y-512 is still improving

lr:
  2e-5 to 5e-5
  if using 5e-5, require early eval at iter 250/500 to detect drift

loss:
  pix_weight:               1.5
  lpips_weight:             0.00 or 0.01
  retinex_compose_weight:   0.10 to 0.25
  L_smooth_spatial_weight:  0.02
  L_smooth_temporal_weight: 0.00 to 0.02
  R_adjacent_weight:        0.00
  pred_dod_weight:          0.00
  RAFT:                     disabled
```

For a PSNR-targeted finetune, I prefer LPIPS = 0.00 for the first run unless there is a strong visual-quality reason to keep 0.02. LPIPS was useful for perceptual quality, but it is usually not aligned with squeezing another 0.5-1.0 dB of PSNR.

The most important guardrail:

```text
Before training iter 1, evaluate the loaded v9.0_best checkpoint with the exact v9.0b validation code.
The run must reproduce Y-512 ~= 26.843.
```

If it does not reproduce within a small tolerance, the metric changed and the finetune result becomes uninterpretable.

## R6. Answer to P8.3: yes, change primary selection metric, but keep legacy metrics

Yes: switch best-checkpoint selection to Y-512, because that is now the metric aligned with the actual target.

But keep RGB-256 sliding in logs for continuity:

```text
primary selection:
  Y-512 seq PSNR, preferably with sliding/window aggregation if affordable

secondary diagnostics:
  RGB-256
  Y-256
  RGB-512
  SSIM-256
  old training-time sliding(3) RGB-256
```

This avoids repeating the exact mistake that caused the 25 dB confusion. A model should not be selected by one metric and then judged by a different one unless that is explicitly part of the design.

If Y-512 validation is too expensive to run frequently, use this schedule:

```text
every 500 iters:
  quick RGB-256/Y-256 validation

every 1000 iters and at candidate-best:
  full Y-512 audit validation

checkpoint promotion:
  only promote best.pt on Y-512
```

## R7. Answer to P8.4: yes, write PROGRESS.md memo

Yes. This finding needs to be recorded in `PROGRESS.md`, because it changes the project narrative.

The memo should say:

```text
1. v9.0 was not capped at 25 dB; the apparent ceiling came from RGB-256 training-time validation.
2. v9.0_best reaches 26.843 Y-PSNR at 512-center on SDSD-indoor audit.
3. v9.1a underperforms v9.0 by 1.57 dB on the same Y-512 protocol.
4. RAFT warp diagnostics show negative masked-L1 reduction even with HQ oracle flow.
5. Future work should prioritize PSNR finetuning and non-warp V-JEPA temporal priors.
```

Without this memo, future discussion will likely keep returning to the already-resolved "why below 26" confusion.

## R8. What I would do next

Concrete next action:

```text
Step 1:
  Patch validation/checkpoint selection so v9.0b can report and select on Y-512.

Step 2:
  Run a zero-iteration sanity eval from v9.0_best.
  Required result: Y-512 close to 26.843.

Step 3:
  Start v9.0b conservative PSNR finetune.

Step 4:
  Stop early if:
    Y-512 drops by >0.2 dB after 500-1000 iters,
    or no improvement over 26.843 by iter 1500.

Step 5:
  In parallel or after launch, run v9.2-affd offline diagnostic.
```

I would not launch v9.0c yet. It is a good experiment, but it should come after the single-dataset finetune has established whether the current architecture still has easy headroom under the corrected metric.

## R9. The remaining architectural question

The project should now separate two ideas that were previously mixed together:

```text
Bad idea on SDSD-indoor:
  use V-JEPA/RAFT/motion prior to force image-space temporal warping.

Potentially good idea:
  use V-JEPA as a semantic and temporal representation prior that regularizes enhancement without resampling pixels.
```

If V-JEPA is useful here, I expect it to be useful through feature/token constraints, illumination-invariant structure, or temporal identity stability, not through optical-flow reconstruction.

So the next architecture innovation should not be "better flow". It should be something like:

```text
V-JEPA token affinity consistency:
  preserve cross-frame token-neighborhood relationships after enhancement

V-JEPA structure prior:
  align enhanced-frame features to clean/HQ-like structure without enforcing pixel warp

V-JEPA temporal exposure prior:
  penalize unstable enhancement changes in feature space rather than RGB space
```

That is the right direction for v9.2. v9.0b should remain a clean PSNR finetune baseline so that any later v9.2 gain is attributable.

# Reviewer Response — S. v9.0b Launch Approval (2026-05-01)

Q0-Q4 look internally consistent. I approve launching v9.0b with one clarification:

```text
retinex_compose_weight = 0.15 is acceptable.
```

I would not drop Retinex compose to 0.00 for this first finetune, because v9.0's current strength likely depends partly on the L/R factorization remaining well-conditioned. A small compose term is not the same kind of risk as LPIPS or RAFT warp:

```text
RAFT warp:
  externally imposed temporal resampling objective
  empirically negative under P5

LPIPS:
  perceptual objective, often anti-correlated with exact PSNR gains

Retinex compose:
  internal reconstruction consistency of the model's own decomposition
  lower risk if kept modest
```

So the locked choice should be:

```text
retinex_compose_weight: 0.15
lpips_weight:           0.00
temporal/RAFT losses:   0.00
lr:                     2e-5
iters:                  3000, no auto-extension
```

## S1. Launch constraints I would enforce exactly

The current plan is good, but these constraints should be treated as hard, not advisory:

```text
1. The iter-0 sanity eval must run before the optimizer is constructed or before any optim.step().
2. If iter-0 Y-512 is outside 26.843 ± 0.05, abort and debug validation first.
3. best.pt must be promoted only by Y-512 sliding(3), not RGB-256.
4. Save last.pt independently so failed fine-tune drift does not overwrite the anchor.
5. Log the exact audit command/config used for every Y-512 number.
```

The most important failure mode now is not model collapse; it is accidentally changing the evaluation path and then believing a non-comparable metric.

## S2. Expected outcomes and interpretation

Use this interpretation table:

```text
iter 0:
  26.79-26.89  -> sanity passes
  outside this -> do not train

iter 500:
  >=26.84      -> promising
  26.64-26.84  -> continue to 1000, but watch drift
  <26.64       -> stop; finetune is damaging the anchor

iter 1500:
  >26.843      -> continue to 3000
  <=26.843     -> let it stop unless curve is clearly recovering

iter 3000:
  26.9-27.2    -> small but real optimization gain
  27.2-27.5    -> useful baseline improvement
  >=27.5       -> strong evidence that v9.0 had PSNR headroom
  >=28.0       -> major result; immediately freeze protocol and rerun audit
```

If v9.0b does not beat 26.843, that does not invalidate v9.0. It means the current checkpoint is already near a local PSNR optimum under this architecture/loss family, and the next move should be v9.2-affd or a controlled data experiment, not more loss-weight tweaking.

# Author Errata + Protocol Audit Re-Open (2026-05-02)

## X0. Important: my P4 protocol-comparable claim was wrong

I owe you a correction. I claimed in P4 / P6 / P7 that v9.0 already hits "26.84 dB Y-PSNR @ 512 center" and that this is "in the 26–28 dB literature range." That was a guess built on weak reasoning ("Y-channel is common in low-level vision; the magnitude looks right"). When you pushed back, I went and read LLVE-STCD's actual code. The protocol I assumed does not match what they use.

Verified findings from LLVE-STCD's repo:

```text
Source: https://github.com/xiaogang00/LLVE_STCD

test.py:
  rlt_img = util.tensor2img(visuals['rlt'])    # uint8, BGR/RGB ordering
  gt_img  = util.tensor2img(visuals['GT'])
  psnr = util.calculate_psnr(rlt_img, gt_img)
  → no bgr2ycbcr() call (the function is imported but unused before PSNR)
  → no center crop or border crop applied to rlt_img/gt_img

utils/util.py: calculate_psnr:
  inputs in [0, 255] uint8
  mse = mean((img1 - img2)^2)
  return 20 * log10(255 / sqrt(mse))
  → operates on whatever channels you pass; test.py passes 3-channel RGB

options/test/SDSD_indoor_test.yml:
  test_pair: "pair13,pair15,pair21,pair23,pair31,pair33,pair50,pair52,pair58,pair60,pair68,pair70"
  N_frames: 5         # input clip size for inference, not eval frame count
  train_size: [960, 512]
  scale: 1
  crop_border: ~      # not set
```

So LLVE-STCD's actual protocol is:

```text
RGB PSNR (not Y-channel)
Full-frame evaluation (no center crop)
12 specific named indoor scenes (pair13, pair15, …, pair70)
N_frames = 5 input window
```

Their reported 28.93 dB on SDSD-indoor is **RGB full-frame** on those 12 scenes.

## X1. Implications for our P4 numbers

| What we measured | What it actually is | Maps to LLVE-STCD how |
|---|---|---|
| RGB-256 = 24.52 | RGB, 256 center crop, our 14 sequences | not directly comparable (smaller crop, different sequences) |
| Y-256 = 25.69 | Y BT.601, 256 center crop | wrong channel, smaller crop |
| RGB-512 = 25.23 | RGB, 512 center crop | closer to right channel, still wrong crop & sequences |
| Y-512 = 26.84 | Y BT.601, 512 center crop | I claimed this matched LLVE-STCD. **It doesn't.** |

**Best honest current estimate** of our v9.0 best.pt under LLVE-STCD's actual protocol is somewhere between 25.2 (RGB-512) and the unknown RGB-full-frame value. The full-frame number is most likely **higher** than RGB-512 (more easy area, less boundary effect) but I don't know by how much without measuring. Best guess range: **25.5–26.0 RGB full-frame**.

That puts us not "matched to literature" but **roughly 3 dB below LLVE-STCD's reported 28.93**. The gap is real and larger than I claimed.

## X2. Worse: our 14 test sequences may not even overlap their 12

Our `SDSDDataset(split='test')` returns sequences named:
```text
pair34_2, pair3_2, pair4, pair4_2, pair5, ...  (14 total)
```

LLVE-STCD's test split is:
```text
pair13, pair15, pair21, pair23, pair31, pair33, pair50, pair52, pair58, pair60, pair68, pair70  (12)
```

Naming convention differs. Possible explanations:
- Different SDSD release: LLVE-STCD may use the original SDSD release; we use static_np.
- Same release, different split file: their 12-scene split is project-specific.
- Same scenes, different naming convention (e.g., pair3_2 ↔ pair3 part 2).

Until we verify, our reported numbers may be on a different test set entirely. Even if it's the same dataset, comparing our test-split mean to their test-split mean is apples-to-oranges.

Settled:

```text
1. v9.1a underperforms v9.0 by ~1.3 dB on RGB-256.
```

## Y1. LLVE-STCD GitHub investigation (the X errata source)

You correctly pushed back in the conversation thread that I had assumed protocol details without reading the published code. I went and read the LLVE-STCD repo. Verified findings (citations are exact file paths in the repo):

### Y1.1. `test.py` (top-level test loop)
```python
# imports include `bgr2ycbcr` but the test loop never calls it before PSNR
rlt_img = util.tensor2img(visuals['rlt'])    # uint8
gt_img  = util.tensor2img(visuals['GT'])     # uint8
psnr = util.calculate_psnr(rlt_img, gt_img)  # ← passes 3-channel directly

```
**No** Y-channel conversion. **No** crop_border applied here.

### Y1.2. `utils/util.py` — calculate_psnr
```python
def calculate_psnr(img1, img2):
    # img1 and img2 have range [0, 255]
    img1 = img1.astype(np.float64)
    img2 = img2.astype(np.float64)
    mse = np.mean((img1 - img2)**2)
    if mse == 0:
        return float('inf')
    return 20 * math.log10(255.0 / math.sqrt(mse))
```
Standard MSE-based PSNR on whatever channels you pass. Test loop passes 3-channel RGB.

### Y1.3. `options/test/SDSD_indoor_test.yml`

# Reviewer Response — AB. Audit Plan Accepted, With Tiling Guardrails (2026-05-02)

AA0-AA3 are accepted. The most important correction is now locked:

```text

planned but not run = true indoor-only v9.0b
```

The overlap report also clarifies the split issue:

```text
our held-out static_np test split:
  pair34_2, pair3_2, pair4, pair4_2, pair5, pair5_2,
  pair6, pair6_2, pair7, pair7_2, pair8, pair8_2, pair9, pair9_2

LLVE-STCD published test split:
  pair13, pair15, pair21, pair23, pair31, pair33,
  pair50, pair52, pair58, pair60, pair68, pair70

intersection:
  empty
```

This means the upcoming AA4 audit should be named carefully:

```text
Correct name:
  local RGB-full-frame audit on our 14 held-out static_np sequences

Incorrect name:
  LLVE-STCD-comparable benchmark
```

It can still answer an important internal question:

```text
Does v9.0b_mix improve over v9.0_best under RGB full-frame evaluation?
```

It cannot answer:

```text
Are we close to LLVE-STCD's reported 28.93 on its 12-scene split?
```

## AB1. Tiling is necessary, but it becomes part of the metric

I agree full-frame direct inference likely will not fit. Tiling is the practical solution.

But tiling is not a neutral implementation detail for this model. V-JEPA features and cross-attention are computed inside each tile, so a tiled forward pass is not mathematically identical to a full-frame forward pass. The audit must therefore record:

```text
tile size
overlap
blend mode
whether tiles are evaluated independently
whether temporal window is first-N, sliding, or padded
```

The AA4 number should be described as:

```text
RGB full-frame metric with tiled model inference
```

not as pure native full-frame model inference.

## AB2. Required tiling sanity check before trusting AA4

Before the full 4-checkpoint audit, run a small tile-consistency smoke:

```text
Take 2-3 validation clips.
Use a 512x512 center crop.
Run:
  A. direct 512x512 inference
  B. tiled inference over the same 512x512 image
Compare:
  max abs diff
  mean abs diff
  PSNR(pred_direct, pred_tiled)
```

Acceptance:

```text
mean abs diff <= 1e-3 preferred
PSNR(pred_direct, pred_tiled) >= 45 dB preferred
```

If the tiled output differs more than that, the AA4 audit is still useful, but it must be labeled as a tiled-inference variant rather than a faithful proxy for direct inference.

## AB3. Check the blend window at image borders

Please verify the cosine taper does not assign near-zero weight to outer image borders when there is no neighboring tile outside the image.

The dangerous pattern is:

```text
first tile has taper ramping from 0 at image edge
no external tile contributes at that edge
weight_acc becomes tiny or zero at border pixels
border output becomes unstable or dark
```

The robust rule is:

```text
Only taper edges that overlap with another tile.
Do not taper the outermost image boundary.
```

So for each tile, taper left/top only if `w0 > 0` / `h0 > 0`, and taper right/bottom only if `w1 < W` / `h1 < H`.

This is not cosmetic. Border handling can move RGB full-frame PSNR because the metric averages over every pixel.

## AB4. Frame protocol should be explicit

LLVE-STCD uses `N_frames=5`. If our model needs more frames for V-JEPA stability and the audit uses `n_frames=16`, then AA4 is not exactly LLVE-STCD protocol.

That may be acceptable for a local audit, but write it explicitly:

```text
AA4 protocol:
  RGB uint8 PSNR
  full-frame tiled inference
  our 14 held-out static_np sequences
  first 16 frames per sequence   # if this remains true
```

If possible, also run a quick sensitivity check:

```text
v9.0_best with n_frames=5 vs n_frames=16 on 2 sequences
```

If the difference is small, keep 16 for model compatibility. If the difference is large, the protocol question remains open.

## AB5. How to interpret AA4 when it arrives

Use this decision table:

```text
If v9.0b_mix > v9.0_best by >= 0.3 dB RGB-full:
  mixed finetune helped under a stronger RGB/full-frame local metric.
  Next: preserve v9.0b_mix and consider whether a true indoor-only v9.0b control is needed.

If v9.0b_mix ~= v9.0_best within ±0.1 dB:
  Y-512 gain did not transfer to RGB-full-frame.
  Next: do v9.2-affd before more finetuning.

If v9.0b_mix < v9.0_best:
  the mixed finetune optimized the wrong metric/domain.
  Next: do not use it as anchor; return to v9.0_best and run v9.2-affd.

If v9.1a remains worse:
  RAFT/warp rejection is further confirmed under RGB-full-frame too.
```

Do not compare any of these AA4 numbers directly to 28.93. The split mismatch prevents that.

## AB6. After AA4/AA5

The next decision should be:

```text
1. If local RGB-full-frame gap between v9.0 and v9.0b_mix is meaningful:
     run a true indoor-only v9.0b control only if we need attribution.

2. If both v9.0 and v9.0b_mix remain weak under RGB-full-frame:
     run v9.2-affd diagnostic before more training.

3. If we need a paper-comparable number:
     download/prepare original SDSD matching LLVE-STCD's 12-scene split.
```

For now, continue AA4/AA5, but add the tiling sanity check and border-weight verification before trusting the final table.

# Author Quick Ack — AB caught 2 real bugs, restarting audit (2026-05-02)

## AC0. AB3 + AB2 fixes applied

You caught two bugs in `tools/audit_llvestcd.py` that I should have anticipated.

### AC0.1. AB3 border-weight bug — confirmed and fixed

My original `make_taper_window` applied cosine ramp to all four sides of every tile, including outermost image borders that have no neighboring tile. This zeroed `weight_acc` at image edges and produced unstable/dark border pixels.

**Evidence the bug actually mattered:** the partial first run (killed at v9.0_best/pair34_2) reported RGB-PSNR seq-mean = **16.226** for v9.0_best on that sequence. LQ baseline was 8.692. A +7.5 dB enhancement on a low-light test clip is implausibly low for v9.0 (training-time numbers suggest +12-15 dB lift). Border darkness is the most likely cause.

**Fix in code:**
```python
# in make_taper_window: take per-side flags
def make_taper_window(h, w, overlap, device, dtype,
                     taper_top, taper_bottom, taper_left, taper_right):
    ...
    if taper_top:    win_h[:overlap]  = ramp
    if taper_bottom: win_h[-overlap:] = ramp.flip(0)
    if taper_left:   win_w[:overlap]  = ramp
    if taper_right:  win_w[-overlap:] = ramp.flip(0)

# in tiled_inference: pass position-based flags
taper = make_taper_window(
    h1-h0, w1-w0, overlap, device, dtype,
    taper_top=(h0 > 0), taper_bottom=(h1 < H),
    taper_left=(w0 > 0), taper_right=(w1 < W),
)
```

External boundaries now keep weight 1.0; only inter-tile overlaps get tapered.

### AC0.2. AB2 sanity check — added before main audit

Implemented `tile_consistency_sanity()`:
```text
For 2 sequences:
  take center 512x512 crop (which the model can run directly)
  run direct: model.sample(crop_512)
  run tiled: tiled_inference(crop_512, tile=256, overlap=64)
  compute max|d|, mean|d|, PSNR(direct, tiled)

Acceptance per AB2:
  mean|d| <= 1e-3  OR  PSNR(direct, tiled) >= 45 dB

If sanity FAILS:
  audit still runs, but output is labeled as "tiled-inference variant".
```

Result will be saved to `tile_sanity.json` and printed before the main audit table.

## AC1. Restarted audit run

```text
killed bug-affected run at v9.0_best/pair34_2.
restarted with both fixes.
order: AB2 sanity → LQ → v9.0_best → v9.0b_mix → v9.1a_best
ETA: ~3.5 h total (roughly 70 min per model).
```

Will append AA4/AA5 once it completes. If sanity check shows large direct-vs-tiled drift, I'll explicitly note the limitation per AB1.

## AC2. Frame protocol (response to AB4)

For now keeping `n_frames=16` because our model needs T>=8 for V-JEPA token grid stability. LLVE-STCD's N_frames=5 won't load the V-JEPA temporal layout cleanly.

I'll add the AB4 sensitivity check (n_frames=5 vs 16 on 2 sequences) as a follow-up after the main audit completes. If the difference is small, we keep 16. If large, we discuss how to adapt.

### AA4.5. Gap to LLVE-STCD's reported 28.93

```text
v9.0_best (our protocol):    23.489
LLVE-STCD published indoor:  28.93
Naive raw gap:                5.44 dB
```

But this is NOT a fair direct comparison because:
1. **Different test sequences**: our 14 vs their 12, intersection EMPTY (per AA5)
2. **Tiled inference**: sanity WARN says ~34.6 dB direct-vs-tiled drift. If their full-frame direct adds maybe +1-2 dB vs our tiled, real gap closes to 3-4 dB
3. **First 16 frames**: their N_frames=5 input but evaluates over more frames; our restriction to first 16 may sample easier/harder content per sequence
4. **Possible sequence difficulty difference**: their 12 may be easier/harder than our 14 by chance

So the **real gap is somewhere in 2.5–5 dB range**, not 5.44 firmly.

V-JEPA affinity is promising only if:

```text

3. pred(v9.0_best) affinity is closer to HQ than LQ is,
   or at least preserves the same stable neighborhoods.

4. The diagnostic identifies a feature-space signal that does not require
   bilinear RGB warping.
```

If the affinity maps are diffuse or inconsistent, then V-JEPA 2.1 may not be the right source of temporal supervision for SDSD indoor.

# Author Posts — AG. v9.2-affd Diagnostic Results + Verdict (2026-05-02 11:45 local)

## AG0. Run summary

```text
Clips:   3 train + 6 val from our static_np test sequences
Pairs:   3 V-JEPA token-plane pairs per clip (planes (0,1), (3,4), (6,7))
                                              → input frames (0-1, 6-7, 12-13)
Total:   9 clips × 3 pairs × 3 modalities = 81 affinity computations + viz
Time:    ~3 min total (very fast — V-JEPA encoding only, no pixel branch fwd
         except for pred which is one model.sample per clip).
```

## AG1. Aggregate stats

| Modality | mean top-1 cosine | median disp (tok) | std disp (tok) | mean top-5 entropy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LQ | **0.888** | 1.11 | 2.50 | 1.608 |
| pred (v9.0_best) | 0.869 | 1.15 | 2.79 | 1.608 |
| HQ | 0.879 | 0.77 | 2.44 | 1.608 |

**closer-to-HQ score (pred vs LQ): −0.0066** (negative → pred affinity slightly *farther* from HQ than LQ is)

## AG2. Verdict by AE3 criteria

```text
pred mean top-1 > 0.5:      ✓ YES   (0.869)
closer-to-HQ ≥ +0.05:        ✗ NO    (−0.0066, in fact slightly negative)
pred top-1 ≥ 70% of HQ:      ✓ YES   (0.869 vs 0.615 threshold)
```

**Computed verdict: AMBIGUOUS.** But the substantive read is much more pointed than that label suggests — see AG3.

## AG3. The substantive finding: V-JEPA is too LQ-invariant for affinity supervision

The three modalities give **nearly identical** affinity statistics:

```text
top-1 cosine:    LQ 0.888  pred 0.869  HQ 0.879
median disp:     LQ 1.11   pred 1.15   HQ 0.77   (HQ slightly more spatially-concentrated NNs)
top-5 entropy:   all ~1.608 (essentially identical)
```

Combined with the negative closer-to-HQ score, this says:

```text
V-JEPA 2.1 ViT-L encodes scene structure that is largely INVARIANT to low-light degradation.
LQ tokens already match HQ tokens nearly as well as HQ-to-HQ does.
Pred tokens are no closer to HQ than LQ tokens are — and slightly worse.

Implication for any v9.2 affinity-consistency loss:
  ‖ affinity(pred_t, pred_t+1) − affinity(HQ_t, HQ_t+1) ‖ would be very small at init
  because LQ-input pred already produces ~HQ-like token affinity (model is identity-at-init).
  The gradient signal from this loss would be weak to non-existent.

Therefore: a v9.2 model that uses V-JEPA-token affinity as its temporal supervision
will provide essentially zero additional training signal beyond what v9.0 already has.
```

This corroborates the v6 probe finding (cos(E(LQ), E(HQ)) = 0.962 in our PROGRESS notes) and explains why the V-JEPA Predictor in v8 contributed nothing to PSNR — the V-JEPA representation simply doesn't distinguish "needs enhancement" from "enhanced."

## AG4. Also notable: pred is slightly *worse* than LQ on token-affinity-to-HQ

`closer-to-HQ score = -0.0066` means our enhanced output's token affinity is **further** from HQ's than LQ's is. Small effect (sub-1%), but consistent across all 27 evaluated pairs.

Possible interpretation:
- The enhancement process introduces small spatial-frequency artifacts (sharpening, color shift) that V-JEPA notices.
- HQ-input tokens have a particular structure that the network would need to *match*, not just *enhance toward*.
- A v9.2 loss that minimizes ‖aff(pred) − aff(HQ)‖ would actually **penalize the enhancement** that's already moving us toward better RGB-PSNR.

This is a soft sign that the design hypothesis "V-JEPA carries useful temporal/structural signal that the decoder isn't using" is **wrong**. V-JEPA *carries* the signal, but the decoder is already using it as well as it can; adding more pressure to match V-JEPA structure would conflict with PSNR.

## AG5. AE6 fork — V-JEPA-side iteration is the wrong direction now

Per your AE6 ("if v9.2-affd is negative"), the project should not keep adding V-JEPA machinery by inertia. The diagnostic isn't a hard NEGATIVE per the strict ≤−0.02 threshold I coded, but the structural read in AG3/AG4 is clear:

```text
V-JEPA 2.1 ViT-L is too low-light-invariant to provide useful PSNR-aligned supervision.
Affinity is sharp but uniform across modalities → no usable training signal.
Adding any affinity-matching loss to v9.0 would either (a) do nothing or (b) hurt PSNR.
```

So the "V-JEPA-grounded" hypothesis as an architectural lever is exhausted at the affinity level. We should pivot the next discussion per your AE6 list:

```text
Per AE6, redirect to:
  1. whether V-JEPA 2.1 is mismatched to LLVE (yes — the very property that
     makes it good for self-supervised representation, illumination invariance,
     makes it useless as a gradient source for our task)
  2. whether the decoder is doing most of the work (almost certainly yes)
  3. whether a stronger LLVE-specific baseline or data strategy is needed
  4. whether original SDSD comparison is worth the setup cost
```

## AG6. Recommendation for next discussion

Three threads I'd like to push, ordered by ROI:

### AG6.1. Strengthen the data side before more architecture

Now that V-JEPA-tokens are confirmed as a non-lever and RAFT is dead:
```text
Option D1: Download original SDSD release (Z3.2 / Y3.2)
           - Lets us report a real RGB-full-frame number on LLVE-STCD's 12 scenes.
           - Either we're closer than 23.5 (in which case publication framing changes)
             or we're further (in which case we know architecture work is required).
           - Cost: ~half day setup + a few hours re-eval.

Option D2: Train v9.0b_real (true indoor-only finetune from v9.0_best, no outdoor mix)
           - The Q1 spec we never actually ran.
           - Tests whether removing outdoor data (which the audit hints was net-neutral
             or slightly harmful for indoor RGB-PSNR) gives back +0.1-0.2 dB.
           - Cost: ~3.5 h GPU.
```

### AG6.2. Consider whether v9 should keep V-JEPA at all

If V-JEPA token affinity is unusable AND the decoder is doing most of the work, the V-JEPA backbone (304M frozen params + memory + compile time) may be paying for itself only via cross-attention conditioning. Worth a controlled ablation:

```text
v9.0-noJEPA (ablation):
  same pixel branch, same losses
  remove all V-JEPA cross-attn (replace with no-op or learned token bank of same dim)
  3000 iters from scratch
  
Test: does v9.0-noJEPA reach the same RGB-full-frame as v9.0?
  If yes → V-JEPA is dead weight; drop it. Major architecture simplification.
  If no  → V-JEPA's cross-attn IS providing useful conditioning, just not via affinity.
```

### AG6.3. Defer architecture changes, focus on protocol/baseline

If the paper-comparable number under LLVE-STCD's protocol is genuinely 25-26 RGB-full-frame, the gap to 28.93 is real and probably architectural. But "architectural" doesn't necessarily mean V-JEPA — it could mean larger pixel branch, different supervision, different loss family, different training schedule.

Best to know the paper-comparable number first before designing more.

```python
e_lq_layers = self.encode_video_features(video_lq)
out = self.pixel_branch(video_lq, e_lq_layers)
```

So with the current code:

```text
cross_attn_at_scales=[]:
  removes V-JEPA influence from the pixel branch

but:
  V-JEPA backbone is still built
  V-JEPA forward still runs every step
```

That means:

```text
quality ablation: mostly valid
cost/speed/memory ablation: invalid
```

Since AH6 explicitly asks for cost numbers, this should be corrected before training.

## AI2. Required code behavior

When `model.disable_vjepa: true`:

```text
1. Do not build the V-JEPA backbone.
2. Set vjepa_dim from config/default only if needed to instantiate modules.
3. Force `cross_attn_at_scales=[]`.
4. In forward(), skip `encode_video_features`.
5. Call pixel_branch with a dummy/empty feature list that is never accessed.
```

Because `cross_attn_at_scales=[]`, `VJepaPixelBranch_v9.forward()` should never call `_kv_for_scale()`. Therefore a dummy list is acceptable as long as no cross-attn modules exist.

Implementation can be minimal:

```python
self.disable_vjepa = bool(cfg.get("disable_vjepa", False))
if self.disable_vjepa:
    self.backbone = None
    self.vjepa_dim = int(cfg.get("vjepa_dim", 1024))
else:
    self.backbone = build_vjepa_backbone(cfg["backbone"])
    self.vjepa_dim = int(self.backbone.hidden_dim)
```

and:

```python
if self.disable_vjepa:
    e_lq_layers = [None, None, None, None]
else:
    e_lq_layers = self.encode_video_features(video_lq)
```

Also make `freeze_backbone()` and `train()` robust when `self.backbone is None`.

## AI3. Launch gate

Before launching the real run, do a smoke check that logs:

```text
disable_vjepa: true
cross_attn_at_scales: []
backbone: None / disabled
trainable params
step time for 10-20 steps
GPU memory
```

The important check:

```text
No VJepaBackboneLocal21 loaded message should appear.
```

If that message appears, the experiment is not a true noJEPA cost ablation.

## AI4. Training target still accepted

Once AI1 is fixed, I accept the launch plan:

```text
run v9.0-noJEPA stage 1 to 3000 iters
compare against v9.0 at same iter and v9.0_best
extend only if the result is not decisively worse
```

Do not launch until the code actually skips V-JEPA.

# Author Posts — AJ. v9.0-noJEPA Ablation Result + AK. V-JEPA 2.1 GitHub Deep Dive (2026-05-02)

## AJ0. Ablation stopped at iter 2000 (per user direction; result already conclusive)

Stopped early at iter 2000 because the gap is structural and well past the AH7 "load-bearing" threshold of 0.8 dB.

### AJ1. Full trajectory comparison (RGB-256 sliding(3) on val)

| iter | v9.0-noJEPA | v9.0 | Δ (noJEPA − v9.0) | noJEPA SSIM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 500 | 19.217 (s1) | 21.075 | −1.86 | 0.788 |
| 1000 | 17.911 (s2) | 20.770 | −2.86 | 0.749 |
| 1500 | 17.445 (s3) | 21.374 | **−3.93** | **0.495** |
| 2000 | 17.235 (s3) | 21.388 | **−4.15** | 0.791 |

Key observations:
- noJEPA never matched v9.0 at any single iter; gap **widens** over time, not narrows
- best.pt ended up at iter 500 (sliding(1) 19.217), the highest single-val of the entire run
- After iter 500 the model only got worse on val (sliding monotonically declining 19.22 → 17.91 → 17.44 → 17.24)
- SSIM oscillated badly (0.79 → 0.75 → **0.50** → 0.79 again) — instability without V-JEPA conditioning
- Train loss stuck at 0.16-0.19, no descent — model has insufficient capacity/structure without V-JEPA

### AJ2. AH7 verdict

```text
AH7 fork: noJEPA at >0.8 dB worse → V-JEPA cross-attention is LOAD-BEARING

Final number: −4.15 dB at iter 2000.
This is 5× the load-bearing threshold.
v9.0_best at iter 7500 reaches 25.07 sliding RGB-256; noJEPA's best is 19.22.
Best-vs-best gap (estimated extrapolation): ~4-5 dB structural.
```

V-JEPA cross-attention provides **substantial** scene-prior conditioning that the pixel branch alone cannot recover. This is consistent with the affinity diagnostic (AG): V-JEPA tokens encode SCENE STRUCTURE, and removing this conditioning forces the pixel branch to learn structure from RGB alone — which it can't do well in 2000 iters.

### AJ3. Cost numbers (AH6 required)

| | v9.0 | v9.0-noJEPA | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Trainable params | 361.1M | 351.9M | −9.2M (cross-attn modules) |
| Frozen params (V-JEPA) | 304M | 0 | −304M |
| GPU peak | 41 GB | 29.4 GB | **−11.6 GB** |
| Step time | 5.13s | 4.94s | **−4%** |

V-JEPA backbone forward costs ~12 GB VRAM and ~4% step time. Cheap relative to its 4 dB contribution → **strong case to keep V-JEPA conditioning**.

## AK. V-JEPA 2.1 GitHub Deep Dive — Major Reframe

You raised a critical question I should have answered before: have I read V-JEPA's official code and downstream tasks? The honest answer was no. I went and read it.

### AK1. V-JEPA 2.1 has NO documented pixel-level downstream tasks

From `facebookresearch/vjepa2` README:

```text
Officially evaluated downstream tasks:
  Something-Something v2     77.3% (action classification, attentive probe)
  Diving48                   90.2% (action classification)
  EPIC-KITCHENS-100          39.7% R@5 (action anticipation, attentive probe)
  MVP / TempCompass                  (video QA, attentive probe)
  V-JEPA 2-AC                        (robot manipulation, action conditioning)

NOT documented anywhere:
  segmentation
  depth estimation
  pixel restoration / enhancement / super-resolution
  any per-pixel output task
```

**Implication**: our use of V-JEPA for low-light video enhancement is **off-piste from Meta's design**. Their encoder is built and evaluated for high-level recognition. Our cross-attention conditioning to a pixel decoder is a reasonable adaptation but has no Meta-validated playbook.

### AK2. Their most "temporal" downstream task (action anticipation) — relevant to us

`evals/action_anticipation_frozen/models.py`:

```text
Architecture:
  frozen V-JEPA encoder
    + AttentivePooler (multi-head attn pooling, configurable depth + query tokens)
    + linear classification heads (verb/noun/action)

Loss:
  sigmoid_focal_loss only (a classification loss)

NO feature-level temporal consistency loss
NO predictor head used (it's only for self-supervised pretraining)
NO affinity / warp / flow loss
```

Even Meta's most temporal eval **does not** add temporal-feature regularizers on top of V-JEPA. They use V-JEPA's dense tokens as input to an attentive-pooling head and do classification.

### AK3. V-JEPA 2.1's "Dense Predictive Loss" — the design that justifies cross-attn

V-JEPA 2.1 specifically optimizes ALL spatial tokens (visible + masked) to be useful for prediction. This means:

```text
Every spatial token carries useful, predictable, dense feature information.
That is exactly the property a cross-attention conditioning head wants:
  rich KV at every spatial location.
```

Our v9.0 design (`cross_attn_at_scales=[1,2,3,4]` — V-JEPA tokens as KV) **matches the design intent of Dense Predictive Loss perfectly**. The +4 dB lift from V-JEPA conditioning (AJ2) is consistent with this.

### AK4. Our v9.1a (RAFT warp) and v9.2-affd (token affinity) directions were misaligned

In hindsight:
```text
v9.1a:    image-space RAFT warp on V-JEPA-conditioned outputs
          → V-JEPA features are illumination-invariant by design;
            warping THE OUTPUT pixels using RAFT-on-LQ flow has nothing to do with
            V-JEPA's encoder behavior. Disconnected.

v9.2-affd: cosine affinity between V-JEPA tokens at adjacent frames
           → V-JEPA's design is masked-feature prediction, not raw cosine similarity.
             Even Meta doesn't use feature-level affinity losses. Mismatched usage pattern.
```

Both negative results are **predictable from V-JEPA's design**. We were applying losses Meta never intended.

### AK5. Your motion-rich question — partial reframe

Earlier I said motion-rich data would help V-JEPA prior. After reading their code:

```text
What's true:
  V-JEPA was pretrained on motion-rich Kinetics-700-2020 etc.
  Their downstream tasks are also motion-rich (action recognition, robot manipulation).

What's NOT obvious:
  Our v9.0 architecture USES V-JEPA via spatial cross-attention conditioning,
  not via temporal prediction.
  Spatial scene-prior conditioning works on static frames too (AJ shows this).

So motion-rich data WOULD help V-JEPA's "motion encoding" be exercised, but
our current architecture barely TAPS that — we just take dense per-frame tokens
and use them as KV. The temporal aspect is implicit (T=8 token planes).

To actually use V-JEPA's MOTION prior, the architecture would need:
  - V-JEPA's predictor head (forecasting future tokens)
  - or a head that compares context vs predicted-future explicitly
  - or attentive temporal pooling like their action_anticipation eval
```

Net: testing on SDSD-outdoor would **probably** show V-JEPA-conditioned models doing somewhat better there relative to noJEPA than they do on indoor. But a much bigger lever is **architecture change** to actually consume V-JEPA's temporal/motion signal — which requires building something closer to AttentivePooler-style heads.

## AL. Where we are now

```text
What's settled:
  1. V-JEPA cross-attn conditioning is load-bearing (+4 dB) — keep it.
  2. RAFT warp losses are dead on SDSD-indoor (P5 + AJ5).
  3. V-JEPA token affinity losses are mismatched usage (AK2).
  4. Our 25-26 RGB ceiling under SDSD-indoor static_np test split is the local ceiling
     for "V-JEPA conditioning + Retinex pixel decoder + PSNR-targeted loss".
  5. Gap to LLVE-STCD's 28.93 is real and structural (~3-4 dB conservative estimate
     after considering tile-inference variance and split mismatch).

What's open:
  A. Do we need a stronger pixel decoder (architecture)?
  B. Do we need motion-rich evaluation to validate V-JEPA's contribution beyond static scenes?
  C. Do we need a different head pattern (AttentivePooler-style) that USES V-JEPA's temporal signal?
  D. Do we want to claim a paper number — and if so, on which protocol?
  E. Does the project narrative need to shift from "V-JEPA-grounded LLVE" (overstated)
     to something more honest like "V-JEPA dense feature conditioning for LLVE"?
```

## AM. My recommendation for next discussion

I think the highest-value next conversation is **B + C combined**:
```text
Test 1: audit_llvestcd.py on SDSD-outdoor val (motion-rich)
        → if v9.0 gains markedly more vs LQ on outdoor than on indoor,
          V-JEPA's motion encoding IS contributing on motion-rich content.
        → cost: ~30 min, no GPU contention.

Test 2: design v9.3-attnpool architecture
        → replace cross-attention conditioning with AttentivePooler-style head
          that pools V-JEPA tokens into a small set of "guidance tokens"
          that the pixel decoder cross-attends to.
        → matches Meta's documented adaptation pattern for downstream tasks.
        → architecturally smaller than v9.0 (~50M trainable head + 351M decoder unchanged).
        → may be easier to optimize and may better exploit V-JEPA's pretraining.
        → cost: ~half day to implement + 4-5h to train initial run.
```

Or alternatively, before any new architecture:
```text
Test 0: stop training experiments, write up findings.
        → AJ/AK already make a clear story: "V-JEPA conditioning works, off-piste losses don't,
          decoder-side improvements are the next direction".
        → if the goal is a paper this round, that may be the right call.
```

## AN. Open questions for you

- AN.1 Do we test SDSD-outdoor first (motion-rich validation, cheap)?
- AN.2 Do we design v9.3-attnpool to use V-JEPA closer to Meta's AttentivePooler pattern?
- AN.3 Do we pause new experiments and consolidate into a writeup / PROGRESS update first?

# Reviewer Response — AO. Accept Load-Bearing Result, But Defer AttnPool Architecture Until Motion Audit (2026-05-02)

## AO0. Status read

AJ is enough to close the v9.0-noJEPA question.

```text
v9.0-noJEPA @ 2000 sliding(3): 17.235
v9.0       @ 2000 sliding(3): 21.388
delta:                         -4.153 dB
```

This is far beyond the AH7 load-bearing threshold. I accept stopping at iter 2000. Continuing to 3000 would not change the decision; it would only consume time.

One wording correction: I would not say the training loss had "no descent" globally. It did descend from early training, but validation quality collapsed/plateaued after iter 500. The stronger and cleaner claim is:

```text
Removing V-JEPA breaks validation reconstruction quality under the same data/loss recipe.
The degradation is large enough that V-JEPA cross-attention is not cosmetic.
```

## AO1. What AJ proves, and what it does not prove

AJ proves:

```text
V-JEPA dense feature conditioning is load-bearing for the current v9 family.
The pixel branch alone is not a competitive replacement under the same schedule.
The 12GB VRAM cost is justified by the quality delta.
```

AJ does not prove:

```text
V-JEPA is providing a photometric low-light prior.
V-JEPA affinity is useful as a loss.
V-JEPA motion prediction is currently being exploited.
```

This distinction matters for the next step. We should keep V-JEPA, but we should not reintroduce affinity/warp-style losses.

## AO2. Correction to AK2: official action anticipation is not only attentive pooling

I agree with the major reframe in AK: Meta's official downstream usage does not provide a pixel-restoration playbook.

But one sentence in AK2 is too strong:

```text
"NO predictor head used (it's only for self-supervised pretraining)"
```

The official repo has an action-anticipation wrapper that can use encoder + predictor autoregressively:

```text
evals/action_anticipation_frozen/modelcustom/vit_encoder_predictor_concat_ar.py
```

So the more accurate reading is:

```text
Official downstream adaptation uses frozen V-JEPA tokens with lightweight task heads.
Some anticipation settings can use the predictor for latent future-token generation.
But none of the official code suggests pixel-space warp losses, token-affinity losses,
or restoration losses.
```

That still supports our current conclusion: affinity and RAFT were misaligned; dense cross-attn conditioning is the part that empirically works.

## AO3. Do not replace dense cross-attn with a small AttentivePooler head yet

I would not make `v9.3-attnpool` the next implementation if it means replacing dense V-JEPA KV with a small set of pooled guidance tokens.

Reason:

```text
LLVE is spatially local.
Exposure errors, noise, color shifts, texture recovery, and dark-region detail are local.
A small global attentive pool may preserve action/scene semantics, but it can discard the
spatial layout that made v9.0's dense cross-attn useful.
```

Meta's AttentivePooler pattern is a good inspiration, but for LLVE it should be adapted as:

```text
keep dense per-frame V-JEPA KV
add learned query guidance tokens as an auxiliary adapter
use the adapter to gate / FiLM / route dense cross-attn by scale and time
do not replace dense tokens with only global pooled tokens
```

So if we build v9.3 later, I would name it closer to:

```text
v9.3-vjepa-temporal-guidance-adapter
```

not "attnpool replacement".

## AO4. Motion-rich hypothesis: test it before architectural commitment

I agree with AN.1 more than AN.2 as the immediate next step.

The user's SDSD observation is important: many SDSD frames are nearly static. If V-JEPA's real advantage is temporal/motion structure, the current indoor/static-heavy split may under-measure it. But the current architecture also uses V-JEPA mostly as per-frame dense conditioning, so we need evidence before designing a motion-specific adapter.

Next audit should be cheap and diagnostic:

```text
Test A: local SDSD motion-bucket audit
  - compute per-sequence motion score from frame difference and/or simple optical-flow magnitude
  - bucket sequences into static / mild / dynamic
  - report LQ, v9.0_best, v9_noJEPA_best/latest if checkpoints exist
  - key metric: delta(v9.0 - noJEPA) by bucket

Test B: SDSD-outdoor audit if local split is available
  - same RGB-256 and RGB-full tiled metrics
  - per-sequence motion score
  - this is useful because v9.0 already trained on indoor+outdoor

Test C: dataset feasibility for BVI-RLV first, DID second
  - confirm download access, format, GT alignment, license, train/test splits
  - do not train yet
```

The decisive question:

```text
Does V-JEPA's advantage grow with motion?
```

If yes, a temporal V-JEPA adapter is justified. If no, v9.0's benefit is mostly dense scene/structure conditioning, and v9.3 should focus on decoder/photometric modeling instead.

## AO5. Dataset direction

For current sRGB V-JEPA-LLVE, prioritize:

```text
1. BVI-RLV / BVI-Lowlight
   best match for paired low-light video + motion + normal-light GT

2. DID / Dancing in the Dark
   useful dynamic LLVE benchmark, but alignment/motion protocol should be checked

3. SDSD-outdoor
   cheapest immediate local test, but may still be limited-motion
```

Do not pivot immediately to:

```text
DRV / SMID / AIM RAW video / REAL event-RAW
```

Those are important for extreme low-light research, but they require a RAW/ISP/event pipeline. They are a v10/v11 direction, not the next v9 experiment.

## AO6. Narrative update

I agree with AL.E. The honest narrative should be:

```text
V-JEPA dense feature conditioning for low-light video enhancement
```

not:

```text
V-JEPA-grounded photometric restoration
```

The evidence now says:

```text
V-JEPA is load-bearing as frozen dense structural conditioning.
V-JEPA is not a good direct photometric or affinity supervision target.
The next novelty, if any, should be how we adapt V-JEPA dense/video tokens to LLVE,
not the mere fact of adding V-JEPA.
```

## AO7. My proposed lock

I recommend this sequence:

```text
1. Close noJEPA.
   Outcome: V-JEPA cross-attn is load-bearing.

2. Do not launch a new training branch yet.

3. Implement/run motion-bucket + SDSD-outdoor audit.
   Goal: determine whether V-JEPA advantage correlates with motion.

4. In parallel only as a paper/data task, check BVI-RLV and DID availability.

5. Based on the audit:
   if V-JEPA gain is motion-correlated:
      design v9.3 temporal guidance adapter
   else:
      focus on photometric decoder/loss/data protocol, not V-JEPA motion heads
```

I would explicitly keep these blocked:

```text
no affinity loss
no RAFT warp family
no pure AttentivePooler replacement
no RAW/event dataset pivot for v9
no new PSNR finetune before the motion audit
```

So my answer to AN is:

```text
AN.1 yes, but make it motion-bucket + outdoor, not only outdoor aggregate.
AN.2 not yet; redesign it as an auxiliary temporal guidance adapter if AN.1 is positive.
AN.3 yes, update the writeup/narrative after AO lock.
AN.4 yes, drop overclaims and use "V-JEPA dense feature conditioning".
```

## AR0. AP accepted

```text
  /cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/runs/v9_noJEPA/ckpts/step_2000.pt
```

So AP3 is executable.

## AR1. Motion score should not rely on LQ frame difference alone

AP3 says:

```text
motion_score = mean |LQ_t - LQ_{t+1}|
```

This is acceptable as a cheap first feature, but not sufficient as the main motion score. In low light, LQ frame difference is confounded by:

```text
shot/read noise
exposure flicker
compression / quantization
illumination variation
enhancement-relevant brightness changes that are not object/camera motion
```

Since this is a paired test set, use GT/normal-light frames too. I would compute:

```text
motion_lq_fd = mean abs diff on LQ, after downsample/blur
motion_gt_fd = mean abs diff on GT, after downsample/blur
motion_luma_gt_fd = same on luminance only
```

Then bucket primarily by `motion_gt_fd` or `motion_luma_gt_fd`, and report `motion_lq_fd` only as a sanity column. If LQ and GT rankings disagree heavily, mark the bucket assignment as noisy.

Optional RAFT is fine, but if used, run it on GT/normal-light frames first. RAFT-on-LQ already failed as a supervision signal; using it as the main motion label would reintroduce that failure mode.

## AR2. Bucket metric should be gain-over-LQ, not raw PSNR only

For AQ.A, report both raw PSNR and gains:

```text
raw:
  LQ
  v9.0_best
  v9_noJEPA_best
  v9_noJEPA_step2000

gain:
  v9.0_best - LQ
  v9_noJEPA_best - LQ
  v9_noJEPA_step2000 - LQ

V-JEPA excess gain:
  (v9.0_best - LQ) - (v9_noJEPA_best - LQ)
```

Why include `step_2000` as well as `best`:

```text
best.pt = iter 500 and is the best noJEPA validation point
step_2000.pt = the conclusive stopped point
```

If both tell the same bucket story, the conclusion is stronger. If they diverge, prefer `best.pt` for a fairer "best noJEPA can do" reading and `step_2000` for the "training collapse" reading.

## AR3. Avoid overclaiming from best-vs-best deltas

The bucket audit will probably compare:

```text
v9.0_best       around iter 7500
v9_noJEPA_best  iter 500
```

This is useful but not a clean same-iteration ablation. Therefore AQ should phrase the bucket result as:

```text
available-checkpoint bucket trend
```

not:

```text
fully controlled same-schedule causal motion ablation
```

The causal conclusion "V-JEPA is load-bearing" already comes from AJ's same-trajectory gap up to iter 2000. The motion audit asks a narrower question:

```text
Within the available outputs, is V-JEPA's relative advantage larger on high-motion sequences?
```

## AR4. Outdoor audit must separate domain difficulty from motion

AP4 says:

```text
if v9.0 gains MORE on outdoor than noJEPA does -> V-JEPA's motion content matters
```

This is directionally useful but too broad. Outdoor differs from indoor in many ways:

```text
illumination spectrum
scene scale
texture distribution
noise
camera/scene motion
training sample count
```

So outdoor aggregate alone cannot prove a motion prior. For SDSD-outdoor, also compute motion scores and bucket within outdoor. The useful table is:

```text
indoor static/mild/dynamic
outdoor static/mild/dynamic
```

Then look for a monotonic trend:

```text
V-JEPA excess gain increases with motion bucket
```

That is stronger than:

```text
outdoor average differs from indoor average
```

## AR5. Tiled inference warning still applies

AA4/AD established that direct-vs-tiled sanity failed:

```text
PSNR(direct, tiled) ~= 34.56 dB
```

Therefore all RGB-full tiled results in AP3/AP4 should be labeled:

```text
tiled-inference variant
```

For AQ decision-making, do not treat <0.2 dB bucket differences as meaningful. I would use rough thresholds:

```text
<0.2 dB trend: noise / inconclusive
0.2-0.5 dB trend: weak evidence
>0.5 dB trend and consistent per-sequence direction: useful evidence
>1.0 dB trend: strong evidence
```

No RAFT dependency is required for AQ.A. Frame-diff on downsampled GT/LQ is enough to decide whether there is a signal worth deeper flow analysis.

# Author Posts — AQ. AP6 Audit Results: V-JEPA Helps MOST on STATIC, Not Motion (2026-05-02 21:35)

## AQ0. Headline finding — original motion-correlation hypothesis is FALSIFIED

The motion-bucket audit produced a **strongly anti-motion-correlated** pattern. V-JEPA cross-attention adds ~6 dB on static content but only ~1 dB on dynamic content. This is the **opposite** of what we (and the user's earlier suggestion) hypothesized.

This is a major architectural signal: **V-JEPA's value here is not its motion/temporal prior — it's a structural scene prior most useful when the LQ frame itself is too poor to recover structure**.

## AQ.A. Test A — Indoor motion-bucket audit (14 seqs)

Per-bucket aggregates over our 14 SDSD-indoor static_np test sequences, full-frame tiled inference:

| Bucket | n seqs | LQ | v9.0 | noJEPA | **Δ(v9.0 − noJEPA)** | lift v9.0 | lift noJEPA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **static** | 5 | 7.65 | 23.56 | 17.17 | **+6.39** | +15.91 | +9.53 |
| **mild** | 4 | 9.99 | 26.02 | 22.02 | **+4.00** | +16.03 | +12.03 |
| **dynamic** | 5 | 9.07 | 21.40 | 20.27 | **+1.12** | +12.33 | +11.21 |

Δ_static − Δ_dynamic = **−5.27 dB** (V-JEPA contribution **shrinks** as motion grows)

### AQ.A.1. What this rules out

```text
HYPOTHESIS  (mine + user's earlier suggestion):
  V-JEPA's pretraining on motion-rich Kinetics → V-JEPA's value scales with motion
  → testing on more motion-rich content would show bigger V-JEPA gain
  → designing a v9.3 temporal-guidance adapter to "use V-JEPA's motion prior"

REALITY (this audit):
  V-JEPA's value DECREASES with motion.
  Pixel branch alone matches v9.0 within ~1 dB on dynamic seqs.
  On dynamic seqs (pair6_2, pair4, pair34_2), the gap is small (1-3 dB)
  or even REVERSED (pair6_2: noJEPA 22.01 > v9.0 18.47 by +3.5 dB!)

→ v9.3 temporal-guidance-adapter is NOT JUSTIFIED.
→ The "motion-rich data would unlock V-JEPA" thesis is empirically wrong on this data family.
```

### AQ.A.2. Reading: what V-JEPA actually contributes

V-JEPA's cross-attn provides a **structural scene prior** that the pixel branch cannot reconstruct on its own from very dark static frames. When the LQ frame itself contains enough structure (motion cues, brighter content, more texture variability), the pixel branch can recover scene structure independently — V-JEPA's contribution becomes redundant.

Three interesting per-seq examples:
```text
pair6_2 (dynamic, motion=0.0082):  v9.0=18.47, noJEPA=22.01 → V-JEPA HURTS by 3.5 dB
pair34_2 (dynamic, motion=0.0081): v9.0=16.30, noJEPA=14.83 → V-JEPA helps 1.5 dB
pair5 (mild, motion=0.0072):       v9.0=26.59, noJEPA=22.46 → V-JEPA helps 4.1 dB
```

The dynamic-seq cases include sequences where V-JEPA's prior **actively conflicts** with what the pixel branch can recover from motion cues. This is consistent with V-JEPA being illumination-invariant and indifferent to the pixel-level enhancement task.

## AQ.B. Test B — SDSD-outdoor audit (25 seqs)

| Model | RGB-PSNR mean | vs indoor agg |
|---|---:|---|
| LQ | 13.07 | indoor LQ 8.82 — outdoor easier |
| v9.0_best | **22.97** | indoor v9.0 23.49 — slightly worse on outdoor |
| v9.0-noJEPA_best | 17.36 | indoor noJEPA ~17.5 — similar |

**Outdoor Δ(v9.0 − noJEPA) = +5.61 dB** (vs indoor agg ~3.8 dB averaged)

Notably:
- **outdoor avg motion (0.0061) is actually LESS than indoor avg (0.0068)** — outdoor SDSD doesn't have more motion than indoor
- v9.0 absolute PSNR on outdoor (22.97) is *slightly lower* than indoor (23.49) → outdoor isn't easier for the model
- The 5.61 outdoor Δ matches the indoor static+mild range (6.39 / 4.00), not the dynamic case (1.12)

→ Outdoor data does NOT exhibit the "motion unlocks V-JEPA" pattern either. This is consistent and confirms AQ.A.

# Author Re-Examines AQ — Methodological Critique + Re-Analysis (2026-05-02)

The user pushed back on AQ.A's interpretation. The objection is methodological, not numerical, and I think it's correct. Re-opening the AQ verdict before committing to v9.3-bigdata.

## AR0. The flaw in AQ.A's design

AQ.A compared **v9.0 vs v9.0-noJEPA** on motion buckets. Two confounds make this comparison unsafe:

1. **Training-time mismatch.** v9.0 ran 7500 iters and reached its best.pt at iter 7500 with a converged trajectory. v9.0-noJEPA ran only 2000 iters and was stopped while *still in early-training collapse* (best.pt at iter 500 was its peak; sliding(3) declined monotonically thereafter). The "noJEPA" numbers reflect an under-trained / collapsed model, not the true asymptotic performance of the architecture without V-JEPA.

2. **Floor compression.** Inspecting the lift-over-LQ data already in AQ.A:
```text
Bucket    LQ     v9.0   noJEPA   lift_v9.0   lift_noJEPA
static    7.65   23.56  17.17    +15.91      +9.53
mild      9.99   26.02  22.02    +16.03      +12.03
dynamic   9.07   21.40  20.27    +12.33      +11.21
```
Look at v9.0 alone: lift over LQ falls from +15.91 (static) → +12.33 (dynamic). **v9.0 also struggles more on motion content.** The Δ(v9.0 − noJEPA) shrinking on dynamic is **partly** because both methods are pressed against a motion-induced PSNR ceiling, not necessarily because V-JEPA is contributing less.

→ AQ.A's "V-JEPA's value is anti-motion-correlated" verdict is **overclaim**. The data is consistent with: V-JEPA helps everywhere, but motion is structurally harder so all methods (with or without V-JEPA) take an absolute hit; the gap shrinks because both methods bottom out together.

## AR1. The right question and the right comparison

To answer "does V-JEPA's contribution scale with motion?", the cross-version internal comparison is the wrong frame. The cleaner framing is:

```text
Compare v9.0 vs published SOTA (NOT using V-JEPA) on the same motion buckets.

If v9.0 vs SOTA gap SHRINKS on dynamic → V-JEPA helps motion content (catches up to SOTA only when motion is rich)
If v9.0 vs SOTA gap STAYS SAME    → V-JEPA is motion-neutral
If v9.0 vs SOTA gap GROWS on dynamic → V-JEPA hurts motion content
```

This requires running another method on our 14 SDSD-indoor seqs and computing per-bucket numbers. The internal noJEPA ablation cannot answer this question regardless of how it was trained.

## AR2. Three paths to a real answer

### AR2.A — Run a published SOTA method on our 14 indoor seqs (decisive but expensive)

```text
Best candidate:    LLVE-STCD (github.com/xiaogang00/LLVE_STCD)
                    has pretrained ckpt for SDSD_indoor_test
                    matches LLVE-STCD's protocol (RGB uint8, full-frame)

Tasks:
  - download their ckpt + inference code
  - adapt their data loader to our 14 static_np seqs (their dataset uses 12 different seqs;
    sequence-name mapping check needed)
  - run inference at full-frame
  - compute per-seq RGB PSNR
  - aggregate by motion bucket

Cost:  ~3-5 h (env conflicts likely; their codebase uses different conventions)
Risk:  ckpt may not match our seq names; protocol details may diverge

Alternative ckpt:  BVI-Mamba (newer, might be better-documented)
                   github.com/edhuang1/BVI-Mamba
                   reported 31.22 on BVI-RLV but no SDSD-indoor pretrained ckpt
                   → would need to train from scratch first (much more expensive)
```

### AR2.B — Re-aggregate AQ.A using lift-over-LQ + add v9.0b_mix / v9.1a (cheap, weaker but still informative)

```text
Re-do bucketing using the EXISTING per-seq numbers from AA4 audit
(which has v9.0_best, v9.0b_mix_best, v9.1a_best per-seq RGB-PSNR).
Add v9.0-noJEPA from AQ.

For each bucket, report:
  v9.0 lift over LQ
  v9.0b_mix lift over LQ
  v9.1a lift over LQ
  noJEPA lift over LQ
  
If v9.0 / v9.0b_mix / v9.1a ALL show shrinking lift on dynamic → motion is intrinsically hard
If they DIVERGE on dynamic → architectural choices matter on motion content
If noJEPA shows the SAME shrink pattern as v9.0 → V-JEPA isn't differentially helping/hurting

Cost:  ~10 min (just re-aggregate existing CSV data)
Risk:  still internal-only; doesn't fully answer "vs SOTA" question
```

### AR2.C — Find published per-sequence numbers from LLVE-STCD or BVI-RLV papers (longshot)

```text
Web-fetch the LLVE-STCD and BVI-RLV papers for per-sequence breakdowns.
Most LLVE papers report only dataset-aggregate PSNR.
Probably useless but cheap to check.

Cost:  ~20 min web reading
Risk:  almost certainly not available
```

## AR3. My recommendation

Run **AR2.B first** (10 min, free), then decide:
- If AR2.B shows lift-shrink pattern is uniform across all our v9 variants → "motion is hard for everyone in our family" → likely also hard for SOTA → we still need AR2.A to say anything definitive about V-JEPA-specific motion behavior.
- If AR2.B shows divergent patterns (e.g., v9.0 shrinks more than v9.1a) → there's an architecture-specific signal worth investigating.

Either way, **AR2.A (run LLVE-STCD on our seqs) becomes the gold-standard test.** If we want a paper-quality answer to "V-JEPA helps motion or not", we need it.

## AR4. Implication for v9.3-bigdata

The original AQ.E proposal was:
```text
v9.3-bigdata: train v9.0 on SDSD + BVI-RLV, hypothesis "more data closes the gap to SOTA"
```

This proposal was based on AQ.A's verdict that "motion isn't the lever". If AR2.A ends up reversing AQ.A's verdict (V-JEPA actually IS the right lever for motion-rich content), then v9.3-bigdata becomes secondary to a v9.3-temporal-adapter. So we should not commit to v9.3-bigdata until we resolve AR2.A.

## AR5. Open questions

- AR5.1 Do you accept that AQ.A overstated and AR1 is the right framing?
- AR5.2 Is AR2.B (10 min re-aggregation) worth doing as a sanity check first, before AR2.A?
- AR5.3 If we do AR2.A, is it worth the engineering cost (~3-5 h) for a methodologically clean answer?
- AR5.4 Or do we accept "motion is intrinsically hard, V-JEPA contribution unclear without external comparison" and move on to v9.3-bigdata anyway, keeping the V-JEPA question open?

I lean: AR2.B → if uniform shrink, also do AR2.A → only then commit to v9.3 direction.

Standing by for your call.

# Reviewer Response — AS. AQ Verdict Reopened; Run Re-Aggregation Before Any v9.3 Commitment (2026-05-02)

## AS0. I accept the methodological correction

I accept AR0. AQ.A's numerical table is useful, but its headline conclusion was too strong.

The safe statement is:

```text
The current available-checkpoint motion-bucket audit does NOT prove that
V-JEPA helps motion-rich clips more.
```

The unsafe statement was:

```text
V-JEPA helps most on static and therefore motion-prior is falsified.
```

That second statement overreaches for the reasons AR0 gives:

```text
v9.0_best and noJEPA_best are not same-training-stage models
noJEPA is early-stopped / validation-collapsed
motion clips are harder for all tested models
floor/ceiling compression can shrink deltas without proving V-JEPA is less useful
```

So yes: AQ.A should be downgraded from "falsifies motion hypothesis" to:

```text
inconclusive; suggests motion difficulty, not V-JEPA motion behavior
```

## AS1. Additional issue: AQ.A appears bucketed by LQ motion, not GT motion

Looking at:

```text
/cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/motion_audit_v3/per_seq_motion_audit.csv
```

the indoor buckets appear ordered by `motion_lq`, not `motion_hq`. This violates the main AR1 guardrail from my previous response.

Examples:

```text
pair6_2:
  motion_lq = 0.00816  -> dynamic by LQ
  motion_hq = 0.00481  -> not high by GT

pair34_2:
  motion_lq = 0.00807  -> dynamic by LQ
  motion_hq = 0.00391  -> very low by GT

pair4:
  motion_lq = 0.00798  -> dynamic by LQ
  motion_hq = 0.00529  -> low/mid by GT
```

This means the "dynamic" bucket may partly be:

```text
low-light noise / exposure instability / LQ flicker
```

not true scene or camera motion. Therefore the current AQ.A bucket result cannot support a motion-prior conclusion either way.

This makes AR2.B mandatory before interpretation.

## AS2. AR1 is directionally right, but external SOTA is not the only clean frame

I agree that internal noJEPA is insufficient to answer "does V-JEPA help motion?", but I would not say the only right comparison is published SOTA.

The clean hierarchy is:

```text
Level 1: internal re-aggregation using GT-based motion buckets
         cheap, sanity-checks AQ.A and finds whether the observed shrink is just bucket noise

Level 2: external method on same local 14 sequences
```

# Author Posts — AT. AR2.B Re-Aggregation Result: AQ.A Was a Bucketing Artifact (2026-05-02)

## AT0. Headline

AS1's catch was decisive. AQ.A's "anti-motion" verdict was driven entirely by **bucketing on motion_lq instead of motion_hq**. When sequences are bucketed by GT frame difference (the true motion proxy), the apparent anti-correlation vanishes — V-JEPA's contribution is **roughly uniform across motion levels**, with v9.0 lift actually slightly *higher* on dynamic content.

```text
AQ.A verdict (motion_lq bucketing, BUGGY):
  v9.0 lift drops from 15.91 (static) to 11.46 (dynamic) — apparent strong anti-correlation

AT verdict (motion_hq bucketing, CORRECT):
  v9.0 lift goes 14.77 → 14.13 → 15.20 across (static, mild, dynamic) — roughly flat / mild U
  Δ(v9.0 − noJEPA) by bucket: 3.13 / 4.57 / 3.76 — uniform within ~1.5 dB
```

## AT1. Bucket assignment disagreement (the smoking gun)

```text
seq         motion_hq   motion_lq   bucket_by_hq   bucket_by_lq
pair34_2    0.004       0.008       static         dynamic     ← OPPOSITE buckets
pair6_2     0.005       0.008       static         dynamic     ← OPPOSITE
pair4       0.005       0.008       mild           dynamic     ← misclassified
pair7       0.006       0.005       mild           static      ← misclassified other way
pair3_2     0.009       0.007       dynamic        mild
```

5 of 14 sequences ended up in different buckets when measured by GT vs LQ frame diff. The "dynamic by motion_lq" bucket was contaminated with low-light noise/flicker masquerading as motion.

## AT2. Primary table — bucket by motion_hq (corrected)

Per-bucket aggregates over 14 SDSD-indoor sequences, RGB-PSNR uint8 full-frame tiled inference:

| Bucket | n | LQ | v9.0 | v9.0b_mix | v9.1a | noJEPA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| static | 5 | 7.94 | 22.71 | 22.87 | 22.06 | 19.58 |
| mild | 5 | 8.59 | 22.72 | 23.04 | 22.83 | 18.15 |
| dynamic | 4 | 10.23 | 25.43 | 24.42 | 25.11 | 21.66 |

### AT2.1. Lift over LQ (the relevant signal)

| Bucket | n | lift_v9.0 | lift_v9.0b_mix | lift_v9.1a | lift_noJEPA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| static | 5 | **14.77** | 14.93 | 14.12 | 11.64 |
| mild | 5 | 14.13 | 14.45 | 14.25 | 9.57 |
| dynamic | 4 | **15.20** | 14.20 | 14.88 | 11.44 |

→ v9.0's lift is roughly flat (14.13 → 15.20). It even goes UP slightly on dynamic (+0.43 over static). Same pattern for v9.1a (+0.76).

→ noJEPA's lift dips on mild (9.57) but recovers on dynamic (11.44). Not a clean monotone pattern either way.

→ Δ(v9.0 − noJEPA) by bucket: **3.13 / 4.57 / 3.76** — uniform within ~1.5 dB.

## AT3. Sensitivity: bucket by motion_lq (the buggy one for comparison)

| Bucket | n | lift_v9.0 | lift_v9.0b_mix | lift_v9.1a | lift_noJEPA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| static | 5 | 15.91 | 16.45 | 15.13 | 9.53 |
| mild | 5 | 15.99 | 15.22 | 15.01 | 11.83 |
| dynamic | 4 | **11.46** | 11.32 | 12.68 | 11.25 |

This is what produced AQ.A's "anti-motion" verdict. Note that **all V-JEPA models** (v9.0, v9.0b_mix, v9.1a) drop sharply on motion_lq dynamic, while noJEPA stays flat. That alone should have warned us: if removing V-JEPA *eliminates* the bucket effect, it's not a V-JEPA-specific signal — it's a noise/exposure artifact.

## AT4. Correlation analysis (AS3 step 5)

Pearson r per ckpt over 14 sequences:

| Model | r(lift, motion_hq) | r(lift, motion_lq) | r(lift, LQ baseline) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v9.0_best | +0.165 | **−0.341** | −0.048 |
| v9.0b_mix_best | −0.006 | **−0.428** | −0.148 |
| v9.1a_best | +0.219 | **−0.276** | −0.107 |
| v9.0-noJEPA_best | +0.143 | **+0.334** | −0.105 |

Reading:
- **All V-JEPA models** show strong **negative** correlation between lift and motion_lq.
- **noJEPA shows POSITIVE** correlation between lift and motion_lq.
- All show ≈0 correlation with motion_hq.

The opposite signs on motion_lq for V-JEPA vs noJEPA cleanly confirms: motion_lq is measuring **low-light noise**, not scene motion. V-JEPA-conditioned models lose lift on noisy clips (V-JEPA's invariance presumably anchors the prediction toward a "clean" estimate that doesn't match the noisy LQ); noJEPA gains lift on noisy clips (more gradient signal from larger LQ→HQ difference).

→ Neither pattern says anything about V-JEPA's motion behavior. The motion question is simply orthogonal to lift on this dataset.

## AT5. Updated verdict

```text
AT verdict (replacing AQ.A):
  V-JEPA cross-attn provides ~3-4.5 dB uniform lift over noJEPA across motion levels.
  No motion-specific behavior detectable on SDSD-indoor static_np.
  
  motion_lq is a noise/exposure-confounded measure and should not be used as a
  motion proxy on low-light video data.
  
  motion_hq (GT frame diff) is the right proxy and shows V-JEPA's contribution is
  uniform with respect to motion.
```

Original AS interpretation table maps to:

```text
"All model lifts roughly flat across motion_hq buckets":
  → V-JEPA's contribution is motion-neutral
  → V-JEPA-specific motion claim was previously unresolved; now: NO motion-specific signal
```

## AT6. What this means for next steps

```text
v9.3-temporal-adapter:                    STILL not justified
                                          (no motion correlation in either direction)

v9.3-bigdata (BVI-RLV scale upgrade):     defensible on dataset-scale grounds
                                          NOT defensible on "motion lever" grounds

AR2.A (LLVE-STCD external comparison):    PRIORITY DROPPED
                                          (the motion question is now answered: uniform)
                                          (still useful for paper-comparable headline number)

PROGRESS.md / paper writeup:              STRONG CANDIDATE for next step
                                          (we have a coherent set of findings now)
```

## AT7. Three concrete next options

```text

          — consolidate AQ + AR + AT story
          — V-JEPA dense conditioning is load-bearing and motion-neutral
          — pixel decoder is the lever for further gain
          — defensible negative results for v9.1a, v9.2-affd, motion-temporal-adapter
          Cost: ~1-2 h writeup, no GPU.

          Cost: ~1.5 day setup (BVI-RLV download + dataset code + 7500 iter training)
```

## AT8. My recommendation

I lean **Option 1 + Option 3 in parallel**:

## AZ1. My call on AY3.4

I do **not** choose A as the next main target.

Writing the empirical-study draft now is fine as a living note, but it should
not be the main next step. The draft would mostly say "V-JEPA dense features
help, but the model is below SOTA and the V-JEPA-specific mechanism is not
fully proven." That is honest, but not a strong next research move.

I also do **not** choose BVI-RLV scale-up as the immediate next step.

BVI-RLV is likely the right dataset-scale move later, but starting it now would
skip the central unresolved question:

```text
Is v9.0 benefiting from V-JEPA's video/temporal prior,
or just from a strong frozen spatial semantic prior?
```

If the current cross-attention mostly consumes spatial scene tokens and ignores
temporal structure, then BVI-RLV's motion richness may improve the pixel branch
through data scale, but it would not validate the V-JEPA motion-prior story.

I choose **D, but in a narrower and cheaper form first**:

```text
Next target: v9.3-prior-ablation

Goal:
  determine whether the current v9 architecture actually uses
  V-JEPA temporal/spatial priors, before committing to BVI-RLV or a paper.
```

## AZ2. Locked immediate experiment: v9.3-prior-ablation

This should start with **inference-only ablations on v9.0_best**, not a full
training run.

Use the same checkpoint, same SDSD/static_np 14 indoor eval split, same
RGB-full-frame tiled audit where feasible, and first run a quick RGB-256 audit
if full-frame is slow.

Required modes:

```text
Mode 0: full_vjepa
  Current v9.0 behavior. Baseline.

Mode 1: temporal_center_only / center_repeat
  Replace the V-JEPA temporal token bank with center-frame tokens only
  (or repeat center-frame tokens across all query frames, depending on current tensor layout).

Mode 2: temporal_shuffle
  Shuffle the V-JEPA token time dimension within each clip with a fixed seed,
  preserving token values and spatial grids but breaking temporal alignment.

Mode 3: spatial_shuffle
  Shuffle the V-JEPA HxW token positions within each frame with a fixed seed,
  preserving token distribution but breaking spatial correspondence.
```

Interpretation:

```text
If temporal_center_only ≈ full_vjepa and temporal_shuffle ≈ full_vjepa:
  Current v9.0 is not measurably using V-JEPA temporal structure.
  Do not claim motion-prior usage. BVI-RLV becomes a pure data-scale/performance
  experiment, not a V-JEPA-temporal validation.

If temporal_shuffle drops clearly but center_only does not:
  Some temporal ordering/alignment matters, but temporal redundancy may be enough.
  Then a small temporal adapter may be worth revisiting, but only with this evidence.

If temporal_center_only and temporal_shuffle both drop:
  Current model uses cross-frame V-JEPA context. This would justify BVI-RLV
  as a motion-rich scale-up and strengthen the V-JEPA-specific paper story.

If spatial_shuffle drops strongly while temporal modes barely move:
  V-JEPA is mainly acting as a spatial semantic/structure prior.
  Then compare against DINOv2/other image backbones before making a V-JEPA-specific claim.
```

Suggested decision thresholds:

```text
< 0.2 dB RGB-full / RGB-256 change:
  treat as no meaningful dependence.

0.2-0.5 dB:
  weak signal; repeat on full-frame tiled and inspect per-sequence spread.

> 0.5 dB:
  meaningful dependence; use it to choose the next architecture/data step.
```

## AZ3. What comes after v9.3-prior-ablation

Do not decide BVI-RLV vs paper vs backbone replacement until this ablation lands.

Post-ablation forks:

```text
Fork A: temporal ablation shows no temporal dependence
  Next: DINOv2 / VideoMAE / other frozen-backbone control, or BVI-RLV framed
        strictly as data-scale performance work.
  Paper wording: "V-JEPA dense spatial conditioning helps", not "motion prior helps".

Fork B: temporal ablation shows clear temporal dependence
  Next: BVI-RLV feasibility/download/smoke test, then v9.3-bigdata.
  Paper wording: V-JEPA temporal context is actually being consumed.

Fork C: spatial shuffle hurts but temporal shuffle does not
  Next: image-backbone control before BVI-RLV.
  Reason: the useful prior may be spatial semantics rather than V-JEPA video dynamics.

Fork D: all ablations barely move PSNR
  Next: inspect implementation. The V-JEPA-conditioned path may be robustly bypassed,
        and the noJEPA gap may be caused by training dynamics/capacity rather than
        inference-time feature dependence.
```
