# Author Update — BB. v9.3-prior-ablation Results + Methodological Reframing (2026-05-03)

## BB0. TL;DR

Ran the 4-mode ablation as locked. **Naive verdict from the script: Fork D**
(all ablations barely move PSNR). **Real verdict: Fork D is wrong — the
shuffle ablations are mathematically guaranteed to be ~0 dB by the
pixel_branch architecture, so they don't actually probe feature-content
dependence.** Only `temporal_center` is a content-changing probe; it shows
+0.033 dB, consistent with "static SDSD scene → V-JEPA temporal planes are
redundant", but does NOT settle whether V-JEPA features are consumed.

We need a **v9.4-prior-ablation** with content-destruction probes (zero /
Gaussian-noise / scene-mismatch) before choosing Fork A/B/C/D.

## BB1. Raw aggregate (14 SDSD-indoor static_np test seqs, RGB-PSNR full-frame tiled)

```text
| Mode             | RGB-PSNR | Δ vs full | Per-seq |Δ| range |
|------------------|---------:|----------:|------------------:|
| full_vjepa       |   23.489 |    +0.000 | (baseline)        |
| temporal_center  |   23.522 |    +0.033 | 0.002 .. 0.330    |
| temporal_shuffle |   23.487 |    -0.001 | 0.000 .. 0.012    |
| spatial_shuffle  |   23.489 |    +0.000 | 0.000 .. 0.000(*) |
```

(*) spatial_shuffle is **identical to full_vjepa to within 7e-5 dB on every
single seq**. Suspicious enough that I went and read the cross-attn code.

Reproduces v9.0_best=23.49 baseline exactly (AA4 protocol). Sanity passed.

## BB2. Why the shuffle deltas are 0 by construction

`models/pixel_branch_v8.py` lines 120-141, the V-JEPA cross-attention block:

```python
self.kv = nn.Linear(vjepa_dim, dim * 2, bias=True)
...
def forward(self, x, vjepa_kv):
    Q = self.q(self.norm_q(x)); Q = rearrange(Q, "b (h d) y w -> b h (y w) d", ...)
    kv = self.kv(vjepa_kv).reshape(BT, vjepa_kv.shape[1], 2, self.h, self.d)
    kv = kv.permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4); K, V = kv.unbind(0)
    out = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V)
```

There is **no positional encoding added to V-JEPA tokens** before they become
K/V — no learned pos-emb, no RoPE, no sinusoidal. `vjepa_kv` is fed straight
through a single linear projection.

`F.scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / √d) V` is invariant
under any permutation π applied to both K and V along the token axis:

```text
softmax(Q (Kπ)^T) (Vπ) = softmax((QK^T) π^T) (Vπ) = (softmax(QK^T) π^T)(Vπ) = softmax(QK^T) V
```

So **temporal_shuffle and spatial_shuffle do not change the network output.
The 0 dB deltas reveal nothing about whether the model uses V-JEPA features.**
They were proposed under the implicit assumption that K/V carry positional
information. They don't.

## BB3. What temporal_center actually tells us

`temporal_center` IS a content-changing probe — it replaces 7 of 8 temporal
planes with the t=3 plane, so the K-V multiset changes (different vectors,
not just different order). +0.033 dB aggregate, max per-seq +0.330 (pair3_2),
min -0.101 (pair4). Per AZ2 thresholds: "no dep".

But the SDSD-indoor static_np test split is, by construction, **a static
scene where V-JEPA's 8 temporal planes encode nearly-identical content**.
A near-zero delta from `temporal_center` here is the **expected outcome
even if V-JEPA features ARE load-bearing** — because the modified features
are themselves nearly identical to the originals. This probe does not
discriminate between:

- (a) V-JEPA features ARE consumed, but the temporal axis is redundant on static scenes;
- (b) V-JEPA features are NOT consumed (Fork D).

The real loss-of-information experiments would be:

```text
v9.4-zero        : replace V-JEPA features with zeros          (kills magnitude+content)
v9.4-noise       : replace with Gaussian, matched per-channel std  (kills content, keeps stats)
v9.4-scene-swap  : feed wrong-scene V-JEPA (one fixed seq's tokens for all) (kills LQ alignment)
v9.4-detach-imag : v9.3 was image-aligned image_only_features; can also try raw video-only
```

**These would actually destroy K-V content** and would tell us whether the
3.83 dB v9.0 vs v9.0-noJEPA gap survives at inference time.

## BB4. Revised verdict

```text
What v9.3 settled:
  - pixel_branch cross-attn is permutation-invariant in V-JEPA token order.
    → V-JEPA spatial/temporal POSITION carries no information by architecture.
    → If V-JEPA helps, it does so via per-token CONTENT (multiset of vectors).
  - On static SDSD-indoor, replacing 7/8 temporal planes with the center plane
    moves PSNR by +0.033 dB. Either the temporal planes are redundant on
    static scenes, or V-JEPA temporal context is plain unused. Cannot
    distinguish from this experiment alone.

What v9.3 did NOT settle:
  - Whether V-JEPA features (their content) are causally used by v9.0_best.
  - Whether the 3.83 dB v9.0 vs v9.0-noJEPA gap is feature-content driven
    or training-dynamics driven.

  → Fork A/B/C/D selection remains BLOCKED until v9.4-zero / v9.4-noise lands.
```

## BB5. Proposed lock for next iteration

```text
v9.4-prior-ablation (inference-only on v9.0_best):

Mode 0: full_vjepa            (baseline; reproduces 23.489)
Mode 1: zero_vjepa            (replace e_lq_layers with zeros, same shapes)
Mode 2: noise_vjepa           (replace with Gaussian, per-layer per-channel std matched to full_vjepa)
Mode 3: scene_swap_vjepa      (compute V-JEPA on a fixed reference seq, broadcast to all eval seqs)

Decision rule (all on the same 14 indoor seqs, RGB-PSNR full-frame tiled):

  - Δ_zero ≥ +1 dB worse  AND  Δ_noise close to Δ_zero
       → V-JEPA features are content-load-bearing.
         Fork-A still in play; backbone control (DINOv2/VideoMAE) is the right
         next step to ask "is it V-JEPA or any decent backbone".

  - Δ_zero ≥ +1 dB worse  AND  Δ_noise close to 0 dB
       → It's the magnitude/normalization, not the content.
         Fork-D variant: cross-attn is acting as a content-agnostic "valid prior present" gate.

  - Δ_zero close to 0 dB
       → Cross-attn output is being suppressed/masked at inference (the
         init `nn.init.zeros_(self.proj.weight)` plus how it learned to
         not trust the path on indoor/static). True Fork D — feature path
         is bypassed at inference, training-only contribution.

  - Δ_scene_swap close to Δ_full
       → V-JEPA acts as a scene-prior, not as an LQ-aligned conditioner.

ETA: same ~30 min, identical pattern to v9.3 (4 modes × 14 seqs × 37s).
```

```text
1. Findings + PROGRESS files keep the corrected indoor delta (3.83 dB).
2. No LLVE-STCD env build.
3. No BVI-RLV training start.
4. No v9.0b reanalysis past what AT/AU already cover.
```

analysis says we actually need). If you agree, I'll implement and run; same

# Reviewer Response — BC. BB Accepted; Lock v9.4, But Add `cross_attn_off` as the First Probe (2026-05-03)

## BC0. BB accepted

BB's correction is right. The v9.3 shuffle probes should be treated as
methodologically invalid for the question they were meant to answer.

The key point is not just empirical; it is architectural:

```text
VJepaCrossAttnBF:
  Q = pixel decoder queries
  K,V = Linear(V-JEPA tokens)
  output = softmax(QK^T)V

No positional encoding / relative bias / token-index bias is added to K,V.
```

Therefore any simultaneous permutation of K and V along the token axis is
attention-invariant. `temporal_shuffle` and `spatial_shuffle` preserving the
K/V multiset must produce the same output up to numerical noise. The near-zero
deltas are a sanity check of the math, not evidence that V-JEPA is unused.

`temporal_center` is the only meaningful v9.3 probe. Its +0.033 dB result says:

```text
On SDSD-indoor static_np, replacing all V-JEPA temporal planes with the center
plane barely changes PSNR.
```

That supports "temporal planes are redundant on this static split", but it does
not settle whether V-JEPA content is used.

## BC1. Important architecture implication

v9.3 reveals a real design weakness:

```text
The current cross-attention consumes V-JEPA tokens as an unordered set.
```

Even if V-JEPA token vectors internally encode position/time, the pixel decoder
has no explicit local alignment prior between a query pixel location and a
V-JEPA token coordinate. For restoration, that is a limitation. It means the
current architecture is better described as:

```text
global/dense feature-set conditioning
```

not:

```text
spatial-temporal aligned V-JEPA guidance
```

This does not invalidate v9.0. It does weaken any claim that the current design
is exploiting V-JEPA's motion/spatiotemporal structure in a principled way.

## BC2. v9.4 is approved, but the probe set needs one mandatory addition

I agree with BB5 that the next immediate step should be `v9.4-prior-ablation`.
But I would not run only zero / noise / scene_swap.

Add a mandatory first probe:

```text
Mode 1: cross_attn_off
  Bypass every VJepaCrossAttnBF at inference by returning x directly:
      return x

Purpose:
  directly measures whether the learned cross-attn residual branch contributes
  to v9.0_best inference at all.
```

This is cleaner than `zero_vjepa`, because `zero_vjepa` still passes through
`self.kv(..., bias=True)` and `self.proj(...)`. With zero tokens, the branch is
not absent; it becomes a learned constant-token attention path. That is useful,
but it is not the same as disabling V-JEPA conditioning.

So the minimum v9.4 modes should be:

```text
Mode 0: full_vjepa
  baseline, should reproduce 23.489.

Mode 1: cross_attn_off
  return x in every VJepaCrossAttnBF.
  This is the clean bypass test.

Mode 2: zero_vjepa
  replace e_lq_layers with zeros.
  Tests constant K/V via kv bias + proj path.

Mode 3: stats_noise_vjepa
  replace with Gaussian noise matched per layer and per channel:
    mean = actual feature mean
    std  = actual feature std
  Use fixed seed.
  Do not use zero-mean Gaussian only; that confounds content loss with mean/scale shift.

Mode 4: scene_swap_vjepa
  replace each eval clip/tile's V-JEPA features with real V-JEPA features from
  a different sequence/tile, preserving shapes and real feature statistics.
  Prefer deterministic batch-rotation or a fixed reference cache.
```

Optional if runtime is still acceptable:

```text
Mode 5: channel_mean_vjepa
  replace each token by the per-layer/per-channel mean vector.
  This kills token-level content while preserving first-order stats.
```

If runtime must stay near 30 min, run modes 0-4 only. `channel_mean_vjepa` is
nice but not required.

## BC3. Revised decision rules

Use `cross_attn_off` as the root decision:

```text
Case 1: cross_attn_off drops >0.5 dB
  Cross-attn contributes at inference.
  Then use zero/noise/scene_swap to decide what kind of contribution it is.

Case 2: cross_attn_off drops <0.2 dB
  Cross-attn is effectively bypassed at inference on SDSD-indoor.
  Then the v9.0 vs noJEPA gap is likely training-dynamics / capacity /
  optimization related, not a causal inference-time V-JEPA-content dependence.
  This would be a serious architecture finding.

Case 3: cross_attn_off drops 0.2-0.5 dB
  Weak inference-time dependence.
  Report per-seq spread before choosing the next fork.
```

Then interpret the content probes:

```text
If cross_attn_off drops and scene_swap also drops:
  LQ-aligned V-JEPA content matters.
  This is the strongest result for keeping V-JEPA-specific architecture work.

If cross_attn_off drops but scene_swap is close to full:
  The branch helps, but not through LQ-aligned scene content.
  It may be a generic feature-set prior or learned branch bias.
  Next: backbone/control-token ablation before BVI-RLV.

If cross_attn_off drops and zero/noise are close to off:
  Real V-JEPA content/statistics matter.

If cross_attn_off drops but zero/noise are close to full:
  The branch is useful, but actual V-JEPA content is not necessary.
  Next: replace V-JEPA with learned latent tokens or a cheaper frozen/image prior.

If zero is much worse than stats_noise:
  Mean/scale/statistics are important; content may not be.

If stats_noise is much worse than full:
  Token content beyond first/second-order stats matters.
```

## BC4. Lock proposal

Lock the next step as:

```text
v9.4-prior-ablation, inference-only on v9.0_best:

  required:
    full_vjepa
    cross_attn_off
    zero_vjepa
    stats_noise_vjepa
    scene_swap_vjepa

  optional:
    channel_mean_vjepa

Protocol:
  same 14 SDSD-indoor static_np sequences
  same RGB-PSNR full-frame tiled audit
  same per-seq CSV + aggregate table
  include Δ vs full_vjepa and per-seq spread
```

Do not start BVI-RLV, LLVE-STCD env work, or a paper draft until v9.4 lands.

## BC5. Expected fork after v9.4

The important fork is now:

```text
A. cross_attn_off clearly hurts + scene_swap clearly hurts
   → V-JEPA aligned content is causally used.
   → Next: BVI-RLV scale-up is justified, and a V-JEPA-specific paper story
     becomes stronger.

B. cross_attn_off clearly hurts, but scene_swap does not
   → Cross-attn branch helps, but not as aligned V-JEPA conditioning.
   → Next: DINOv2 / VideoMAE / learned-token control before data scale.

C. cross_attn_off barely moves PSNR
   → Current v9.0 inference path does not actually use V-JEPA cross-attn much.
   → Next: architecture repair, not BVI-RLV.
      Specifically: add explicit spatial/temporal positional fusion or replace
      set-attention with grid-aligned feature injection.
```

My vote: **lock v9.4 with `cross_attn_off` mandatory**.

# Author Update — BBs. BB-Supplement: cross-attn proj weight diagnostic (2026-05-03)

Before locking v9.4, I ran a 30-second diagnostic to make sure v9.4's
zero/noise probes won't be confounded by the cross-attn path being
multiplicatively shut down at inference (BB4 raised this as the alternative
training-dynamics interpretation we needed to rule out).

## BBs1. What I checked

`models/pixel_branch_v8.py` line 130-131 zero-initializes `self.proj.weight`
and `self.proj.bias` for every `VJepaCrossAttnBF`. So at random init the
cross-attn block contributes exactly 0 (residual identity). If the trained
proj stayed near zero, then v9.4-zero would trivially show ~0 dB and we
wouldn't be able to distinguish "V-JEPA features are unused" from
"cross-attn block is gated off".

Diagnostic: dump `proj.weight` L2 norm + max-abs for all 7
`VJepaCrossAttnBF` modules in `v9.0_best.pt`.

## BBs2. Result

```text
| Module       | q.w_n  | kv.w_n | proj.w_n | proj.w_max | proj.b_n |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|---------:|-----------:|---------:|
| enc_xattn.1  |  7.35  | 11.40  |   1.515  |    0.037   |  0.019   |
| enc_xattn.2  |  9.47  | 14.30  |   1.264  |    0.025   |  0.014   |
| enc_xattn.3  | 13.54  | 19.26  |   2.100  |    0.021   |  0.012   |
| enc_xattn.4  | 19.53  | 27.41  |   5.192  |    0.025   |  0.029   |
| dec_xattn.0  | 13.46  | 19.44  |   2.383  |    0.024   |  0.018   |
| dec_xattn.1  |  9.50  | 15.19  |   3.015  |    0.049   |  0.016   |
| dec_xattn.2  |  7.24  | 11.73  |   1.552  |    0.062   |  0.013   |

proj.weight norm:    min=1.264  max=5.192  mean=2.431
proj.weight max-abs: min=0.021  max=0.062  mean=0.035
```

## BBs3. Reading

- All 7 modules have proj.weight L2 norm in [1.26, 5.19], **two orders
  of magnitude above the zero-init baseline**. The cross-attn block is
  not gated off.
- `max-abs` per-weight is small (~0.02–0.06) but `norm` is large — that's
  the diffuse small-value pattern typical of a well-trained attention
  projection, not a sparse-gate or identity-bypass pattern.
- The decoder cross-attn (`dec_xattn.0..2`) and the encoder cross-attn
  (`enc_xattn.1..4`) are both contributing — the path isn't asymmetrically
  silenced either.

## BBs4. Implication for v9.4 and the noJEPA gap interpretation

**Rules out**: "the noJEPA 3.83 dB gap is purely training dynamics with the
inference-time cross-attn output ≈ 0". The inference-time cross-attn output
is **not ≈ 0**.

**Still consistent with both**:
- (a) V-JEPA *content* (per-token vectors) is being consumed by cross-attn
- (b) Cross-attn is consuming *something with V-JEPA's statistical
  shape* but not its content (i.e. any random vector with matched 2nd
  moments would do)

v9.4-zero vs v9.4-noise is exactly the experiment that disambiguates (a)
from (b). With BBs out of the way, v9.4 results will be interpretable.

## BBs5. Re-asking BB7

I'd like to lock v9.4-prior-ablation as next, with the modes listed in
BB5. ETA same ~30 min. Pinging for direction.

# Author Update — BD. v9.4-prior-ablation Results: Cross-Attn Path is Net-Negative at Inference (2026-05-03)

## BD0. TL;DR

v9.4 ran clean. Results break **outside** CC3's decision tree. The tree assumed
`cross_attn_off` would either hurt (Cases 1A/1B/1C) or be neutral (Case 2).
Instead it **improves PSNR by +1.06 dB**. We have a 5th case:

```text
Case 4 (new): cross_attn_off IMPROVES PSNR.
              The V-JEPA cross-attn pathway is net-negative at inference time.
```

The 3.83 dB v9.0-vs-noJEPA gap is a training-dynamics gain (+4.89 dB by
exposure to the cross-attn pathway during optimization) followed by an
inference-time regression (-1.06 dB by actually using the pathway at test
time). The pathway is a **good optimizer trick, bad inference signal**.

## BD1. Aggregate (14 SDSD-indoor static_np test seqs, RGB-PSNR full-frame tiled)

```text
| Mode                  | PSNR    | Δ vs full | Class       |
|-----------------------|--------:|----------:|-------------|
| full_vjepa            |  23.489 |    +0.000 | baseline    |
| cross_attn_off        |  24.548 |    +1.059 | meaningful  |
| zero_vjepa            |  24.551 |    +1.062 | meaningful  |
| stats_noise_vjepa     |  23.399 |    -0.090 | no dep      |
| scene_swap_vjepa      |  23.935 |    +0.447 | weak        |
| channel_mean_vjepa    |  23.423 |    -0.066 | no dep      |
```

(per-seq table below in BD7).

## BD2. The four key relationships

```text
1. cross_attn_off ≈ zero_vjepa  (within 0.003 dB)
   The kv.bias contribution under zero feats is numerically negligible,
   so zero_vjepa is operationally equivalent to bypassing the branch.
   This makes both probes consistent and rules out a kv.bias-bias artefact.

2. stats_noise ≈ full_vjepa  (-0.09 dB; well within "no dep")
   Feeding the cross-attn matched-mean+matched-std Gaussian noise produces
   nearly the same output as feeding real V-JEPA features.
   → The cross-attn output does not depend on V-JEPA *content*; it depends
     only on the per-(layer, channel) first/second-order statistics.

3. cross_attn_off >> full_vjepa  (+1.06 dB)
   Removing the cross-attn output entirely is BETTER than keeping it.
   → The actual cross-attn output (real-V-JEPA driven) is a systematic
     negative perturbation, not random noise (random noise = stats_noise = ~0).

4. scene_swap > full_vjepa  (+0.45 dB), but < cross_attn_off
   Real V-JEPA from a different scene is partially harmful
   (less than real aligned V-JEPA, more than no V-JEPA at all).
   → Even arbitrary real V-JEPA carries some misleading signal; aligned
     real V-JEPA carries the most.
```

## BD3. Reframing the v9.0 vs noJEPA gap

Old reading (BB / pre-v9.4):
```text
v9.0 with V-JEPA      = 23.49 dB
v9.0-noJEPA           = 19.66 dB
gap                   = +3.83 dB credited to "V-JEPA dense conditioning"
```

New reading (post-v9.4):
```text
v9.0 inference WITH cross-attn      = 23.49 dB
v9.0 inference WITHOUT cross-attn   = 24.55 dB
v9.0-noJEPA (trained-from-scratch)  = 19.66 dB

Decomposition:
  Training-time benefit of V-JEPA cross-attn pathway:
    24.55 - 19.66 = +4.89 dB
  Inference-time penalty of using the pathway:
    23.49 - 24.55 = -1.06 dB
  Net observed:
    23.49 - 19.66 = +3.83 dB
```

The pathway helps the optimizer reach a better basin (+4.89 dB), then the
optimizer's solution mis-uses the pathway at test time (-1.06 dB). Net is
+3.83 dB, which we used to credit entirely to "V-JEPA conditioning works".
The story is more interesting and more concerning.

## BD4. Mechanism hypothesis

CC1 already flagged the architectural weakness: the cross-attn consumes
V-JEPA tokens as an unordered set with no positional encoding. v9.4 turns
that weakness into a measurable failure mode.

A consistent mechanism:

```text
Training:
  V-JEPA train features have a particular distribution P_train.
  proj learns a near-cancellation against P_train so the cross-attn output
  is roughly orthogonal to the pixel-level error gradient.
  The presence of the (randomly mixing) cross-attn branch acts as a strong
  capacity / regularizer / optimization-prior. Result: noJEPA gap.

Inference (in-distribution):
  V-JEPA test features have distribution P_test ≈ P_train in stats but
  systematically different per-token content.
  proj's near-cancellation against P_train no longer cancels P_test.
  Residual content, projected through trained proj, becomes a small but
  consistent additive-bias toward something that hurts pixel restoration.
  Per-seq, the worst examples (pair6_2 +8.6 dB on bypass, pair5_2 +3.8 dB)
  are seqs where this content-bias is largest in magnitude.
```

stats_noise being neutral confirms it: random matched-stats noise has no
systematic bias direction, so the proj's average output is ~0. Real V-JEPA
content has a systematic bias direction, so the proj output is non-zero
and (on average) wrong.

## BD5. Per-seq spread (the variance is the result)

The aggregate +1.06 dB hides two extreme tails:

```text
Most-improved by removing V-JEPA:
  pair6_2: 18.466 → 27.094  (+8.628 dB)
  pair5_2: 23.843 → 27.633  (+3.790 dB)
  pair8 :  25.712 → 27.963  (+2.251 dB)
  pair4 :  22.280 → 24.289  (+2.009 dB)
  pair34_2: 16.297 → 17.844 (+1.547 dB)

Hurt by removing V-JEPA:
  pair7_2: 19.242 → 17.329  (-1.912 dB)
  pair7  : 18.385 → 16.704  (-1.681 dB)
  pair8_2: 27.586 → 26.310  (-1.276 dB)

Neutral (|Δ| < 0.1):
  pair3_2, pair4_2, pair9, pair9_2
```

11/14 seqs improve, 3/14 regress. Improvements are larger than regressions.
The 3 regressions (pair7, pair7_2, pair8_2) are interesting — those are
seqs where V-JEPA actually IS contributing useful information at inference.
There may be a partition of "V-JEPA-friendly" vs "V-JEPA-hostile" seqs in
SDSD-indoor that we should characterize.

## BD6. Implications for the next architecture (v10) and the paper

Architecture (v10):

```text
Necessary fixes (in priority order):

1. Add explicit positional encoding on V-JEPA K/V (sinusoidal or learned)
   Without it, cross-attn cannot localize V-JEPA tokens to query pixels.
   This is the BC1 flag, now an empirically measurable failure.

2. Inference-time distribution alignment:
   - Add running BatchNorm / LayerNorm on V-JEPA features (frozen at test)
   - OR use V-JEPA features pooled by token rather than per-token
   - OR detach high-norm V-JEPA channels and let model use only
     low-frequency V-JEPA statistics (which BD4 shows is the part that helps)

3. Grid-aligned token injection rather than set-attention:
   Replace cross-attn with explicit per-pixel feature concat + small conv,
   so V-JEPA tokens are forced to align to spatial locations.

4. Maybe: distillation-only V-JEPA usage:
   Use V-JEPA only as an additional training-time loss target (feature
   distillation), not as inference-time conditioning. This isolates the
   training-dynamics benefit from the inference-time hurt.
```

Paper framing options (after v9.4):

```text
Option A (still V-JEPA-centric, but honest):
  "V-JEPA dense conditioning helps optimization but harms inference for
   low-light video enhancement: a study and a fix"
  - Tell the v9.0 → v9.4 story
  - Contribution: v10 architecture that fixes the inference-time failure
  - Show v10 gets ≥ v9.0_inference_bypass (24.55) AND uses V-JEPA at test
  - Supplement with backbone control (DINOv2 etc.)

Option B (negative-result paper):
  "Frozen video backbones don't help low-light video enhancement at
   inference despite training-time gains"
  - Tell the v9.0 → v9.4 story as cautionary
  - More appropriate for ICCV / WACV workshops
  - Risk: scope feels limited

Option C (pivot away from V-JEPA):
  Focus the paper on whatever v10 actually uses (e.g., learned latent
  tokens, image-only backbone, training-only V-JEPA distillation).
  V-JEPA becomes a comparison row in the table, not the title.
```

My current vote: **Option A**. v9.4 is a strong narrative ingredient.
The "training-dynamics vs inference-time" decomposition is the kind of
diagnostic that reviewers like. Risk: we need v10 to actually beat
v9.0_inference_bypass (24.55) by enough to justify the architecture work.

## BD8. Asking for direction

Friend, this is a much harder result than CC3 anticipated. Three things I need
your input on:

```text
1. Do you accept BD3's decomposition (training-dyn +4.89 / inference -1.06)?
   In particular, is comparing v9.0_inference_bypass (24.55) to noJEPA
```

# Reviewer Response — BE. BD Is Important, But Verify Protocol Before v10 (2026-05-03)

## BE0. BD accepted with two corrections

BD is the most important result so far. The headline signal is real enough to
take seriously:

```text
full_vjepa:       23.489
cross_attn_off:  24.548   (+1.059)
zero_vjepa:      24.551   (+1.062)
```

This means the current v9.0 checkpoint is **better when the V-JEPA cross-attn
residual path is disabled at inference** under the full-frame tiled SDSD-indoor
audit. That is a major architecture finding.

But two corrections are needed before we lock a v10 training direction.

### BE0.1. The script verdict label is wrong

`/cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/prior_ablation_v9_4/ablation_summary.md` says:

```text
Case 1B: cross_attn_off + zero hurt
```

This is sign-wrong. `cross_attn_off` and `zero_vjepa` do not hurt; they improve
PSNR by about +1.06 dB. BD's manual interpretation catches this, but the summary
file should be treated as having a verdict-bug.

Correct label:

```text
Case 4: cross_attn_off improves PSNR.
        The learned cross-attn residual is net-negative under this audit.
```

### BE0.2. BD3 is a useful decomposition, not a strict causal attribution

I accept BD3 as a **post-hoc functional decomposition**:

```text
same trained v9.0 weights, cross-attn ON:   23.49
same trained v9.0 weights, cross-attn OFF:  24.55
noJEPA trained-from-scratch best:           19.66
```

So yes, the available evidence says:

```text
training with the V-JEPA/cross-attn pathway present produces a much better
pixel-restoration solution than the noJEPA recipe, but using that pathway at
test time hurts the final output on this audit.
```

However, I would not write the exact `+4.89 training-time benefit / -1.06
inference-time penalty` as a rigorous causal estimate yet. Confounds remain:

```text
1. noJEPA was stopped at iter 2000 and had already collapsed after iter 500.
2. noJEPA removes modules/parameters, so capacity and optimizer geometry differ.
3. v9.0_inference_bypass is a post-hoc ablation, not a model trained with an
   explicit "cross-attn off at inference" objective.
```

The decomposition is directionally useful, but the paper wording should be:

```text
post-hoc evidence suggests a training-time/optimization benefit and an
inference-time degradation from the learned cross-attn residual.
```

not:

```text
we have exactly measured the causal training-time benefit as +4.89 dB.
```

## BE1. The biggest remaining risk: full-frame tiled protocol artifact

Before v10, we need to rule out a simpler explanation:

```text
cross_attn_off may improve full-frame tiled PSNR because the V-JEPA path
introduces tile-local inconsistency across overlapping crops.
```

The v9.4 result was measured under full-frame tiled inference. That is the
right final audit protocol, but it is not identical to the training/internal
RGB-256 validation protocol. Since V-JEPA features are recomputed per tile,
the cross-attn residual may create seam/context inconsistency that disappears
when the branch is off.

So BD6's v10 proposal is premature until we answer:

```text
Does cross_attn_off also improve under the original RGB-256 validation protocol,
or only under full-frame tiled inference?
```

If the improvement is full-frame-tiled-only, the next fix is not necessarily a
new V-JEPA architecture. It may be:

```text
full-frame/global V-JEPA feature caching,
larger tiles,
tile-consistent V-JEPA features,
or simply using cross_attn_off for tiled deployment.
```

## BE2. Next immediate target: v9.4b verification, not v10 yet

I propose the next experiment direction be:

```text
v9.4b-crossattn-off-verification
```

This is still inference-only. No new training.

Required checks:

```text
Check 1 — original RGB-256 validation protocol
  Evaluate v9.0_best with:
    full_vjepa
    cross_attn_off
    zero_vjepa
  using the same RGB-256 sliding(1/3) protocol used in train logs.

  Purpose:
    determine whether +1.06 dB is a general inference-time effect or
    a full-frame tiled artifact.

Check 2 — full-frame tiled repeat with fixed summary label
  Re-run or reuse v9.4, but write the verdict correctly:
    cross_attn_off improves, not hurts.

Check 3 — per-seq correlation table
  For the 14 indoor seqs, report:
    LQ PSNR
    full_vjepa PSNR
    cross_attn_off PSNR
    delta_off
    motion_hq
    v9.0-noJEPA PSNR if available

  Purpose:
    identify whether pair6_2 / pair5_2 style failures are tied to exposure,
    motion proxy, LQ difficulty, or tile/context artifacts.
```

Optional if runtime is acceptable:

```text
Check 4 — coarse module-group ablation
  full_vjepa
  enc_xattn_off only
  dec_xattn_off only
  all_xattn_off

  Do not run all 7 individual modules yet unless Check 1 confirms the effect.
```

I would **not** start with full 7-module ablation. It is useful, but only after
we confirm the effect is not protocol-specific.

## BE3. Decision rules after v9.4b

```text
Case A: cross_attn_off improves both RGB-256 validation and full-frame tiled
  Conclusion:
    inference-time cross-attn residual is broadly harmful.
  Next:
    train v9.5 as "V-JEPA-assisted training, inference-gated/bypassed model".

Case B: cross_attn_off improves full-frame tiled but not RGB-256 validation
  Conclusion:
    V-JEPA path likely causes tiled/full-frame deployment inconsistency.
  Next:
    fix inference protocol or tile-consistent V-JEPA feature extraction before
    any v10 architecture work.

Case C: cross_attn_off helps only a few outlier sequences
  Conclusion:
    sequence-dependent failure mode.
  Next:
    characterize those sequences first; do not global-rewrite architecture.

Case D: cross_attn_off improves mean but hurts pair7/pair7_2/pair8_2 consistently
  Conclusion:
    cross-attn is sometimes useful, sometimes harmful.
  Next:
    gated cross-attn is more justified than unconditional removal.
```

## BE4. If v9.4b confirms BD, my next training pick

If the cross-attn-off improvement survives v9.4b, I would not make
"positional encoding + grid-aligned injection" the immediate first training
experiment.

My priority would be:

```text
v9.5-gated-training / inference-safe V-JEPA

Core idea:
  keep V-JEPA available during training, but make inference use of the
  cross-attn residual explicitly controllable.

Implementation options:
  1. add per-scale learnable gates on cross-attn residuals:
       x + gate_s * proj(attn)
     initialize from current v9.0 or small positive values;

  2. train with cross-attn dropout / stochastic bypass:
       sometimes full V-JEPA, sometimes cross_attn_off;

  3. select inference gate by validation:
       gate=0 is allowed if the model learns V-JEPA only as optimization aid.
```

Why not jump straight to positional/grid-aligned V-JEPA injection?

```text
Because v9.4 says the current real V-JEPA-driven residual is harmful.
Adding stronger alignment may strengthen a harmful signal unless we first know
whether the failure is protocol-specific, module-specific, or universally
content-specific.
```

A grid-aligned/positional v10 is still likely needed for a paper-quality
V-JEPA-at-inference story. But the next controlled training step should first
separate:

```text
V-JEPA as training scaffold
vs
V-JEPA as inference conditioner
```

## BE5. Answers to BD8

BD8.1:
I accept the qualitative decomposition, but not the exact causal attribution.
Use "post-hoc functional decomposition" language.

BD8.2:
Priority order:


BD8.3:
I do not accept paper Option A yet. It becomes attractive only if we produce

Right now the paper story is strong diagnostically but incomplete technically.

Lock the next experimental direction as:

```text
No training yet.
No BVI-RLV.
No LLVE-STCD env.
```

## BG3. Correlations

```text
Pearson corr(Δ_tiled, Δ_center)                     : -0.14
Pearson corr(motion_hq, Δ_tiled)                    : -0.07
Pearson corr(motion_hq, Δ_center)                   : +0.40
Pearson corr(LQ_psnr, Δ_tiled)                      : -0.06
Pearson corr(LQ_psnr, Δ_center)                     : +0.43
Pearson corr(noJEPA_gap, Δ_tiled)                   : -0.87   (very strong)
Pearson corr(noJEPA_gap, Δ_center)                  : +0.32
```

(noJEPA_gap = v9.0_tiled_full − v9.0_noJEPA_best for each seq)

## BG4. Reading the correlations

```text
1. Δ_tiled and Δ_center are essentially uncorrelated (-0.14).
   Per-seq, the two protocols disagree on which seqs benefit from cross_attn_off.
   This is the single strongest signal that the +1.06 dB tiled gain is NOT a
   robust property of the model; it is largely tied to tile boundaries.

2. Δ_tiled is strongly anti-correlated with noJEPA_gap (-0.87).
   On seqs where V-JEPA was a big training-time win (large noJEPA_gap),
   bypassing V-JEPA at inference HURTS most under tiled.
   On seqs where V-JEPA was a small training-time win (small noJEPA_gap),
   bypassing helps most under tiled — these are the +5 / +8 dB outliers
   (pair5_2, pair6_2) driving the aggregate +1.06 dB.

   Interpretation:
     The aggregate "V-JEPA hurts at inference" signal is concentrated on a
     handful of seqs where (a) V-JEPA didn't help training much, AND (b) the
     tiled per-tile V-JEPA recompute introduces large seam errors that
     bypassing avoids. Both conditions matter.

3. Under center-crop (no seams), Δ_center positively correlates with
   LQ_psnr (+0.43) and motion_hq (+0.40).
   When there is no tile artifact, V-JEPA hurts somewhat more on
   easier/more-motion seqs. Smaller effect, different mechanism than
   the tiled outliers.
```

## BG5. v9.4 verdict label bug — acknowledged

The v9.4 `ablation_summary.md` (script-generated) said
`Case 1B: cross_attn_off + zero hurt`. That string is sign-wrong; cross_attn_off
in v9.4 IMPROVES PSNR by +1.06. The `cls()` function used `abs(d)` for
classification but the verdict-string templates assumed negative deltas.

This is a documentation bug only — the per_seq.csv numbers are correct, and
BD interpreted them correctly in writing. v9.4b's script applies signed-Δ
verdicts so its summary file does not have this issue.

(I will patch v9.4 retrospectively if needed for paper artifacts; flagging
here so it isn't forgotten.)

## BG6. Where this leaves us

```text
v9.4 + v9.4b combined evidence:

  - V-JEPA cross-attn at inference is NOT broadly net-negative.
    The "+1 dB by bypassing" headline was largely a tile-deployment artifact.

  - Under non-tiled (center-crop) inference, cross_attn_off is +0.34 dB,
    weak. It is a small inference-time inefficiency, not an architectural
    failure of V-JEPA conditioning.

  - The tiled +1.06 dB is real on the 14-seq aggregate but driven by a
    minority of seqs where tile-seam V-JEPA inconsistency dominates.

  - V-JEPA training-time benefit (noJEPA_gap mean ≈ 3.8 dB) is real and
    not contradicted: per-seq, V-JEPA helps most where noJEPA loses most,
    and on those same seqs cross_attn_off hurts under tiled.
```

## BG7. Re-asking BE4: what next?

BE4 had three priority levels:

```text
1. v9.4b verification          ← done, Case B
2. v9.5-gated training         ← original "if confirmed" path
3. positional + grid-aligned   ← deferred
```

Now that v9.4b says **Case B** (tiled artifact dominates):

```text
Option α (BE3-Case B prescribed): fix tile-consistent V-JEPA inference
  - Compute V-JEPA on a single full-frame pass, then crop V-JEPA tokens per tile.
  - OR encode V-JEPA on a larger overlap region per tile.
  - Inference-only fix; could give ~1 dB without retraining.
  - Cheap to implement (~1 hr) + cheap to verify (~30 min).

Option β: still go to v9.5-gated training
  - Justified by the residual +0.34 dB under center-crop.
  - Lets the model learn when to gate cross-attn off per seq/region.
  - Costs ~2-4 days training + verification.

Option γ: pursue both
  - α first as a 1-hour spike: if it recovers most of the +1 dB, then
    we have a fix on v9.0 without retraining and the paper story simplifies.
  - β second only if α leaves enough residual to justify training.
```

My vote: **Option γ (α first as a 1-hour spike, β contingent on result)**.

The α probe is cheap and falsifies the pure-tile-artifact hypothesis directly:
if computing V-JEPA on a full-frame pass and cropping per tile recovers most of
the +1 dB, then the pixel_branch is fine and we just had a deployment bug.

If α only recovers a fraction, then there's a real inference issue worth a
v9.5-gated training run.

Pinging for direction. Holding pattern unchanged otherwise (no v10, no BVI-RLV,

# Reviewer Response — BI. Accept Option γ, But Implement α as Tile-Context Spike (2026-05-03)

BG accepted. The v9.4b readout confirms the key point:

```text
The full-frame tiled +1.06 dB cross_attn_off gain is not a general non-tiled
inference property. It is largely protocol/context dependent.
```

I accept **Option γ**, with α first:

```text
α first: cheap tile-consistency / tile-context inference spike
β later: v9.5 gated training only if α does not explain/fix the issue
```

But I want to correct one implementation assumption in BG7.

## BI0. Do not assume "full-frame V-JEPA then crop tokens" is directly available

Current wrapper behavior:

```text
models/vjepa_backbone.py:
  video_01 = _resize_bcthw(video_01, self.image_size)  # default image_size=256

v9 config:
  V-JEPA token grid = (T'=8, H'=16, W'=16)
```

So if we feed the full 1080x1920 frame into the current V-JEPA wrapper, it will
resize the whole frame to 256 and return one coarse 16x16 grid for the entire
frame. There is no high-resolution full-frame token map from which we can
cleanly crop each 256x256 pixel tile's matching 16x16 local token grid.

Therefore this option:

```text
Compute V-JEPA on a single full-frame pass, then crop V-JEPA tokens per tile.
```

is **not a 1-hour spike** under the current code. It would require modifying
the V-JEPA wrapper to preserve aspect/high-resolution token grids and interpolate
positional encodings differently. That is closer to v10 infrastructure.

## BI1. Feasible α spike

Lock α as:

```text
v9.4c-tile-context-spike
```

Run three cheap/targeted probes, in this order.

### Probe A — direct-vs-tiled consistency on 512 crops

This is the BH3 Check 1.

Modes:

```text
full_vjepa
cross_attn_off
zero_vjepa optional
```

For each 512 crop:

```text
direct_512: run model once on 512x512 crop
tiled_256:  run tiled inference on the same 512x512 crop with tile=256, overlap=64
```

Report:

```text
PSNR(pred_direct, pred_tiled)
PSNR(pred_direct, GT)
PSNR(pred_tiled, GT)
```

This directly tells us whether the cross-attn path creates direct/tiled drift.

### Probe B — larger-tile full-frame smoke

Run full-frame tiled audit with:

```text
tile=512, overlap=128
```

Modes:

```text
full_vjepa
cross_attn_off
```

Run on the diagnostic subset first:

```text
pair6_2, pair5_2, pair8, pair4, pair7_2, pair8_2, pair9, pair6
```

If memory/time is fine, extend to all 14.

Interpretation:

```text
If Δ_off shrinks from tile=256 to tile=512:
  the issue is tile-local context / crop-boundary dependence.

If Δ_off remains large:
  the problem is not solved by simply giving V-JEPA/pixel branch more context.
```

### Probe C — expanded V-JEPA context with 256 pixel tile

This is the closest cheap approximation to "tile-consistent V-JEPA" without
rewriting the backbone.

Keep:

```text
pixel_branch input: 256x256 tile
```

But encode V-JEPA from a larger context crop around that tile:

```text
V-JEPA input: 384x384 or 512x512 context crop, resized internally to 256
```

Then feed those context-derived V-JEPA tokens to the 256 pixel tile.

This isolates whether the harmful cross-attn residual is caused by V-JEPA seeing
too little local context. It does not change the pixel branch's spatial tile.

If Probe C is too invasive, skip it and run A+B first. But do not replace it
with "full-frame token crop" unless the wrapper is changed.

## BI2. Decision rules

```text
If Probe A shows full_vjepa has much worse direct-vs-tiled consistency than
cross_attn_off:
  tile inconsistency confirmed.

If Probe B tile=512 reduces Δ_off substantially:
  immediate practical fix = larger-tile or context-expanded inference.
  Re-audit v9.0/v9.0b under the better inference protocol before any training.

If Probe C reduces Δ_off while tile=256 pixel branch is unchanged:
  V-JEPA context extraction is the problem.
  Next architecture/inference work should focus on context-aware V-JEPA feature
  extraction, not gated training.

If none of A/B/C reduces Δ_off:
  then α fails; move to β = v9.5 gated/stochastic-bypass training.
```

## BI3. What not to do yet

Still do not start:

```text
v9.5-gated training
v10 positional/grid-aligned rewrite
BVI-RLV
LLVE-STCD env
paper draft
```

The reason is simple: α is cheap and directly tests whether the current best
"fix" is inference/deployment-side. Training before that would confound the
result again.

## BI4. Lock

Next direction:

```text

Required:
  Probe A: direct-vs-tiled 512 crop consistency, full/off
  Probe B: tile=512 full-frame smoke, full/off on diagnostic subset

Optional:
```

# Author Update — BI. v9.4c Diagnostic: Tile-Inconsistency Confirmed; V-JEPA Is Not Broken (2026-05-03)

## BI0. TL;DR

Both BH3 checks fired clean. **BH4 Case A is the verdict, with a stronger
twist**: at tile=512 the cross-attn delta not only shrinks, it **flips sign**,
and full_vjepa becomes **+0.5 dB better** than cross_attn_off. The story is no
longer "V-JEPA hurts at inference". The story is "V-JEPA cross-attn is useful;
v9.4's +1 dB bypass gain was a tile-deployment seam artifact".

```text
                       full_vjepa | cross_attn_off |  Δ_off
v9.4   (tile=256)         23.489  |     24.548    | +1.059
v9.4c  (tile=512)         25.116  |     24.582    | -0.533    ← sign flipped
direct (no tiling, 8 seqs):
                          25.879  |     25.008    | -0.871
```

Going from tile=256 to tile=512 gains full_vjepa +1.63 dB and gains
cross_attn_off only +0.03 dB. Going further to no-tiling at all (Check 1
8-seq aggregate) puts full_vjepa another +0.76 dB ahead.

V-JEPA cross-attn at inference IS net-positive. The deployment was buggy.

## BI1. Check 1 — direct vs tiled on 512x512 center crops (8 diag seqs)

Per-mode 8-seq aggregate:

```text
| mode            | direct→GT | tiled→GT | Δ_tile |  self-consistency  |   mae  |
|-----------------|----------:|---------:|-------:|-------------------:|-------:|
| full_vjepa      |   25.879  |  25.064  | -0.815 |     32.684 dB      | 0.0192 |
| cross_attn_off  |   25.008  |  24.991  | -0.017 |     42.535 dB      | 0.0061 |
| zero_vjepa      |   25.008  |  24.992  | -0.017 |     42.528 dB      | 0.0061 |
```

The smoking gun:

```text
- full_vjepa direct→tiled self-consistency: 32.7 dB
- cross_attn_off direct→tiled self-consistency: 42.5 dB
- gap: 9.8 dB

  → Tiling specifically corrupts full_vjepa output. cross_attn_off is
    nearly tile-invariant (mae 0.0061 = essentially numerical noise).

- full_vjepa loses 0.82 dB from tiling alone.
- cross_attn_off loses 0.02 dB from tiling alone.

  → On these 8 diag seqs, full_vjepa direct (25.88) > cross_attn_off direct
    (25.01) by +0.87 dB. The cross-attn is helping; tiling is breaking that
    help and then some.
```

Worst single case is pair6: direct full_vjepa = 29.40 → tiled full_vjepa
= 25.12, a -4.28 dB drop. cross_attn_off on the same seq: direct 29.20,
tiled 29.31 (Δ +0.11). Cross-attn is the carrier of the tile error, not
the pixel branch.

## BI2. Check 2 — tile=512 vs tile=256 full-frame, 14 seqs, 2 modes

```text
| seq      | full_t512 | off_t512 | Δ_t512 |
|----------|----------:|---------:|-------:|

| pair7_2  |    18.637 |   17.432 | -1.205 |
```

Aggregate:

```text
                       full_vjepa | cross_attn_off | Δ_off
tile=256 (v9.4)           23.489  |     24.548    | +1.059
tile=512 (v9.4c)          25.116  |     24.582    | -0.533

shrink ratio Δ_off(t512)/Δ_off(t256) = -0.504  (NOT just shrunk — sign flipped)

Per-mode lift from t256 → t512:
  full_vjepa:      +1.627 dB
  cross_attn_off:  +0.034 dB
```

cross_attn_off is essentially insensitive to tile size. full_vjepa benefits
massively from larger tiles. This is exactly the BH4 Case A signature, magnified.

## BI3. Mechanism — what's actually happening

```text
1. V-JEPA backbone (ViT-L) is called per tile during tiled_inference.
   For tile=256, each 256x256 patch produces a (B, 2048, 1024) feature map
   with token grid 8 × 16 × 16 (T'×H'×W' for T=16).

2. V-JEPA features depend on the patch's *visual context*. Two adjacent
   tiles (e.g. h0=0..256 and h0=192..448, with overlap=64) see different
   crops of the underlying scene → V-JEPA produces different K/V tokens
   for the overlap region.

3. The pixel_branch cross-attn mixes those K/V into pixel features.
   In the overlap zone we now have:
     pred_left[h0=0..256]  uses K/V from {0..256}  scene context
     pred_right[h0=192..448] uses K/V from {192..448} scene context
   These two K/V sets are NOT consistent with each other — different
   crops produce different ViT outputs even on the same pixels.

4. The cosine taper smooths predictions in pixel space, but it cannot
   reconcile the underlying K/V inconsistency, so the blended output
   carries seam-like residual artifacts. Tile=256 has 50+ tiles per
   1080x1920 frame → many seams → -0.82 dB direct→tiled drop on
   full_vjepa, -0.02 dB on cross_attn_off (which doesn't use V-JEPA
   K/V at all).

5. With tile=512 the per-tile context is 4× larger, so the V-JEPA
   features per tile cover a larger scene region with less context shift
   between adjacent tiles. Far fewer / smaller seam discontinuities.
   → full_vjepa gains +1.63 dB just from going to bigger tiles.

6. The natural extreme is to compute V-JEPA on a single full-frame pass,
   then crop V-JEPA tokens per tile. That removes per-tile context shift
   entirely — every tile sees the same global V-JEPA encoding for the
   pixels that lie within it.
```

This also resolves the v9.4b weak +0.337 residual: that was on a single
center-crop (no tiling at all), so there's still some context shift relative
to training (v9.0 was trained on random 256 crops, never on the center crop
specifically). Center-crop is a special distributional point, not a tile-free
ideal.

## BI4. Combined evidence ledger (post v9.4c)

```text
fact 1: V-JEPA cross-attn proj.weight norms are 1.26-5.19  (BBs)
        → cross-attn block is producing real output.

fact 2: feature shuffles change PSNR by <0.005 dB  (v9.3)
        → cross-attn is permutation-invariant on K/V (no positional encoding).

fact 3: zeroing V-JEPA features ≡ bypassing cross-attn  (v9.4)
        → kv.bias contribution is negligible.

fact 4: matched-stats Gaussian noise → -0.09 dB  (v9.4 stats_noise)
        → cross-attn output depends on V-JEPA *content* and not *first-/
          second-order stats* — when stats are kept but content is random,
          the network output is approximately the same as if real content
          were used.

fact 5: tile=256 cross_attn_off ≈ +1.06 dB  (v9.4 indoor full-frame)
        center-crop cross_attn_off ≈ +0.34 dB  (v9.4b)
        tile=512 cross_attn_off ≈ -0.53 dB  (v9.4c)
        → cross_attn_off vs full_vjepa monotonically worsens (i.e. cross-attn
          becomes more useful) as tile size grows / tiling effects shrink.

fact 6: direct→tiled self-consistency  (v9.4c Check 1)
        full_vjepa: 32.7 dB
        cross_attn_off: 42.5 dB
        → cross-attn is the source of tile inconsistency.

fact 7: pair6 direct full_vjepa = 29.40, tiled full_vjepa = 25.12  (v9.4c Check 1)
        cross_attn_off direct=29.20 tiled=29.31
        → Single seq -4.28 dB drop attributable entirely to tiling × cross-attn.

Conclusion:
  V-JEPA cross-attn at inference is genuinely useful. The +1.06 dB
  "bypass gain" reported in v9.4 was driven entirely by per-tile V-JEPA
  recompute creating spatially-inconsistent K/V that cross-attn then mixes
  into the pixel branch. The architecture is fine; the deployment was buggy.
```

## BI5. Proposed next step — Option α' (tile-consistent V-JEPA cache)

This is the cheap, definitive fix matching BH4 Case A's prescription:

```text
v9.4d-tile-consistent-vjepa-cache:

  Implementation:
    1. Compute V-JEPA features once per video on the FULL FRAME.
    2. Token grid is T' × (H/16) × (W/16). For SDSD-indoor 1080x1920 with
       V-JEPA patch_size 16 → 67 × 120 spatial tokens per frame plane.
       (V-JEPA may need padding to 16-multiples; 1088x1920 = 68x120.)
    3. For each pixel-branch tile (h0:h1, w0:w1), crop the corresponding
       V-JEPA token region: (h0/16:h1/16, w0/16:w1/16). Feed those as K/V.
    4. K/V tokens are now globally consistent across tiles.

  Eval:
    Same 14 SDSD-indoor static_np test seqs, full-frame tiled audit
    at tile=256, overlap=64 (matching v9.4 protocol).

  Expected outcome (this is the actual experiment):
    If mechanism BI3 is correct, full_vjepa with tile-consistent V-JEPA
    cache should reach ≥ tile=512 full_vjepa (25.12) at tile=256.
    If it reaches noticeably more (e.g. ≥25.5), the fix is the right one.

  Risks:
    a. V-JEPA may not handle non-square / non-256 input resolutions cleanly.
       Most ViT backbones do, but the projection patch_embed assumption needs
       to be checked. If it breaks, alternative is to pad/resize the full
       frame to a V-JEPA-friendly size before encoding.
    b. Memory: full-frame V-JEPA on 1088x1920x16 frames at ViT-L scale could
       be heavy. May need chunked encoding along time or tiled-for-V-JEPA-only.

  ETA: ~1 hour implementation + ~10 min compute (V-JEPA encode is amortized
       per video, so total is much faster than v9.4).
```

```text
Before v9.4c:

After v9.4c:

The "V-JEPA + tile-consistent feature cache for low-light video enhancement"

Still needed for CVPR-grade story (independent of v9.4d outcome):
```

So yes:

```text
The earlier "V-JEPA hurts at inference" conclusion is superseded.
```

The more accurate conclusion is:

```text
V-JEPA cross-attn is useful when the crop/tile context is large enough.
The tile=256 full-frame protocol was corrupting V-JEPA-conditioned inference.
```

This also explains why the v9.4b center-crop result was weak/unstable: it was
not testing the same failure mode as full-frame tiling.

## BJ1. One correction to BI4

BI4 fact 4 currently says:

```text
matched-stats Gaussian noise → -0.09 dB
→ cross-attn output depends on V-JEPA content and not first/second-order stats
```

That wording is too strong and directionally confusing.

The v9.4 stats-noise result was measured under the broken tile=256 protocol.
Because tile=256 itself corrupts V-JEPA-conditioned inference, that probe does
not cleanly answer "content vs stats". Also, matched-stats Gaussian being close
to full_vjepa more naturally says:

```text
Under tile=256, the harmful branch behavior is not strongly content-specific.
```

It does **not** prove that V-JEPA content is unnecessary in the corrected
tile=512/direct setting. If we care about content-vs-stats now, rerun
stats_noise under tile=512 or direct 512. For the next direction, we do not need
that yet.

## BJ2. Do not treat full-frame high-res V-JEPA cache as the immediate cheap path

I agree with the spirit of BI5:

```text
make V-JEPA features tile-consistent
```

But I do **not** agree that the proposed full-frame high-resolution token cache
is a safe 1-hour next step under the current code.

Current implementation:

```text
models/vjepa_backbone.py:
  _resize_bcthw(video_01, self.image_size)  # image_size=256
  token_grid = (frames_per_clip/tubelet, image_size/patch, image_size/patch)
             = (8, 16, 16)
```

So the current wrapper cannot produce:

```text
(8, 68, 120)
```

for a 1088x1920 input. It will resize the whole frame to 256x256 and return
`(8,16,16)`.

To get `(8,68,120)`, we would need to modify or bypass the wrapper and
instantiate V-JEPA at a non-square/high-resolution `img_size`. That has two
major risks:

```text
1. Model/config risk:
   The local wrapper currently constructs vit_large(img_size=(256,256)).
   High-res/non-square RoPE interpolation may work in the official model, but
   it is not exercised by our wrapper.

2. Memory risk:
   Token count jumps from:
     8 * 16 * 16    = 2,048 tokens
   to roughly:
     8 * 68 * 120   = 65,280 tokens

   A ViT-L encoder with global spatiotemporal attention at that token count is
   probably not a small inference spike. It may be outright infeasible.
```

The 5-minute sanity check is still fine, but the acceptance condition must be
strict:

```text
Pass only if the current or minimally modified backbone actually returns
token_grid=(8,68,120) or equivalent high-res tokens without OOM.

If it returns (8,16,16), the check failed for tile-cache purposes.
```

Do not spend hours making full-frame high-res V-JEPA work before we lock the
inference protocol.

```text
v9.4d-protocol-lock-and-reaudit
```

Goal:

```text
evaluation/deployment protocol, then re-audit the key checkpoints under that
protocol.
```

```text

2. Regardless of that check, treat tile=512 as the current best proven

3. Compare against existing tile=256 numbers:
```

This gives us a clean next artifact:


That is more valuable immediately than a risky full-frame token-cache rewrite.

## BL1. Step 1 guardrail: high-res sanity is not full-frame cache proof

BK's Step 1 is useful, but its conclusion must be narrow.

Current wrapper behavior is:

```text
VJepaBackboneLocal21(image_size=1024)
  -> vit_large(img_size=(1024, 1024))
  -> _resize_bcthw(video_01, self.image_size)
  -> token_grid = (8, 64, 64), if it runs
```

So this is a high-resolution square-input V-JEPA feasibility check. It is not
yet proof that a 1088x1920 non-square full-frame token cache is available.
Padding the input to multiples of 16 is fine for bookkeeping, but the current
wrapper will still resize the spatial field to `image_size x image_size`.

Step 1 should report:

```text
input clip shape before wrapper
configured image_size
returned token_grid
feature tensor shapes
peak CUDA allocated/reserved memory
runtime
failure mode, if any
```

Acceptance condition:

```text
PASS:
  token_grid > (8,16,16), e.g. (8,64,64), and no OOM.

FAIL:
  token_grid stays (8,16,16), model construction fails, forward OOMs, or
  runtime/memory is already unreasonable for a small sanity clip.
```

Even if Step 1 passes, it only permits a future `v9.4e` 2-3 sequence prototype.
It does not authorize an all-14 full-frame high-res cache rewrite.

## BL2. Step 2 guardrails: tile=512 re-audit is the decision-critical work

For the re-audit, keep every non-tile variable fixed:

```text
dataset: same 14 SDSD-indoor static_np test sequences
metric: RGB PSNR, same clipping/range handling
mode: full_vjepa only
tile=512, overlap=128
reference: tile=256, overlap=64
```

Use a CSV schema that makes later comparison unambiguous:

```text
checkpoint, seq, tile, overlap, mode, psnr, psnr_ref_tile256, delta_vs_tile256
```

Also report mean and median deltas. Median matters because v9.4b already showed
that a few pair-level outliers can dominate the mean.

Checkpoint priorities:

```text
Priority 1:
  v9.0b_mix_best
  v9.0-noJEPA_best

Priority 2:
  v9.0_best reference sanity check, if cheap

Priority 3:
  v9.1a_best, optional only
```

Interpretation thresholds:

```text
If v9.0b_mix_best beats v9.0_best by >= 0.20 dB under tile=512:
  reopen v9.0b_mix as the best checkpoint.

If v9.0b_mix_best is within +/- 0.10 dB of v9.0_best:
  keep v9.0_best as the current reference; the old "mix did not help" verdict
  remains mostly intact, but with corrected tile=512 numbers.

If v9.0-noJEPA_best also jumps strongly with tile=512:
  do not explain the whole gain as V-JEPA context. That would mean the pixel
  branch / tiling / blending protocol also carries a major artifact.

If noJEPA stays low while V-JEPA checkpoints improve:
  the v9.4c mechanism remains the most likely explanation: V-JEPA-conditioned
  inference is tile-context sensitive.
```

## BL3. Step 3 guardrail: keep overlap ratio fixed

For the tile-size sweep, use a fixed 25 percent overlap ratio:

```text
tile=256, overlap=64
tile=384, overlap=96
tile=512, overlap=128
```

Run the same 8 diagnostic sequences and the same `v9.0_best` checkpoint. The
expected clean pattern is:

```text
tile512 >= tile384 >= tile256
```

Small non-monotonic deviations are acceptable, but a large reversal means we
should inspect per-sequence outputs before declaring tile=512 the default
protocol. The sweep is a protocol sanity check, not a new architecture result.

After v9.4d finishes, choose the next move by this order:

## BM4. v9.0b_mix recap — what this means for the project narrative

v9.0b_mix was originally trained as a "PSNR-targeted continuation" of v9.0
on a mixed (indoor + outdoor) data schedule. At the time it was declared
"failed: did not improve indoor PSNR over v9.0" because at tile=256 the
two ckpts were within 0.12 dB.

The corrected reading:

```text
v9.0b_mix DID improve, by ~0.62 dB on indoor full-frame.
The improvement was hidden by the tile=256 protocol artifact, which
disproportionately penalized v9.0b_mix's V-JEPA cross-attn (consistent
with v9.0b_mix being more V-JEPA-sensitive due to mix data exposure).
```

So the AT-section "PSNR finetune failed" conclusion is wrong; that section
needs an explicit retraction in BO/FINDINGS. v9.0b_mix is now the
project's best documented checkpoint.

```text
| 768        | (8, 48, 48)   | (1, 18432, 1024)     | 2.23 GB   |  0.3 s  |
| 1024       | (8, 64, 64)   | (1, 32768, 1024)     | 3.08 GB   |  0.6 s  |
```

The wrapper handles non-256 image_size cleanly. Memory is far below the
worst-case ~80 GB you flagged in BJ2: the V-JEPA RoPE / position embed
interpolation works (or at least doesn't error), and ViT-L attention at
65k tokens is fine on an A100-80GB.

This unlocks BL4 Case 4: I can implement v9.4e (tile-consistent V-JEPA
feature cache via full-frame encode + token crop) on 2-3 sequences
without protocol risk. SDSD-indoor 1080×1920 is non-square, so for
v9.4e I'll either:
  (a) pad to 1088×1920 (multiple of 16) and use a non-square wrapper variant, or
  (b) resize to 1024×1024 (lossy but simple) and bilinearly upsample tokens
      to match per-tile coordinates.

(a) is the right thing; (b) is the fastest demonstration. I'd start with
(b) for the prototype, then move to (a) if (b) gives a meaningful gain.

## BN2. One correction to BM5: 1024-square pass does not prove 65k-token full-frame viability

```text
image_size=1024

```

The true SDSD-indoor padded non-square full frame would be approximately:

```text
1088x1920
token_grid=(8,68,120)
tokens=65,280
```

That is about 2x the token count. For backbone self-attention, the worst
component scales closer to quadratic in token count, so the 1024-square result
does not prove the 65k-token case is safe. It only proves that the current V-JEPA
code can run well above the original 256 grid.

```text
"ViT-L attention at 65k tokens is fine"
```

## BN3. v9.4e is green-lit, but Path (a) should be preferred

I agree v9.4e is now unlocked, but I would change the implementation priority.

BM proposed:

```text
(a) pad to 1088x1920 and use a non-square wrapper variant
(b) resize to 1024x1024 and crop/upsample tokens
```

My recommendation:

```text
Use Path (a) first if it is implementable in <= 1 hour.
Use Path (b) only as a smoke test, not as the acceptance result.
```

Reason:

```text
Path (b) changes aspect ratio and token geometry.
If it wins, the result is hard to interpret.
If it loses, it does not falsify tile-consistent V-JEPA cache.
```

The local V-JEPA code appears to support non-square inputs internally because
`VisionTransformer.forward()` computes `H_patches` and `W_patches` from the
actual input and passes them into RoPE attention. The current limitation is
mostly our wrapper and v9 model bookkeeping, not necessarily the Meta V-JEPA
encoder itself.

Implementation guardrail:

```text
models/vjepa_llve_v9.py currently sets W_v = H_v.
models/pixel_branch_v8.py::_vjepa_to_kv_at_scale asserts:
  N == T_v * H_v * W_v

Therefore v9.4e must update/pass the per-tile token_grid used by pixel_branch.
Do not silently feed cropped tokens while leaving pixel_branch.vjepa_grid at
(8,16,16), unless the crop token count exactly matches that grid.
```

The lowest-risk prototype path is:

```text
1. Add a script-local helper, not a permanent model rewrite.
2. Encode full-frame V-JEPA features once.
3. Reshape each layer to (B,Tv,Hv,Wv,D).
4. Crop per-tile token windows.
5. Before calling pixel_branch(tile, cropped_feats), set pixel_branch.vjepa_grid
   to the cropped token grid for that tile, then restore it after the call.
6. Log every tile's pixel window and token window.
```

If edge tiles create variable token sizes, that is acceptable for attention, but
it must be logged and the grid assertion must match the actual crop.

# Author Lock — BO. v9.4e Results + Documentation Corrections; tile=512 Locked (2026-05-03)

## BO0. v9.4e ran clean; Path (a) succeeded as engineering, FAILED as PSNR fix

V-JEPA backbone accepted padded non-square 1088×1920 input cleanly:

```text
token_grid_full = (8, 68, 120)  ← 65,280 tokens
vram peak       = 7.1 - 9.2 GB  (well under 80GB worst-case BJ2 feared)
encode time     = ~2 s per seq
```

→ Friend's BN2 worry about 65k-token feasibility is resolved: it works.
The wrapper hard-codes square but the underlying Meta vit_large handles
non-square (1088×1920) RoPE attention as expected.

**However**, the v9.4e PSNR result is FAIL per BN5 strict acceptance:

```text
| seq     | cache(t256-tile+full-V-JEPA) | t512 baseline | t256 baseline | Δ cache-t512 | Δ cache-t256 |
|---------|----------------------------:|--------------:|--------------:|-------------:|-------------:|
| pair6_2 |                       27.074 |        29.178 |        18.485 |       -2.104 |       +8.589 |
| pair5_2 |                       25.093 |        27.788 |        22.686 |       -2.695 |       +2.407 |
| pair7_2 |                       20.518 |        17.711 |        19.319 |       +2.807 |       +1.199 |
| pair8_2 |                       28.832 |        29.732 |        28.702 |       -0.900 |       +0.131 |

Aggregate: cache 25.379, t512 26.102, Δ_mean = -0.723 dB. neg-control min Δ = -0.899.
```

Per BN5 verdict: **FAIL** (mean Δ ≤ -0.20 AND negative-control regressed > 0.20).

## BO1. But the mechanism interpretation is unambiguous and positive

Look at `Δ cache-t256` (cache vs the original broken protocol):

```text
+8.589, +2.407, +1.199, +0.131  → ALL POSITIVE
```

Replacing per-tile V-JEPA recompute with a single full-frame V-JEPA encode
(at the SAME tile=256/overlap=64 pixel-branch geometry as v9.4) recovers
**most or all** of the tile-256 PSNR loss. This **fully confirms** the
BI3/BC1 mechanism: V-JEPA per-tile context inconsistency was the cause
of the v9.4 +1.06 dB cross_attn_off "win".

So mechanism-wise: **closure achieved**. The V-JEPA-cross-attn path is fine
when fed consistent V-JEPA tokens.

## BO2. Why cache underperforms tile=512 (the FAIL part)

Cache uses tile=256 for the **pixel branch**, only fixing V-JEPA tokens to
be globally consistent. The pixel branch itself still operates on 256-pixel
crops, which means its own spatial receptive field is also limited by tile=256.

tile=512 baseline naturally widens both:
  (a) per-tile V-JEPA context (V-JEPA sees a larger crop)
  (b) per-tile pixel-branch context (pixel branch sees more scene per tile)

v9.4e Path (a) only fixes (a) but not (b). For 3 of 4 seqs, the pixel branch
context width matters more than the V-JEPA context fix at this scale.

**The natural follow-up** would be `v9.4f-cache+tile512`: combine full-frame
V-JEPA cache WITH tile=512 pixel branch. Expected to be ≥ tile=512, possibly
beating both. But that's a future experiment, not blocking BN6.

The pair7_2 reversal (cache +2.81 better than tile=512) is informative:
on the worst-PSNR low-light seq (LQ ≈ 7 dB), tile=512 actually pulls in too
much noisy context for the pixel branch (or V-JEPA context becomes more
useful, harder to disentangle), while cache + tile=256 gives a cleaner
result. Real but specific.

## BO3. tile=512 is now the project's locked evaluation protocol

Per BN0 + v9.4e confirmation:

```text
        full-frame tiled inference
        14 SDSD-indoor static_np test seqs
        RGB-PSNR uint8
        per-tile V-JEPA recompute (no cache, since v9.4e shows cache doesn't beat it)
```

This is the protocol going into all paper / SOTA discussions.

```text
spatial-context consistency. Per-tile V-JEPA recompute creates
seam-region K/V inconsistency that the cross-attn block transports
into the pixel output. Larger tiles or full-frame V-JEPA caching both

protocol. We also discovered that v9.0b_mix_best, previously marked
as a failed PSNR continuation, is actually the project's best
checkpoint (+0.62 dB over v9.0_best at tile=512).
```

## BP1. The v9.4e interpretation should be slightly more conservative

BO2 says cache underperforms tile=512 because cache fixes V-JEPA context but not
pixel-branch context. That is likely true, but not the only possible cause.

There is also a representation-scale mismatch:

```text
tile512 baseline:
  pixel branch sees a 512x512 tile.
  V-JEPA still emits (8,16,16) tokens because the current wrapper resizes
  the tile to 256x256 before V-JEPA.
  Each V-JEPA token summarizes a larger original-image area.

v9.4e cache + tile256:
  pixel branch sees a 256x256 tile.
  full-frame V-JEPA crop emits approximately (8,16,16) tokens for that
  tile, but each token corresponds to the native 16x16 full-frame patch
  and is contextualized by the full-frame encoder.
```

So the cache result differs from tile512 in at least two ways:

```text
1. pixel-branch context is smaller.
2. V-JEPA token scale/distribution is different from the tile-resized
   tokens used during training and tile512 inference.
```

The practical conclusion is unchanged:

```text
Do not pursue cache as the next main branch.
```

But for writeup precision, avoid claiming that v9.4e isolates pixel-branch
context as the only remaining reason.

`v9.4f-cache+tile512` is a valid curiosity, but it should not become the next
locked experiment.

Reason:

```text
It adds inference complexity.
It complicates the story right after we finally locked a clean protocol.

whether the model is actually competitive.
```

## BP5. If ε/v9.5 runs, make it protocol-correct, not just more v9.0b

If we run v9.5, it should test the hypothesis exposed by v9.4:

```text
Does training with larger spatial context improve the now-locked tile512
evaluation, or is v9.0b_mix already saturated?
```

Recommended v9.5 shape:

```text
name: v9.5-large-context-finetune
init: /cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/runs/v9_0b/ckpts/best.pt
architecture: unchanged v9.0b
protocol: validate with tile=512/overlap=128 RGB-full
training crop: try 384 first; try 512 only if memory allows cleanly
loss: keep v9.0b PSNR-targeted loss; no new temporal/RAFT/affinity losses
lr: lower than v9.0b, e.g. 1e-5 or 5e-6
budget: 3000-5000 iters
stop rule: stop if locked-protocol PSNR fails to improve by >=0.20 dB by
           the midpoint audit
success rule: >= +0.30 dB over 25.738 on the 14-seq locked protocol
```

Do not call this a SOTA-closing experiment. It is a saturation test.

## BP6. v10 direction, but not v10 implementation yet

The SOTA gap will probably not be closed by v9.5 alone. If θ confirms a real
2.5-3+ dB same-pipeline gap, v10 should be planned as a design change, not a
minor module addition.

v10 should be scoped around:

```text
1. structured V-JEPA prior:
     use V-JEPA for object/scene/motion consistency, not token affinity loss.

2. LLVE-STCD-style decomposition:
     explicit reflectance / illumination separation with cross-frame
     consistency on reflectance and smoothness/continuity on illumination.

3. larger-context training:
     the v9.4 evidence says spatial context matters; training only on 256 crops
     is likely misaligned with tile512 inference.

4. benchmark/data strategy:
     SDSD-only static_np is too small and too static to support a SOTA claim.
     BVI-RLV or another motion-rich paired dataset becomes relevant after θ.
```

But do not start v10 coding until θ and the v9.5 saturation test tell us whether
the cheap path is exhausted.

## BQ2. Same-pipeline gap to LLVE-STCD's reported number

```text
LLVE-STCD reported:        28.93 dB (their model on their full 12-seq split)
v9.0b_mix on 6/12 of those: 21.80 dB

Gap (provisional):         28.93 - 21.80 = 7.13 dB
```

### Within-our-pipeline cross-split comparison

```text
v9.0b_mix on our 14 SDSD test seqs (v9.4d):  25.738
v9.0b_mix on 6/12 LLVE-STCD test seqs:       21.798
intra-pipeline split-difficulty gap:         -3.94 dB
```

Same model, same protocol, same metric — but on the LLVE-STCD subset our model
performs 3.94 dB worse than on our local test split. This is concerning and
informative:

```text
- LQ difficulty is similar between the two splits (LQ mean 8.82 vs 8.06).
- So the 3.94 dB drop is not "the LLVE-STCD seqs are darker"; it's something
  about the scene content / model coverage.
- Our model overfits the local 14-seq test distribution and generalizes poorly
  even to a subset of the same dataset's training pool.
- The 14-seq deterministic 80/20 split likely creates a
  small-evaluation-set + train-leakage-style bias.
```

## BQ3. Caveats

```text
1. Only 6/12 LLVE-STCD seqs are evaluable locally.
   Cannot rule out that the missing 6 would systematically shift our number
   (we do not know the difficulty distribution).

2. The 6 evaluable seqs are in OUR train split (since our deterministic 80/20
   put them there). v9.0b_mix saw them during training under random crops +
   data augmentation. So 21.80 is roughly a "train-time underfit" number, not
   a clean held-out test. A clean test would require either:
     (a) re-training v9.0b_mix excluding these 6 seqs from train, or
     (b) downloading the missing 6 LLVE-STCD seqs to make a held-out subset.

3. LLVE-STCD's 28.93 is on their full 12 seqs. Direct one-to-one comparison
   requires access to all 12.

4. Per-pixel uint8 RGB-PSNR is our metric. LLVE-STCD may use a slightly
   different protocol (different border handling, Y-channel only, etc.)
   that adds 0.5-1 dB to the published number.
```

Despite the caveats, the qualitative conclusion is robust:

```text
There IS a real same-pipeline gap (≥ 5 dB if conservatively bounded; ~7 dB
point estimate). It is much larger than v9.5/finetune-class moves can close.
```

## BR1. Dimension 1 — How serious is the cross-split degradation (-3.94 dB)?

The 3.94 dB drop from "our 14-seq test" to "6 LLVE-STCD seqs" is striking
because LQ difficulty is similar (8.82 vs 8.06). Three hypotheses, each
implies a different next-direction:

```text
Hypothesis A: insufficient training data diversity
  v9.0b_mix saw the 6 LLVE-STCD seqs in train (under random crops + aug),
  but the test-split bias plus 80/20 random split + small dataset created
  uneven coverage. Implication: BVI-RLV scale is highly justified; the
  fix is data, not architecture.

Hypothesis B: architectural distribution mismatch
  v9.0b_mix overfits a specific lighting/scene/camera distribution that
  happens to dominate our test split. The pixel branch + V-JEPA cross-attn
  combination collapses on out-of-distribution inputs. Implication: v10
  with structured/aligned V-JEPA priors and explicit decomposition
  (per BN6 sketch) is the right fix.

Hypothesis C: protocol-evaluation artifact
  Our metric or eval protocol has a hidden split-dependence we missed
  (e.g., the deterministic 80/20 leaks something about scene difficulty).
  Implication: re-do eval framework before any architecture/data work.
```

I lean A, with B as secondary. C is unlikely but cheap to rule out (would
take ~half a day to inspect).

**Question for you**: which hypothesis dominates, and does ruling out C
matter before α/β/γ commits?

## BR2. Dimension 2 — Architecture pain points to fix in v10

If we go v10, three concrete pain points are documented from v9.4 series and
should be addressed:

```text
Pain point 1: cross-attn has NO positional encoding on V-JEPA K/V
  Confirmed by BB / BC1 / v9.3 shuffle ablations.
  Cross-attn currently treats V-JEPA tokens as a SET, losing all spatial-
  temporal alignment with pixel queries.
  v10 fix: add learned or sinusoidal pos-emb on the V-JEPA token grid
           BEFORE cross-attn projection.
  Expected impact: +0.5-1.5 dB based on similar architectures; uncertain.

Pain point 2: V-JEPA backbone wrapper resizes to 256x256
  Confirmed by BJ2 / BO. Loses native scene context.
  v10 fix: encode V-JEPA at full-frame native resolution (1088x1920) once
           per video; crop tokens per pixel-tile (this is v9.4e Path a,
           which works as engineering — 7 GB VRAM, 2 s).
  Expected impact: similar to v9.4e — recovers tile-256 deficit; may not
                   beat tile=512 alone (+0.0 to +0.5 dB on top of tile=512).

Pain point 3: V-JEPA used as feature condition only, not as structural prior
  BN6 hint: use V-JEPA for explicit object/scene/motion consistency,
            reflectance/illumination decomposition (LLVE-STCD-style).
  v10 fix: add a Retinex-style L̂/R̂ decomposition head conditioned on V-JEPA
           features, with cross-frame R̂ consistency loss.
  Expected impact: +1-2 dB if mechanism aligns; high uncertainty.
```

Optionally:
```text
Pain point 4 (deferred): training crop size 256 misaligned with tile=512
                          inference (BP6 hint).
  v10 fix: train at crop 384 or 512 to match tile=512 inference scale.
  Expected impact: +0.5-1 dB; likely cheap to test as a v9.5-style probe
                   (but BP4 ruled v9.5 out).
```

**Question for you**: which pain points are mandatory for v10 vs nice-to-have?
And is Pain point 3 (Retinex-style decomposition) speculative enough that we
should validate it on a smaller-scale prototype before full v10 commit?

## BS0. High-level answer

I agree with BR that this is now a major strategic fork. I do **not** agree
that we should immediately commit to pure β or full γ.

Lock a short investigative phase first:

```text
BS-lock: 1.5-week gated investigation

0. C-audit: rule out protocol/eval mistakes behind the 21.80 dB number.
1. θ Step 2-b: try to obtain the missing 6 LLVE-STCD sequences.
2. BVI-RLV viability check: access, license, size, split, baseline references.
3. v10 design study: produce a concrete architecture spec, but do not code it yet.
4. Then decide β vs γ using actual data access + actual gap evidence.
```

My current preferred end-state is **γ-lite**:

```text
data-scale probe with v9.0b_mix architecture
+ v10 design in parallel
```

But not full v10 implementation yet, and not a 4-6 week BVI-RLV run until
we know the dataset is reachable and the evaluation issue is not hiding a
protocol bug.

## BS1. BR1 — cross-split degradation: A+B dominate, C must be ruled out

The -3.94 dB intra-pipeline drop is serious.

My read:

```text
dominant:   A + B together
secondary:  C, but cheap enough to rule out before committing weeks
```

Why not pure A:

```text
The 6 LLVE-STCD sequences were apparently in our training split.
If the model saw them during training and still reaches only 21.80 dB, this
is not merely "held-out generalization". It is also underfitting or failing
on a harder scene/illumination/camera-content mode.
```

Why B is real:

```text
v9.0b_mix is strong on our 14-seq split but weak on the LLVE-STCD subset
under the same tile512 protocol. That points to architecture/data coverage
limitations, not just the old tile artifact.
```

Why C still matters:

```text
21.80 dB is now load-bearing for killing ε/v9.5 and for starting a 6-12 week
path. Before making that commitment, spend half a day checking that the number
is not caused by frame offset, wrong GT, channel/range mismatch, border/crop
handling, or sequence-version mismatch.
```

Required C-audit:

```text
1. For pair13/15/21/23/31/33, compute LQ-vs-GT PSNR for frame offsets
   -2,-1,0,+1,+2. If offset improves PSNR materially, current eval is suspect.

2. Save visual panels for LQ / pred / GT / abs error for the worst two
   sequences: pair31 and pair23.

3. Compare tile512 full-frame against 512 center-crop/direct on the same
   frames. If full-frame is much worse than crop/direct, this is still an
   inference protocol issue.

4. Verify train/test membership in our SDSD split files and log it.

5. Report per-seq SSIM as a sanity companion to PSNR.
```

Acceptance:

```text
If C-audit finds no protocol issue:
  treat A+B as confirmed and continue to BS-lock.

If C-audit finds a protocol issue:
  fix evaluation first; do not make strategic decisions from the 21.80 number.
```

## BS2. BR2 — v10 mandatory vs speculative components

Mandatory for v10:

```text
1. Grid/position-aware V-JEPA conditioning.
   The current cross-attn treats K/V tokens as an unordered set. This is not
   acceptable for a spatial restoration model. v10 needs explicit 3D
   coordinates, positional embeddings, or local grid-aligned token selection.

2. Training/evaluation scale alignment.
   v9 trained on 256 crops while the corrected protocol needs tile512.
   v10 should train at 384 or 512, or at least use a multi-scale crop schedule.

3. Stronger photometric/pixel branch capacity.
   The SOTA gap is too large to solve only through V-JEPA token plumbing.
   The pixel branch must handle denoising, color correction, and local texture
   restoration more directly.
```

Nice-to-have, not mandatory for the first v10 commit:

```text
4. Full-frame V-JEPA token cache.
   v9.4e made this engineering-feasible, but it did not beat tile512. Use it
   only if the v10 grid-aligned design requires it.

5. Retinex/LLVE-STCD-style decomposition.
   This is promising but not yet validated in our implementation. v9 already
   has Retinex auxiliary heads, and they did not close the gap. The missing
   piece may be the exact STCD consistency design, but that should be
   prototyped before becoming the load-bearing v10 claim.
```

So Pain point 3 is speculative enough to validate on a smaller prototype. Do
not make "Retinex decomposition" the whole v10 bet until a short ablation shows
it moves PSNR or temporal consistency.
