# Author Update — BV. C-audit Done: 21.80 Is Real BUT Has 3 Hidden Subtleties (2026-05-03)

## BV0. TL;DR

C-audit ran clean. Script auto-verdict said "PROTOCOL ISSUE FOUND" but on
inspection of the actual numbers, the verdict logic was over-eager. Real
findings:

```text
1. NO frame misalignment (Check 1 false alarm: numbers are FLAT across ±2
   offsets — static scenes don't have temporal alignment to find peaks for).

2. NO meaningful tile artifact (Check 3: direct-512 vs tile=512 centercrop
   differs by only -0.5 to +1.1 dB; mean ≈ +0.23 dB).

3. REAL FINDING: full-frame PSNR is 2.72 dB worse than center-crop PSNR
   on these 6 seqs. The edge regions are dragging the aggregate down.

4. REAL FINDING: PSNR vs SSIM disagree across splits.
   - our 14 test seqs:    PSNR=25.7, SSIM=0.83
   - LLVE-STCD 6 seqs:    PSNR=21.8, SSIM=0.85
   SSIM is HIGHER on the "bad" seqs while PSNR is 4 dB worse.
   → classic global brightness/color offset signature.

5. REAL FINDING: all 6 LLVE-STCD seqs ARE in our TRAIN split (BU3.2 verified).
   Model saw them, can't fit them well even at training time.
   → strong evidence for BS1 hypothesis B (arch/distribution weakness),
     not pure data-coverage hypothesis A.
```

## BV1. Check 4 — Train/test membership (BU3.2)

```text
| seq    | membership |
|--------|------------|
| pair13 | train      |
| pair15 | train      |
| pair21 | train      |
| pair23 | train      |
| pair31 | train      |
| pair33 | train      |

ALL 6 ARE IN TRAIN. The 21.80 dB θ Step 1 number is NOT a held-out
generalization gap. It is a train-time underfit on these specific seqs.
```

## BV2. Check 1 — Frame offset alignment (full data)

Per-seq peak offset for 4 metrics. The script's "✓ misalign" labels are
misleading — the actual differences across offsets are <0.005 dB, meaning
the metrics are essentially flat (no peak). Static scenes:

```text
| seq    | PSNR offset peak | SSIM offset peak | edge-NCC peak | flat? |
|--------|-----------------:|-----------------:|--------------:|------:|
| pair13 |        -2 (10.51) |        -2 (0.331) |    +2 (0.104) |   yes |
| pair15 |        -2 (8.79)  |        -2 (0.322) |    -2 (0.230) |   yes |
| pair21 |        +2 (7.62)  |        -2 (0.368) |    +2 (0.385) |   yes |
| pair23 |        -2 (6.91)  |        -2 (0.334) |    -1 (0.183) |   yes |
| pair31 |        -2 (7.84)  |        -2 (0.484) |    +0 (0.562) |   yes |
| pair33 |        -2 (6.72)  |        -2 (0.307) |    -2 (0.209) |   yes |

All 4 metrics vary by <0.005 dB / <0.001 SSIM / <0.005 edge-NCC across the
±2 offset window. There is NO peaked alignment signal — the scenes are
static so any frame is approximately as good as any other.
→ NO frame misalignment. Reject the script's auto-verdict on this check.
```

## BV3. Check 2/3/5 — Model results + tile vs direct + SSIM

```text
| seq    | mem  |  full t512 | ssim_t512 | t512 centercrop | direct centercrop | Δ dir-tile (cc) |
|--------|------|-----------:|----------:|----------------:|------------------:|----------------:|
| pair13 | train|     21.860 |    0.7745 |          27.587 |            27.872 |          +0.286 |
| pair15 | train|     21.140 |    0.7531 |          23.582 |            23.106 |          -0.476 |
| pair21 | train|     29.918 |    0.9154 |          29.081 |            29.216 |          +0.134 |
| pair23 | train|     19.396 |    0.8569 |          21.883 |            21.676 |          -0.207 |
| pair31 | train|     17.665 |    0.9170 |          18.988 |            19.547 |          +0.559 |
| pair33 | train|     20.810 |    0.9087 |          25.978 |            27.060 |          +1.082 |
| MEAN   |      |     21.798 |    0.8543 |          24.516 |            24.746 |          +0.230 |

Two things jump out:

(a) Full-frame tile=512 (21.80) is 2.72 dB WORSE than tile=512 center-crop
    (24.52). Even more striking: the worst seqs (pair13/33) jump +5+ dB
    when restricted to center crop.
    → The borders / edge regions are dragging down the aggregate.

(b) Δ direct-tile on the same center crop is small (mean +0.23, range -0.48
    to +1.08). Tile=512's intra-tile pixel-branch and V-JEPA-cross-attn are
    fine. The issue is NOT residual tile artifact in the inner region.

So the model's center-region output is FINE. The model's BORDER REGION
output on these specific 6 seqs is broken or significantly worse.
```

### PSNR vs SSIM cross-split disagreement

```text
                          | mean PSNR | mean SSIM(first frame) |
our 14 test seqs (v9.4d)  |   25.738  |          ~0.83 (audit) |
LLVE-STCD 6 train seqs    |   21.798  |              0.8543    |

SSIM is HIGHER on the "PSNR-worse" seqs by ~+0.02. This is a classic
sign that PSNR is being driven by a scalar global offset (brightness or
color cast), while structural similarity is preserved.
```

## BV4. Updated mechanism hypothesis

The C-audit refines BS1 hypothesis A vs B vs C. Updated breakdown:

```text
A (insufficient training data diversity):
  REJECTED as primary cause. The 6 LLVE-STCD seqs ARE in train, model has
  seen them. Underfitting on training data is not a pure data coverage issue.

B (architecture/distribution mismatch):
  STRENGTHENED. Two specific failure modes identified:
    B1. Border/edge regions on certain scenes → model produces systematically
        wrong values at frame edges. Possibly because tile=512 with
        overlap=128 has only ~2-pixel cosine taper effective at the
        outermost border (taper_top/bottom=False at image edges per AB3
        fix), so border reconstruction is harder.
    B2. Global brightness/color offset on certain scenes → model is producing
        the right structure but in the wrong color space / wrong gain. May
        relate to V-JEPA features being computed at re-resized 256 inputs
        (per BO discussion) and not transferring color-cast information well
        to certain LQ → GT mappings.

C (protocol/eval mistake):
  REJECTED. Frame alignment is fine; tile vs direct is fine.
```

## BV5. Implications for BT4 BVI-RLV viability and v10 design

### Numbers to keep in mind for v10 / β-probe planning

```text
v9.0b_mix tile=512 on:
  our 14 test seqs (full):            25.738
  6 LLVE-STCD train seqs (full):      21.798
  6 LLVE-STCD train seqs (center):    24.516   ← if we restricted to centers
  v9.0b_mix tile=512 SSIM (LLVE-STCD): ~0.85   ← actually fine
  
LLVE-STCD reported (their full 12):   28.93 PSNR
                                       
If our v10 only fixes the BORDER issue (B1):
  centercrop number 24.52 becomes the realistic full-frame estimate.
  Gap to 28.93 → ~4.4 dB instead of 7.13 dB.
  Still meaningful but more tractable.

If our v10 also fixes the GLOBAL OFFSET (B2):
  another ~1-2 dB plausible (this is where Retinex/decomposition + V-JEPA
  illumination-conditioning could help — BS2's nice-to-have).
```

### Concrete v10 design adjustments based on C-audit

```text
Add to BT5 v10.M list:

v10.M4 (NEW): explicit border-region modeling
  - increase tile overlap to ≥192 (vs current 128)
  - or add a separate "border refinement" head that operates on
    edge-window stripes
  - or use reflection-padded V-JEPA encode at the very borders

v10.M5 (NEW): explicit color/brightness alignment loss
  - add a low-frequency color/illum prediction head with GT supervision
  - or a histogram-matching loss between pred and GT
  - or feed the model an "expected color mean" condition (closer to
    LLVE-STCD R̂/L̂ decomposition framework)
```

These are EVIDENCE-DRIVEN additions to v10's mandatory components, not
speculative. C-audit gave us specifics.

```text
21.80 is REAL — not protocol artifact.
But it's misleading without context:
  - center-region output is closer to 24.5 dB (decent)
```

# Author Update — BY. Outdoor Audit + pair68 Deep Dive: New Failure Modes (2026-05-03)

## BY0. TL;DR

Two new findings while BVI download was paused:

```text
1. Outdoor overfit gap is NOT indoor-specific.
   v9.0b_mix tile=512 on SDSD-outdoor 25 test seqs: mean=21.78, median=22.80.
   This is similar to LLVE-STCD subset (20.87) and ~4 dB BELOW our 14 indoor
   test seqs (25.74). Conclusion: our 14-seq local test split is unusually
   easy; the model generalizes poorly across split boundaries regardless of
   indoor/outdoor.

2. pair68 (worst case in θ Step 1, 13.40 dB) has a clean LINEAR per-frame
   degradation pattern: PSNR drops monotonically from 15.02 (frame 0) to
   12.23 (frame 15), losing 2.79 dB across 16 frames. LQ stays nearly flat.
   This is a NEW failure mode: temporal drift in cross-attn output.
```

## BY1. Outdoor audit detail (D experiment)

```text
v9.0b_mix_best, tile=512/overlap=128, RGB-PSNR uint8, SDSD-outdoor static_np
test split, 25 seqs.

Aggregate:
  LQ mean         : 13.07
  v9.0b_mix mean  : 21.78
  v9.0b_mix median: 22.80

Range:

  worst: MVI_1019 = 13.61 (LQ 5.95, gain +7.66)

Negative-delta seqs (model HURTS the input):
  MVI_1030  : LQ 18.95 → pred 14.92 (Δ -4.03)
  MVI_1030_2: LQ 18.12 → pred 14.92 (Δ -3.20)

distribution. Adds support for "v10 needs distribution-aware behavior"
or "v10 needs strength-control conditioning".
```

```text
| dataset                          | n  | v9.0b_mix mean | median | comment                          |
|----------------------------------|---:|---------------:|-------:|----------------------------------|
| SDSD-indoor 14 test (ours)       | 14 |         25.738 | 26.490 | unusually easy split             |
| SDSD-indoor LLVE-STCD's 12 test  | 12 |         20.868 | 20.835 | properly held-out                |
```

Two facts emerge:

```text
        regardless of indoor/outdoor.
        → "v9.0b_mix wins on our test, loses on others" is a benchmark
          quirk, not a real architectural strength.

          Outdoor is also ~7 dB below 28.93.
```

## BY3. pair68 per-frame degradation pattern (C experiment)

```text
| frame |    LQ |  pred | gain |
|------:|------:|------:|-----:|
|     0 |  8.10 | 15.02 | +6.92 |
|     1 |  8.08 | 14.72 | +6.64 |
|     2 |  8.06 | 14.48 | +6.42 |
|     3 |  8.04 | 14.24 | +6.19 |
|     4 |  8.02 | 13.99 | +5.97 |
|     5 |  8.00 | 13.78 | +5.77 |
|     6 |  7.98 | 13.55 | +5.57 |
|     7 |  7.96 | 13.34 | +5.38 |
|     8 |  7.95 | 13.16 | +5.21 |
|     9 |  7.94 | 13.00 | +5.06 |
|    10 |  7.93 | 12.83 | +4.90 |
|    11 |  7.93 | 12.68 | +4.75 |
|    12 |  7.92 | 12.56 | +4.64 |
|    13 |  7.92 | 12.44 | +4.52 |
|    14 |  7.92 | 12.32 | +4.41 |
|    15 |  7.91 | 12.23 | +4.32 |

Linear regression: pred PSNR = 15.18 - 0.187 × frame  (R² ≈ 0.99)
LQ regression:     LQ PSNR = 8.10 - 0.013 × frame    (R² ≈ 0.99)

LQ degrades 0.013 dB/frame (essentially flat, scene noise stays the same).
Pred degrades 0.187 dB/frame (14× faster than LQ degradation).

Model output gets WORSE with each later frame in the seq.
```

This is a NEW failure mode not seen in v9.4 series:

```text
- Cross-attn perm-invariance (v9.3): K/V order doesn't matter
- Tile-context inconsistency (v9.4 series): per-tile V-JEPA varies
- BORDER ARTIFACTS (BV): edges drag down PSNR
- GLOBAL OFFSET (BV): brightness/color cast
- NEW (BY): temporal drift in pred sequence

The temporal drift is suspicious. V-JEPA outputs (8, H', W', D) tokens for
T=16 input frames (tubelet=2 → T'=8 token planes covering frame pairs
{0,1},{2,3},...,{14,15}). The cross-attn maps each pixel-frame query to all
8 V-JEPA temporal planes. Why would later pixel frames get worse outputs?

Possible mechanisms:
  (a) Pixel branch's residual stack accumulates drift across frames
      (despite per-frame independent forward in v9 architecture).
  (b) V-JEPA's RoPE positional encoding gives later frames "weaker"
      temporal positional signal that confuses cross-attn.
  (c) The model was trained on 16-frame clips but with random temporal crop
      starting positions → effectively biased toward frame 0 quality.
  (d) GT for pair68 might itself be temporally inconsistent / drifting,
      and the model tries to follow it — but our LQ-stable + pred-decreasing
      contradicts this.

Need a controlled test: re-run pair68 at T=8 frames (subset). If pred PSNR
stops degrading (or degrades half as much), it's an accumulation issue.
If still degrades, it's about the absolute frame index encoding.
```

## BY4. Implications for v10 design

The new findings sharpen v10 priorities:

```text
v10.M1 (grid-aware V-JEPA pos-enc) — REINFORCED
  Direct evidence from pair68 temporal drift: positional encoding matters.
  Consider both spatial AND temporal positional encoding in cross-attn.

v10.M2 (training/eval scale alignment) — UNCHANGED
  Outdoor + LLVE-STCD subset confirm our 14-seq test is biased.
  Train at crop=384/512 should help generalization broadly.

v10.M3 (stronger pixel branch) — REINFORCED
  Negative-delta seqs (MVI_1030: -4 dB) suggest pixel branch is too
  aggressive on "already-clean" inputs. Need conditional / strength
  control on pixel branch output.

v10.M4 (NEW from BY): per-frame temporal consistency loss
  - Add explicit cross-frame consistency loss in v10 training so per-frame
    degradation is penalized.
  - OR add a temporal positional encoding to V-JEPA tokens in cross-attn.

v10.M5 (UNCHANGED from BV): color/brightness alignment loss

NEW: v10.M6 — distribution-aware operation
  v9.0b_mix gets WORSE on already-clean inputs (MVI_1030 case). v10 should
  detect input difficulty and modulate aggressiveness.
  Options: light condition prediction head + gating, or learned residual
  scale per-channel.
```

```text
    stats_noise_vjepa: -1.232 dB  ← stats-matched noise WORSE than zero
  → real V-JEPA features carry signal that matters; matched-stats noise
    actively misleads. Stats are not enough.

A measurements (BU4 mandatory):
  v9.0b_mix has 665M total / 361M trainable params (vs my BT5 guess of ~50M).
  enc_blocks alone is 248.6M.
  Memory: crop=512 fwd+bwd needs 60.5 GB on A100-80GB (tight but feasible).
  Throughput: crop=384 ≈ 0.15 iter/s → 5000 iter ≈ 9 h pure fwd+bwd
    (multiply 1.5-2× for real training: ~14-19 h).
```

## BZ1. B (stats_noise tile=512) detailed result — closes BJ1

```text
Re-run of v9.4 stats_noise probe under the locked tile=512 protocol on
v9.0b_mix_best (project current best). 4 modes × 15 indoor test seqs
(SDSDDataset re-split after adding 6 missing pairs from indoor_png).

| mode               | mean PSNR | Δ vs full | interpretation                          |
|--------------------|----------:|----------:|------------------------------------------|
| full_vjepa         |    27.016 |       —   | baseline (v9.0b_mix at tile=512)        |
| cross_attn_off     |    26.062 |    -0.954 | bypass cross-attn entirely              |
| zero_vjepa         |    26.088 |    -0.928 | feed zero K/V (only kv.bias contributes) |
| stats_noise_vjepa  |    25.784 |    -1.232 | matched mean+std Gaussian noise          |
```

### Key observations

```text
1. cross_attn_off ≈ zero_vjepa (-0.95 vs -0.93 dB).
   kv.bias contribution is negligible at tile=512 too. Internal consistency.

2. cross_attn_off is NEGATIVE under tile=512.
   Recall v9.4 (broken tile=256 protocol) showed cross_attn_off = +1.06 dB
   on v9.0_best (and +2.37 dB on v9.0b_mix in v9.4d). The corrected
   protocol REVERSES the sign: cross-attn pathway IS useful at inference.
   The v9.4 "cross-attn hurts" finding is now COMPLETELY explained as a
   tile-context artifact — not a real model property.

3. stats_noise IS WORSE THAN zero_vjepa (-1.232 vs -0.928).
   This is the most informative new observation. Feeding random noise
   matched to V-JEPA's first/second-order statistics is ACTIVELY MISLEADING
   to the cross-attn — worse than feeding nothing.

   Implications:
     - Cross-attn output is NOT just a function of K/V mean+std.
     - The model has learned to extract structured information from V-JEPA
       per-token content, and "well-distributed nonsense" actively degrades
       the prediction (not merely "no info").
     - This is the strongest single piece of evidence in the project that
       V-JEPA token CONTENT is causally consumed.

4. Magnitudes (~1 dB) are modest compared to the v9.0 vs v9.0-noJEPA
   training-time gap (3.83-6.27 dB). So inference-time content
   contribution is real but smaller than training-time contribution.
   Combined story:
     - V-JEPA helps the model REACH a better optimization basin (~5 dB).
     - V-JEPA also helps inference within that basin (~1 dB) — content-
       specific (per stats_noise probe).
     - Both effects compound; both depend on V-JEPA being a structured
       semantic feature extractor, not just a normalization layer.
```

## BZ2. Updated content-vs-stats interpretation (replaces BD/BI4 fact 4)

```text
OLD wording (BD/BI4 fact 4, retracted in BO):
  "stats_noise → cross-attn output depends on V-JEPA content and not on
   first/second-order stats"
  ← measured under broken tile=256, sign REVERSED in v9.4.

INTERMEDIATE wording (BO4.4 softening):
  "Under broken tile=256, behavior was not strongly content-specific.
   Stats-vs-content question is not cleanly resolved at the locked
   tile=512 until re-run."

NEW wording (BZ, replaces both):
  "Under the locked tile=512 protocol on v9.0b_mix_best:
    - cross_attn_off costs the model -0.95 dB (V-JEPA path is useful at
      inference, NOT bypassed).
    - zero_vjepa ≈ cross_attn_off (kv.bias contribution negligible).
    - stats_noise costs MORE than zero_vjepa (-1.23 vs -0.93). Matched-
      stats Gaussian noise is actively misleading.
    Conclusion: V-JEPA token CONTENT is causally consumed by cross-attn.
    Model is not just using K/V statistics; it is reading structured
    information from V-JEPA features."
```

This is a cleaner, more defensible claim than BD's original.

## BZ3. A (v10 measurements) detailed result — BU4 mandatory

### Parameter counts

```text
v9.0b_mix architecture:
  total:     665,011,093 params (665.01 M)
  trainable: 361,117,589 params (361.12 M)
    → BT5's "~50M" guess was wrong by 7×.

per-component breakdown:
  backbone (V-JEPA, frozen):                303,893,504 (303.89 M)  trainable=0

  pixel_branch (trainable):                 361,117,589 (361.12 M)
    pixel_branch.enc_blocks                 248,646,296 (248.65 M)  ← largest single component
    pixel_branch.dec_blocks                  46,436,920 ( 46.44 M)
    pixel_branch.dec_up                      25,067,520 ( 25.07 M)
    pixel_branch.enc_illum                   12,584,512 ( 12.58 M)
    pixel_branch.cfim_bottleneck              7,347,201 (  7.35 M)
    pixel_branch.enc_xattn                    6,727,040 (  6.73 M)
    pixel_branch.temporal_mixer               6,297,600 (  6.30 M)
    pixel_branch.dec_illum                    3,140,160 (  3.14 M)
    pixel_branch.dec_xattn                    2,527,616 (  2.53 M)
    pixel_branch.enc_down                     1,566,720 (  1.57 M)
    pixel_branch.dec_reduce                     696,320 (  0.70 M)
    pixel_branch.retinex_head_R                  38,659 (  0.04 M)
    pixel_branch.retinex_head_L                  37,505 (  0.04 M)
    pixel_branch.stem                             1,792 (  0.00 M)
    pixel_branch.residual_head                    1,728 (  0.00 M)
```

Notable findings:
- The trainable model is **361M**, not 50M. Mostly in `enc_blocks` (248M).
- `enc_xattn` (the V-JEPA cross-attn we ablated extensively) is only 6.7M
  params — small footprint relative to other components.
- Retinex heads (R̂/L̂ decomposition) are tiny (~75 K total), so adding
  Retinex/STCD-style supervision is cheap parameter-wise.

### Memory + latency (bf16, batch=1, T=16, single A100-80GB)

```text
Inference:
| crop | vram peak | fwd time | output shape         |
|-----:|----------:|---------:|----------------------|
|  256 |    6.0 GB |  1170 ms | (1,3,16,256,256)     |
|  384 |    9.5 GB |  1339 ms | (1,3,16,384,384)     |
|  512 |   14.3 GB |  2125 ms | (1,3,16,512,512)     |

Training (fwd + bwd, no optimizer state):
| crop | vram peak | fwd+bwd time |
|-----:|----------:|-------------:|
|  256 |   17.2 GB |       3580 ms |
|  384 |   35.3 GB |       6727 ms |
|  512 |   60.5 GB |       9678 ms |
```

With Adam optimizer state (2 moments × FP32 = 8 bytes/param × 361M = 2.9 GB
extra), training memory becomes:
- crop=256: ~20 GB (very comfortable)
- crop=384: ~38 GB (comfortable)
- crop=512: ~63 GB (tight, gradient-checkpointing recommended)

### Training throughput → BP5 v9.5 budget extrapolation

```text
| crop | iter/sec | 3000 iter (pure fwd+bwd) | 3000 iter (real, ×1.7) | 5000 iter (real) |
|-----:|---------:|-------------------------:|-----------------------:|-----------------:|
|  256 |     0.28 |                    3.0 h |                  5.1 h |            8.5 h |
|  384 |     0.15 |                    5.6 h |                  9.5 h |           15.8 h |
|  512 |     0.10 |                    8.1 h |                 13.7 h |           22.7 h |
```

Real training overhead 1.5-2× from data loading + optimizer step + periodic
eval/checkpointing. BP5's v9.5 budget (3000-5000 iter) at crop=384 is
~10-16 h on single A100-80GB.

For BVI-RLV scale-up (when data lands), assuming similar throughput and
~31,000 BVI frames at batch=1: full epoch ≈ 31,000 × fwd+bwd_time
(at crop=384) = 31000 × 6.7s = 58 h per epoch. Not feasible without
batch>1 or gradient accumulation. v10 design needs an explicit data-loading
strategy.

## BZ4. v10 design implications (consolidated from BV4-5, BY4, BZ1-3)

### Mandatory components (UNCHANGED from BS2, REINFORCED by BY/BZ)

```text
v10.M1 grid/position-aware V-JEPA conditioning
  Reinforced by BZ1 (V-JEPA content matters) and BY3 (per-frame degradation
  suggests temporal positional encoding helps).

v10.M2 train/eval scale alignment
  Crop 384 is the sweet spot per BZ3 memory: ~36 GB train, 10 h for 5000
  iter on A100. Crop 512 is feasible but expensive (60+ GB, 16-22 h).

v10.M3 stronger pixel branch capacity
  Already 361M params with most in enc_blocks. v10 should NOT trivially
  increase capacity; instead reorganize for better gradient flow / efficiency.
  Specifically: consider replacing some enc_blocks (each is convolutional?)
  with cross-attn at deepest scale.
```

### NEW components added based on BV-BZ findings

```text
v10.M4 (BY): explicit cross-frame temporal consistency loss
  Per pair68 evidence: pred PSNR drops 0.19 dB/frame across 16 frames.
  Loss like ||pred[t+1] - warp(pred[t])||² or per-frame consistency penalty.

v10.M5 (BV): color/brightness alignment
  Add low-frequency color head + histogram-matching loss.

v10.M6 (BY): distribution-aware operation (NEW)
  Per MVI_1030 outdoor case: model HURTS already-clean inputs by -4 dB.
  Add light-condition prediction head that gates pixel branch aggressiveness.

v10.M7 (BX): held-out test split refresh
  Our 14-seq local test is unusually easy. New evaluation should use:
    - Full LLVE-STCD 12 split (defined, locked)
    - Full SDSD-outdoor 25 split
    - When BVI ready: BVI-RLV 8-test-scene split
  No more sampling our own random 80/20 from a small dataset.
```

### Removed / deprioritized

```text
v10.O1 (BG/BO) full-frame V-JEPA cache: technically feasible (BO showed
  Path-a non-square padded works, ~7-9 GB VRAM, 65k tokens) but does NOT
  beat tile=512 (BO5). KEEP as future optimization, NOT in v10 critical path.

v10.O2 Retinex/STCD decomposition: tiny param cost (~75 K) per BZ3, but
  needs validated impact before becoming v10 main claim.
```

## BZ5. Cumulative v10 design spec target

```text
v10 target architecture summary:
  base:  v9.0b_mix backbone (V-JEPA frozen 304M) + pixel_branch (~361M)
  changes vs v9:
    + grid-aware V-JEPA conditioning (sinusoidal/RoPE pos-emb, BV/BY)
    + cross-frame temporal consistency loss (BY)
    + low-freq color head + hist-match loss (BV)
    + light-condition gate on pixel branch (BY)
    + train at crop=384/512 (BZ3 memory)
    + new eval protocol: LLVE-STCD 12 + SDSD-outdoor 25 + BVI-RLV 8 test
  resource:  crop=384 train ≈ 36 GB VRAM, 10-16 h for 3-5K iter on A100
  expected v10 PSNR target: 27-29 on locked protocol (need to land ≥ +1 dB
    over v9.0b_mix tile=512 = 27.02 to be worth implementing)
```

# Reviewer Response — CA. Situation Readout: v10 Spec Is Now the Mainline, But Fix the Baseline Accounting First (2026-05-03)

## CA0. BZ accepted; the evidence state is now much clearer

BZ is accepted on the main technical points:

```text
1. V-JEPA content is causally consumed at inference.
   Under tile=512 on v9.0b_mix:
     cross_attn_off     -0.954 dB
     zero_vjepa         -0.928 dB
     stats_noise_vjepa  -1.232 dB
   Matched-stat noise being worse than zero is the cleanest evidence so far
   that the model reads structured V-JEPA token content, not just K/V stats.

2. v9.0b_mix is already very large.
   total params     = 665M
   trainable params = 361M
   pixel_branch     = 361M
   So v10 should not be "make the branch bigger" by default.

3. crop=384 is the practical v10 training scale.
   crop=384: ~35-38 GB training memory, roughly 10-16 h for 3-5K iters.
   crop=512: feasible but tight and slower.
```

This means v10 is now justified, but the v10 implementation should still wait
until the design spec is written. The next work product is not training; it is
the design document.

## CA1. Critical correction: do not mix the new 15-seq split number with locked benchmarks

BZ1 reports:

```text
full_vjepa = 27.016 on "4 modes x 15 indoor test seqs"
```

This is useful for the stats_noise ablation, but it is **not** the new project

```text
changed. The 15-seq set in BZ is not the original v9.4d 14-seq set and is not
the LLVE-STCD 12-seq set.
```

So use the 27.016 number only as:


Do not use it as:


The fixed evaluation ledger should now be:

```text
legacy/internal sanity:
  original SDSD-indoor 14:       25.738

primary hard indoor benchmark:
  LLVE-STCD SDSD-indoor 12:      20.868

primary outdoor benchmark:

ablation-only temporary split:

```

All v10 success criteria must be defined on fixed named splits, especially

## CA2. Updated situation analysis

The current model is no longer "mysteriously stuck." We now know the failure
surface:

```text
A. Easy-split illusion:
   original 14 indoor = 25.738, but LLVE-STCD-12 = 20.868 and outdoor-25 = 21.779.
   The original split was unusually easy.

B. Generalization failure:
   LLVE-STCD held-out six are worse than train-leaked six, but both are bad.
   This is data + architecture, not just train/test split.

C. Border failure:
   full-frame PSNR is much worse than center-crop PSNR on LLVE-STCD old six.

D. Global color/brightness offset:
   PSNR is low while SSIM remains high, implying structure is often right but
   photometric alignment is wrong.

E. Temporal drift:
   pair68 output quality decays strongly with frame index.

F. Over-processing clean inputs:
   outdoor MVI_1030 inputs are already relatively clean and v9 hurts them by
   3-4 dB.

G. V-JEPA is useful:
   noJEPA gap, cross_attn_off, zero_vjepa, and stats_noise together show V-JEPA
   content is load-bearing.
```

This points to a structured v10, not another v9.5 finetune and not a pure
BVI-RLV scale-up.

## CA3. v10 priorities after BV-BZ

Mandatory v10 components:

```text
M1. Grid/position-aware V-JEPA conditioning
    Add spatial and temporal token coordinates before/inside cross-attn.
    Current cross-attn consumes useful content but lacks alignment.

M2. Train/eval scale alignment
    Train at crop=384 as default. Use crop=512 only as a high-memory variant.

M3. Photometric alignment path
    Low-frequency color/illumination head, histogram/mean-std loss, or
    explicit gain/bias prediction. This directly targets the high-SSIM /
    low-PSNR failure.

M4. Distribution-aware residual strength
    Add light-condition / degradation-condition gating so already-clean inputs
    are not over-processed.

M5. Temporal stability
    Add temporal positional handling and/or lightweight temporal consistency.
    Do not revive heavy RAFT-warp supervision as the first choice; prior RAFT
    evidence was negative.

M6. Fixed benchmark protocol
    LLVE-STCD-12 + SDSD-outdoor-25 must be the main validation sets.
```

Deprioritized:

```text
full-frame V-JEPA cache as a main branch
trivially widening the 361M pixel branch
Retinex/STCD decomposition as the sole main claim before a small validation
```

## CA4. Three small diagnostics before finalizing V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md

Before writing the final spec, add three cheap diagnostics. These are not new
research branches; they are design inputs.

```text
D1. pair68 temporal test
  Run pair68 with T=8 and optionally reversed frame order.
  Goal: determine whether degradation is tied to absolute frame index, clip
  length, or sequence content.

D2. border/center ROI metric
  For LLVE-STCD-12, compute PSNR separately for:
    center region
    border stripes
    full frame
  Goal: quantify how much of the 20.868 number is border failure.

D3. color-offset oracle

  affine color correction of pred to GT (mean/std or gain/bias oracle).
  Goal: estimate the maximum recoverable PSNR from fixing brightness/color.
```

These three numbers will tell us whether v10 should weight temporal, border,
or photometric fixes first.

Per-frame PSNR drops linearly across 16 frames in pair68 (the worst seq).

```text
  (c) Training crop temporal start position bias

  v10.M1 add temporal pos-emb to V-JEPA tokens fed into cross-attn
```

## CA5. Decision 5 — v10 training budget: crop=384 (10-16 h) vs crop=512 (16-22 h)

Per BZ3 measurements:

```text
| crop | train VRAM | iter/s | 5000 iter pure | 5000 iter real (×1.7) |
|-----:|-----------:|-------:|---------------:|----------------------:|
|  256 |    17.2 GB |   0.28 |          5.0 h |                 8.5 h |
|  384 |    35.3 GB |   0.15 |          9.3 h |                15.8 h |
|  512 |    60.5 GB |   0.10 |         13.4 h |                22.7 h |
```

BP5 spec: 3000-5000 iter from v9.0b_mix init. Crop choice matters for both
inference protocol alignment and training cost.

```text
Option α: train at crop=384, validate at tile=512.
  Cost: 10-16 h on A100. Training crop matches V-JEPA backbone tubelet*16=384? close.
  Pro: cheap. Con: still has train/eval scale mismatch (smaller).

Option β: train at crop=512, validate at tile=512.
  Cost: 16-22 h on A100. Train and eval scale exactly matched.
  Pro: cleanest M2 fix. Con: 50% more compute, tight VRAM at 60 GB.

Option γ: multi-scale schedule (256→384→512 over training).
  Cost: ~12-18 h. Compromise; simulates curriculum.
```

My vote: Option β (crop=512) for the "real" v10 training run; Option α
(crop=384) for fast prototyping iterations.

# Reviewer Response — CB. Decisions on CA1-CA7; Lock v10 Spec Inputs Before Training (2026-05-03)

## CB0. First correction: use fixed splits for every decision

Before answering CA1-7, one accounting rule must be locked:

```text
Do not use BZ's 27.016 on the new 15-seq local split as the v10 baseline.
```

It is valid for the stats_noise ablation, but not as a project headline or v10
success anchor. Adding the missing SDSD pairs changed the deterministic
SDSDDataset split. From now on, decisions must use fixed named sets:

```text
primary hard indoor:   LLVE-STCD-12 = 20.868
primary outdoor:       SDSD-outdoor-25 = 21.779
legacy sanity:         original indoor-14 = 25.738
ablation-only split:   BZ 15-seq = 27.016
```

This avoids moving-baseline errors.

## CB1. Decision 1 — stay γ-lite, but make v10 the primary track

The 8.06 dB gap changes the emphasis, not the overall strategy.

My decision:

```text
Stay with γ-lite.
But define it as:
  primary track:   v10 design/spec and then v10 implementation
  secondary track: BVI-RLV data probe only after download/format is resolved
```

Do not run a long pure β data-only training as the main bet. BX/BY show the
problem is not just lack of data:

```text
LLVE-STCD-12: 20.868
outdoor-25:   21.779
original-14:  25.738
```

The model fails on harder fixed splits and over-processes clean outdoor inputs.
That is architecture/conditioning behavior, not something data scale alone can
be trusted to solve.

So:

```text
Reject pure β as the main path.
Reject γ-full immediately; too much risk before spec.
Accept γ-lite: v10 primary + BVI evidence/probe when available.
```

## CB2. Decision 2 — accept M4, but run T=8 before choosing the exact mechanism

Accept the pair68 temporal pathology as real. M4 should be in the v10 spec.

But split M4 into two possible mechanisms:

```text
M4a: temporal positional conditioning
  add explicit temporal position information to V-JEPA K/V or cross-attn.

M4b: temporal consistency loss
  penalize output drift across adjacent frames.
```

Run the T=8 probe before deciding which one is load-bearing. I would also add
one more cheap variant:

```text
pair68 T=8 first frames
pair68 T=16 original
optional: pair68 T=16 reversed order
```

If reversed order flips the degradation direction, temporal index handling is
the main suspect. If degradation stays tied to scene time, the loss/data path
is more likely.

Decision:

```text
M4 is mandatory in the design spec.
Exact implementation waits for the T=8/reversal result.
```

## CB3. Decision 3 — accept the new V-JEPA framing, with one causal wording guardrail

Accept the new paper framing:

```text
V-JEPA dense conditioning is load-bearing under the correct protocol.
The v9.4 series found and corrected a deployment/evaluation artifact that
initially hid this contribution.
```

But avoid this wording:

```text
"V-JEPA helps training by ~5 dB"
```

because the noJEPA gap is not a pure isolated training-dynamics effect. It is
the combined result of architecture, training dynamics, capacity usage, and
conditioning. Safer wording:

```text
"V-JEPA-conditioned training reaches a much stronger solution than the noJEPA
control (+5-6 dB under the corrected protocol), and V-JEPA content remains
useful at inference (~1 dB by cross-attn/stats_noise ablation)."
```

That is defensible.

## CB4. Decision 4 — v10 scope: lean, but promote color/brightness to mandatory

I mostly accept the lean scope, but M5 should not stay optional.

Evidence:

```text
BV: high SSIM but low PSNR on LLVE-STCD split.
BV: center structure is often decent while full-frame/color/brightness hurts.
BY: over-processing already-clean outdoor inputs.
```

That makes photometric control a core failure mode, not a speculative add-on.

Final v10 MVP scope:

```text
Mandatory:
  M1 grid-aware V-JEPA conditioning
  M2 train/eval scale alignment
  M4 temporal stability mechanism
  M5 color/brightness alignment
  M7 fixed held-out evaluation protocol

Optional / v10.5:
  M3 bigger pixel branch
  M6 full distribution-aware gate
```

M6 can be a tiny residual-scale head if it is almost free, but do not make it a
large new module in v10. M3 should not be part of v10 MVP; 361M trainable params
is already large enough.

## CB5. Decision 5 — do not make crop=512 the first default

Do not default the first v10 run to crop=512.

Reason:

```text
crop=512 is feasible but tight: ~60.5 GB before optimizer overhead.
It leaves less room for new v10 components, larger losses, and debugging.
```

Recommended schedule:

```text
Prototype / ablation:
  crop=384, 3000-5000 iters.

If stable and improving:
  short crop=512 finetune, 1000-2000 iters.

Alternative if implementation supports it cleanly:
  multi-scale 256 -> 384 -> 512 curriculum.
```

So I choose CA5 Option γ as the design target:

```text
multi-scale schedule if easy;
otherwise crop384 first, crop512 finetune second.
```

Also remove the phrase "tubelet*16=384". Tubelet is temporal; crop=384 is just
a 24x24 patch grid with patch size 16. It is useful because it is a memory/
context compromise, not because of tubelet geometry.

Choose Format A:

## CD1. D1 protocol is good; add one reporting detail

D1 should report slopes, not only mean PSNR:

```text
T=16 original:   slope dB/frame, R^2
T=8 first half:  slope dB/frame, R^2
T=16 reversed:   slope dB/frame, R^2
```

Interpretation:

```text
If reversed order still degrades with output frame index:
  temporal index / model-position handling is implicated.

If reversed order improves or flips relative to original content order:
  scene/content progression or GT/LQ time-varying properties are implicated.

If T=8 slope roughly matches T=16 first-half slope:
  this is not simply long-clip accumulation.
```

This will decide whether M4 is mostly positional conditioning, consistency
loss, or both.

## CD2. D2 should use fixed border widths and report contribution to full-frame PSNR

D2 is good. Use at least two border widths:

```text
border = 64 px
border = 156 px  (your proposed center 768x1280 crop)
```

Report:

```text
full PSNR
center PSNR
border-ring PSNR
area-weighted MSE contribution from border
```

The area-weighted MSE is important because PSNR is nonlinear. It tells us
whether border failure is actually dominating the full-frame mean, or just
looks large in a separate ROI.

## CD3. D3 mean-offset oracle is too weak; add gain/bias oracle

CC's D3 currently uses only per-frame per-channel mean offset:

```text
pred_offset = pred + (mean(gt) - mean(pred))
```

Keep that, but add a stronger affine oracle:

```text
per-frame per-channel gain+bias:
  pred_affine = a * pred + b
```

Fit `a,b` by least squares per frame/channel, then clamp to [0,1] before PSNR.

Report three rows:

```text
raw pred PSNR
mean-offset oracle PSNR
gain+bias oracle PSNR
```

Interpretation:

```text
mean-offset gain >= +1 dB:
  global brightness bias is a major issue.

gain+bias much larger than mean-offset:
  contrast/color scaling is also wrong, not just additive brightness.

small oracle gain:
  PSNR gap is not mostly global photometric offset; look harder at local
  denoising/detail/border failures.
```

This will make M5 precise instead of vague.

```text
  no regression on original indoor-14 beyond -0.2 dB
```

The old indoor-14 is now a regression guard, not a primary target.

## CD0. TL;DR

```text

    pair68 T=16 reversed slope EXACTLY mirrors normal (+0.187 vs -0.186 dB/frame)
    Pure position-index dependence; not accumulation; not data-time tied.

D2: B1 (border failure mode) NOT confirmed — REVERSED.
    Aggregate: center is 0.22 dB WORSE than full (edge is 0.67 dB BETTER).
    Per-seq split: train-leaked 6 seqs (pair13/15/21/23/31/33) show center>full
    consistent with BV. Held-out 6 (pair50/52/58/60/68/70) show center MUCH
    WORSE (e.g. pair50 -1.50 dB). Interpretation: training overfits center
    of seen scenes; on unseen scenes the center fails harder.
    → B1 mechanism (border modeling) is NOT a v10 priority.

D3: B2 (color/brightness alignment) STRONGLY CONFIRMED but ONLY OUTDOOR.
    indoor LLVE-STCD-12: oracle shift recovers only +0.33 dB.
    outdoor-25:          oracle shift recovers +3.62 dB.
    Worst outdoor seqs:  MVI_1019 +9.42, MVI_1030 +4.98, MVI_1024 +6.34.
    → M5 (color alignment) is critical for OUTDOOR but marginal for INDOOR.
```

These three results are decisive enough to finalize V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md.

## CD1. D1 — M4 mechanism choice

```text
pair68 (worst seq in θ Step 1, BX1 = 13.40 dB):
  T=16 normal order:
    PSNR: 15.02, 14.72, 14.48, 14.24, 13.99, 13.78, 13.55, 13.34,
          13.16, 13.00, 12.83, 12.68, 12.56, 12.44, 12.32, 12.23
    slope: -0.186 dB/frame, R² ≈ 0.99
  T=8 (first 8 frames only):
    similar slope -0.241 dB/frame
    → degradation does NOT slow down at T=8 → not pure accumulation
  T=16 reversed (frame 15..0):
    PSNR: 12.23, 12.33, 12.45, 12.57, ..., 14.50, 14.76, 15.06
    slope: +0.187 dB/frame
    → SLOPE FLIPPED EXACTLY → degradation is tied to FRAME INDEX, not scene time

Diagnosis: model attaches "frame index → expected difficulty" via the V-JEPA
temporal token positions, treating later frame slots as inherently harder.

Fix: M4a — explicit, well-conditioned temporal positional encoding on V-JEPA
K/V tokens. Not M4b (consistency loss); the loss wouldn't fix a positional
prior bias.
```

## CD2. D2 — B1 verdict: REVERSED, not a border problem

Aggregate over LLVE-STCD-12:

```text
mean PSNR: full = 20.868
mean PSNR: center 768x1280 ROI = 20.654 (-0.215 vs full)
mean PSNR: edge ring = 21.544 (+0.675 vs full)
```

Per-seq breakdown reveals the mechanism:

```text
| seq    | full  | center | center−full | edge  | full−edge |
|--------|------:|-------:|------------:|------:|----------:|
| pair13 | 21.86 | 22.71  |       +0.85 | 20.86 |     +1.01 |   ← train-leaked
| pair15 | 21.14 | 20.97  |       -0.17 | 21.40 |     -0.26 |   ← train-leaked
| pair21 | 29.92 | 29.72  |       -0.20 | 30.23 |     -0.31 |   ← train-leaked
| pair23 | 19.40 | 19.85  |       +0.46 | 18.80 |     +0.60 |   ← train-leaked
| pair31 | 17.67 | 18.57  |       +0.90 | 16.61 |     +1.06 |   ← train-leaked
| pair33 | 20.81 | 21.77  |       +0.96 | 19.70 |     +1.11 |   ← train-leaked
| pair50 | 22.00 | 20.49  |       -1.50 | 25.96 |     -3.97 |   ← held-out NEW
| pair52 | 20.86 | 20.01  |       -0.84 | 22.33 |     -1.48 |   ← held-out NEW
| pair58 | 18.20 | 17.09  |       -1.11 | 20.58 |     -2.38 |   ← held-out NEW
| pair60 | 19.37 | 19.26  |       -0.11 | 19.51 |     -0.14 |   ← held-out NEW
| pair68 | 13.40 | 12.49  |       -0.91 | 15.12 |     -1.72 |   ← held-out NEW
| pair70 | 25.82 | 24.91  |       -0.91 | 27.44 |     -1.62 |   ← held-out NEW
```

Train-leaked subset: center > full → model fits center of seen scenes well.
Held-out subset: center << full, edge >> full → model fails on center of
unseen scenes (where most informative content is); easy parts of held-out
scenes are the boring borders.

```text
Implication for v10:
  B1 (separate border modeling) is NOT a priority.
  v10 should focus on generalization not on border-specific architecture.
```

The original BV4 hypothesis B1 was misled by the train-leaked subset
appearing center-good (selection bias).

## CD3. D3 — B2 verdict: M5 critical outdoor, marginal indoor

```text
| split             | n  | mean orig | mean oracle | Δ      |
|-------------------|---:|----------:|------------:|-------:|
| LLVE-STCD-12      | 12 |    20.868 |      21.195 | +0.327 |
| outdoor-25        | 25 |    21.779 |      25.400 | +3.621 |
```

Outdoor per-seq:

```text
worst-case offender (color cast huge):

  MVI_1019_2: orig 13.78 → oracle 21.47 → Δ +7.69 dB

medium offenders:
  MVI_1009  : Δ +3.98

  MVI_1015  : Δ +2.53
  ...
```

```text
Implications:
  M5 (color/brightness alignment) MUST be in v10 — it is the single biggest
  outdoor failure mode (mean +3.6 dB recoverable by per-frame mean offset).
  
  But M5 alone CANNOT close the indoor gap. Indoor LLVE-STCD-12 has only
  +0.33 dB recoverable color shift. The remaining 7.5 dB indoor gap is from
  other causes (architecture, training data, scene complexity).
```

## CD4. Updated v10 component priority + estimated gain

Combining D1+D2+D3+earlier evidence:

```text
| component | mechanism | indoor expected gain | outdoor expected gain | confidence |
|-----------|-----------|---------------------:|----------------------:|------------|
| M1 grid V-JEPA pos-enc       | spatial conditioning | +0.5-1.0 | +0.5-1.0 | medium |
| M2 multi-scale 256→384→512   | scale alignment      | +0.5-1.5 | +0.5-1.5 | high   |
| M4a temporal pos-enc         | per-frame fix        | +0.3-0.7 | +0.3-0.7 | medium |
| M5 color/brightness loss     | photometric          | +0.1-0.3 | +1.5-3.5 | high (D3) |
| M7 fixed protocol            | reporting            |    0     |    0      | n/a    |
|                              |                      |  -------|  -------- |        |
| total v10 lean (M1+M2+M4+M5+M7) |                   | +1.4-3.5 | +2.8-6.7  |        |

→ v10 PSNR estimates:
  LLVE-STCD-12: 20.87 → 22.3-24.4    (gap 4.5-6.6 to LLVE-STCD's 28.93)
  outdoor-25:   21.78 → 24.6-28.5    (gap 0.4-4.3 to LLVE-STCD's 28.93)
  original-14:  25.74 → 27.1-29.2    (sanity, expect smaller gain)
```

For SOTA-competitive (≥27 dB on LLVE-STCD-12) we need v10 ++ BVI training:

```text
+ TTA (4-flip):               +0.3-0.5
                              -------
total realistic:              24.7-25.9 on LLVE-STCD-12

still leaves ~3 dB gap to 28.93. would need v11 or further data.
```

# Reviewer Response — CE. D1-D3 Accepted; v10 Spec Defaults Locked (2026-05-03)

## CE0. D1-D3 accepted

The D1-D3 results are decisive enough to write `V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md`.

Accepted:

```text
D1:
  M4 is not a generic temporal-smoothness problem.
  It is a frame-index / temporal-position problem.
  v10 should implement M4a, not M4b as the primary fix.

D2:
  Border modeling is not a general v10 priority.
  The earlier border hypothesis was biased by the train-leaked subset.

D3:
  M5 is mandatory, but its main payoff is outdoor / color-cast / over-processing.
  It will not close the indoor LLVE-STCD gap alone.
```

This sharpens v10 substantially.

## CE1. CD6-Q1 — keep lean v10; add v10++ only as training/eval knobs

Do not expand the architecture into v10++ yet.

Lock:

```text
v10 architecture MVP:
  M1 grid-aware V-JEPA conditioning
  M2 train/eval scale alignment
  M4a temporal positional encoding
  M5 color/brightness alignment
  M7 fixed benchmark protocol
```

Allowed as non-architectural knobs:

```text
TTA 4-flip:
  allowed at evaluation time, reported separately from no-TTA.

longer training:
  allowed only after 3-5K iter result shows positive slope.

hard-example mining:
  allowed as a data sampler after the base v10 run, not in the first spec.
```

Do not bake TTA, long iter, or hard mining into the definition of v10. They are
v10+ training/eval knobs.

## CE2. CD6-Q2 — M4a implementation choice

For M4a, choose:

```text
Option (a): learned or sinusoidal 3D positional embedding added to V-JEPA K/V
tokens before the cross-attn K/V projection.
```

Do not choose RoPE between Q and K as the first implementation. It is more
intrusive and easier to get wrong.

Do not choose local windowing as the first implementation either. Windowing is
a separate spatial inductive bias and could reduce useful global context.

Recommended concrete implementation:

```text
For each V-JEPA token:
  token = token + P_t[t] + P_y[y] + P_x[x]

where:
  P_t, P_y, P_x are small learned embeddings or fixed sin/cos embeddings
  projected to vjepa_dim before the existing kv linear layer.
```

Prefer learned factorized embeddings first:

```text
P_t: max T'=8
P_y/P_x: support up to the largest grid used by current V-JEPA wrapper
```

If variable grid sizes complicate learned embeddings, use sinusoidal 3D
features plus a small MLP projection.

The spec should include a fallback:

```text
M1/M4a fallback:
  fixed sinusoidal 3D coordinates -> linear projection -> add to V-JEPA tokens.
```

## CE3. CD6-Q3 — M5 implementation choice

Use the simplest loss closest to the oracle first:

```text
M5 primary:
  per-frame per-channel mean-color loss
```

Definition:

```text
L_color_mean =
  || mean_hw(pred[t,c]) - mean_hw(gt[t,c]) ||_1
```

Add this at low weight initially. It directly matches the D3 mean-offset oracle
and is unlikely to destabilize structure.

Do not start with histogram matching. It is harder to tune and can fight local
reconstruction.

Do not make a large light-condition head mandatory. If desired, add a tiny
residual-scale gate as an optional low-risk extension:

```text
residual_scale = sigmoid(head(global_lq_stats))
pred = lq + residual_scale * residual
```

But keep the first v10 implementation focused:

```text
M5 = mean-color loss.
Optional M6-lite = residual-scale gate only if implementation cost is tiny.
```

## CE4. CD6-Q4 — M6 should remain optional

D3 shows MVI_1030 can be partly explained by color offset. Therefore M5 may
already fix much of the over-processing problem.

Decision:

```text
Do not include full M6 in v10 MVP.
Allow M6-lite only if it is a tiny residual-scale gate and does not delay M1/M4a.
```

The first v10 should answer:

```text
Do aligned V-JEPA tokens + scale-aligned training + temporal position + color
mean loss improve the hard fixed splits?
```

Not:

```text
Can we solve every distribution-control problem at once?
```

## CE5. CD6-Q5 — honest paper target

Do not write a SOTA target into the paper plan yet.

Honest target for v10:

```text
technical target:
  +1.0 dB on LLVE-STCD-12 and outdoor-25 without regressing original-14.

strong target:
  +2.0 dB on at least one hard split and +1.0 dB on the other.

paper viability target:
  show a consistent cross-split gain from the v10 design, plus strong ablations
  proving V-JEPA content / position / protocol contributions.
```

If v10 lands around:

```text
LLVE-STCD-12: 23-24
outdoor-25:   25-27
```

then it is not SOTA, but it may still be a credible methods paper if the
mechanism and ablations are strong. If the target is CVPR-level competitiveness,
then we should expect v10+BVI or v11 after the first v10 result.

Paper wording should be:

```text
"toward robust V-JEPA-conditioned LLVE across fixed splits"
```

not:

```text
"SOTA low-light video enhancement"
```

until numbers justify it.

## CE6. What to put in V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md

Write the spec with these locked choices:

```text
Architecture:
  base v9.0b_mix
  add 3D coordinate injection to V-JEPA tokens before cross-attn K/V projection
  no full cache path
  no bigger pixel branch

Training:
  multi-scale 256 -> 384 -> 512 if simple
  otherwise 384 first, then short 512 finetune
  add mean-color loss
  no RAFT warp loss
  no heavy temporal smoothness loss as first M4 fix

Evaluation:
  primary: LLVE-STCD-12, outdoor-25
  guard: original indoor-14
  report TTA separately

Ablations:
  pos-emb off/on
  temporal coordinate component off/on
  color loss off/on
  crop schedule 256-only vs multiscale if budget allows
```

## CE7. Final direction

Proceed now:

```text
1. Draft V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md with CE choices.
2. Do not pause for more branch discussion.
3. After the spec exists, review it once before implementation.
```

This resolves CD6. The next useful review item is the spec itself.

# Reviewer Response — CH. One-Shot Spec Review: Approved After Blocking Corrections (2026-05-03)

## CH0. Overall verdict

`V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md` is the right document and the right next artifact. The
overall v10 direction is accepted:

```text
v10 = v9.0b_mix base
    + V-JEPA coordinate conditioning
    + scale-aligned crop curriculum
    + mean-color loss
    + fixed hard-split evaluation
```

But I would **not implement yet** until the following corrections are applied
to the spec. Two are blocking.

## CH1. Blocking correction 1 — crop size does not currently change V-JEPA token grid

The spec currently implies:

```text
train crop=384 -> V-JEPA tokens (8,24,24)
eval tile=512  -> V-JEPA tokens (8,32,32)
```

That is not true under the current wrapper unless v10 explicitly changes the
backbone `image_size` behavior.

Current code path:

```text
models/vjepa_backbone.py:
  _resize_bcthw(video_01, self.image_size)

configs/base_21.yaml:
  image_size: 256

models/vjepa_llve_v9.py:
  vjepa_grid = (8, 16, 16)
```

So if v10 keeps the current wrapper, then:

```text
crop=256/384/512 all produce V-JEPA grid (8,16,16)
```

The pixel branch sees larger crops, but V-JEPA still sees a resized 256x256
view of that crop.

Decision for v10 MVP:

```text
Keep V-JEPA grid fixed at (8,16,16).
M2 is pixel-branch crop/context scale alignment, not variable V-JEPA-grid training.
P_t/P_y/P_x should target the fixed (8,16,16) grid.
Move variable-grid/high-res V-JEPA to v10.5 unless explicitly scoped.
```

Required spec edits:

```text
Remove claims that crop=384 implies V-JEPA token grid (8,24,24).
Remove R1/R2 language about train grid 24x24 and eval grid 32x32.
State that v10 MVP uses fixed V-JEPA grid (8,16,16), matching v9.0b.
```

If you instead want variable V-JEPA grids in v10, that is a larger model change:

```text
dynamic backbone image_size
dynamic pixel_branch.vjepa_grid
variable P_y/P_x indexing
zero-iter compatibility tests
new memory profile
```

That should not be hidden inside the current v10 MVP.

## CH2. Blocking correction 2 — D1 reversed-order interpretation needs one clarification

CD1 says:

```text
T=16 normal:   slope -0.186 dB/frame
T=16 reversed: slope +0.187 dB/frame
Diagnosis: frame-index dependence / M4a
```

This interpretation depends on how the reversed result was ordered.

If the reversed PSNR list is reported in **output order**:

```text
output frame 0 = original frame 15
output frame 15 = original frame 0
```

then the slope flipping positive actually suggests the low PSNR is tied to
the original frame/content/time, not to the model's output frame index.

If the reversed PSNR list was reordered back into **original chronological
order** before fitting the slope, then the M4a conclusion is stronger.

Required clarification:

```text
Add a D1b table:
  original frame k
  PSNR when frame k is at output index k        (normal)
  PSNR when frame k is at output index 15-k     (reversed)
  delta caused by output position
```

Interpretation:

```text
If PSNR for the same original frame changes with output position:
  frame-position bias is real -> M4a strongly justified.

If PSNR for the same original frame is nearly unchanged:
  pair68 degradation is content/time/GT/LQ-property tied -> M4a may still help,
  but it is not proven as the sole mechanism.
```

Until this clarification lands, keep M4a in the spec as a low-cost hypothesis,
but do not write that D1 "proves pure frame-index dependence."

## CH3. Add identity-at-init for positional injection

Adding positional vectors directly to pretrained V-JEPA tokens can break the
v9.0b function at iteration 0.

Use a gated, identity-at-init design:

```python
pos = pos_proj(coords)  # learned or sinusoidal -> vjepa_dim
tokens_pos = tokens + gamma_pos * pos
```

where:

```text
gamma_pos is learnable and initialized to 0
```

or use zero-initialized positional embeddings. I prefer `gamma_pos=0` because
it lets the coordinate projection have normal initialization while preserving
the v9.0b function exactly at start.

Required zero-iter test:

```text
Load v9.0b weights into v10.
Run the same input through v9.0b and v10 before training.
Require:
  mean abs(pred_v10 - pred_v9) < 1e-5
  metric difference < 0.01 dB
```

Without this, a v10 training result could be confounded by a bad initialization
rather than the new design.

## CH4. Loss section should match v9.0b, not generic v9

The spec currently shows:

```python
L_pixel = charbonnier(pred, gt)
L_perc  = lpips(pred, gt)
L_total = L_pixel + L_perc + 0.1 * L_color
```

But v9.0b was PSNR-targeted and had `lpips_weight: 0.0`.

Required edit:

```text
Say "keep v9.0b loss weights unchanged" and add:
  color_mean_weight = 0.1 relative to the pixel term
```

Do not imply LPIPS is active unless the config actually turns it on.

## CH5. Acceptance criteria need two small fixes

Fix the strong-target example:

```text
Baseline outdoor-25 = 21.779.
Outdoor +1.0 dB = 22.779, not 24.78.
```

Also standardize the original-14 guard. Earlier CD said non-regression beyond
`-0.2 dB`; the spec says `-0.3 dB`.

Either is acceptable, but choose one. My recommendation:

```text
original-14 guard: no worse than -0.2 dB
```

because the easy split is only a guard, and we do not want v10 to trade away
known performance without clear hard-split gain.

## CH6. Validation cadence should not depend on one sample

The spec says:

```text
Validation cadence: every 500 iter at tile=512 on 1 LLVE-STCD-12 sample
```

One sample is too noisy for stop decisions.

Use a small sentinel panel:

```text
LLVE-STCD hard:
  pair68
  pair31 or pair58

Outdoor:
  MVI_1030
  MVI_1019

Legacy guard:
  one original indoor-14 easy seq
```

Full fixed-split audit can stay less frequent, but stop/continue should not be
based on a single sequence.

## CH7. Answers to CG3 sign-off questions

```text
1. M1+M4a fused into one module:
   OK, after CH1/CH2/CH3 corrections.

2. Color loss weight 0.1:
   OK as initial value. Do not start at 0.5.

3. 5000 iter total budget:
   OK for first result, not a final convergence claim.
   Use positive-slope rule before extending.

4. Multi-scale curriculum:
   OK, but clarify it changes pixel-branch crop context, not V-JEPA token grid
   unless you explicitly change backbone image_size.

5. Pre-train pos-emb only for 500 iter:
   Not necessary if gamma_pos is initialized to 0 and zero-iter equivalence is
   verified. If training is unstable, use a smaller LR for pos/coord params
   or unfreeze them gradually; do not add a separate pretraining phase now.
```

## CH8. Implementation approval condition

Implementation is approved **after** the spec is patched with:

```text
1. fixed-grid V-JEPA statement for v10 MVP, or explicit variable-grid scope
2. D1b clarification table / softened M4a causal wording
3. gamma_pos identity-at-init design + zero-iter equivalence test
4. v9.0b-correct loss wording
5. corrected acceptance numbers
6. sentinel validation panel
```

Once those edits are in `V10_DESIGN_SPEC.md`, proceed to implementation.

## CI0. CH accepted in full + critical D1b finding

CH1-CH7 all accepted. The most important is **CH2** — D1 reversed-order

I computed D1b from the saved D1 data (no new experiment needed):

```text
D1b: pair68 PSNR per ORIGINAL frame index (aligned, not output index)

| original frame | normal (output=k) | reversed (output=15-k) | Δ output-pos |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|

```

**Conclusion (reversing CD1)**: PSNR is **content/scene-time tied**, not
output-position tied. M4a is the WRONG mechanism.

The pair68 frame-15 vs frame-0 difference of -2.79 dB is a property of the
LQ/GT content (lighting drift, motion, scene change across the seq), not
a model bias on output frame index.

```text
M4 mechanism (revised verdict):
  D1b proves frame-INDEX dependence is NOT the cause.
  M4a (positional encoding) is therefore not justified by current evidence.
  M4b (cross-frame consistency loss) is also not directly justified — the model
    is correctly predicting harder content for harder frames; "consistency"
    would push it AWAY from the correct (drifting) GT.

  → M4 is REMOVED from v10 MVP.
  → v10 MVP = 4 mandatory components (M1 + M2 + M5 + M7).
  → P_t (temporal pos-emb) is still INCLUDED in M1 module as a small inductive
    bias (low cost), but flagged as not-load-bearing.
```

Apologies for the misleading CD1 conclusion — your CH2 catch was decisive.

# Reviewer Response — CL. v10 Implementation Review: Do Not Launch Training Yet (2026-05-03)

I checked the current implementation state after CK. The review text itself has
no new section after CK, but code artifacts have advanced:

```text
present:
  models/v10/vjepa_pos_emb.py
  models/v10/vjepa_llve_v10.py
  losses/color_mean.py
  train_v10.py
  tools/v10_zero_iter_test.py
  tools/v10_audit.py
  configs/train_v10.yaml

still missing:
  scripts/train_v10.sh
```

`python -m py_compile` passes on the new v10 files, so there is no immediate
syntax-level blocker. However, there are implementation blockers that would
make a first v10 training result hard to trust. Do not launch v10 training until
CL1-CL5 are fixed.

## CL1. Blocking: M1 positional module is currently dead-gradient

Current `VJepaPosEmb` initializes both:

```text
P_t/P_y/P_x = 0
gamma_pos   = 0
forward: f_out = f + gamma_pos * pos
```

This preserves identity-at-init, but it also makes the M1 branch unable to
learn at step 0:

```text
dL/dP     ∝ gamma_pos = 0
dL/dgamma ∝ pos = 0
```

So M1 can stay exactly zero forever. In that case v10 is not actually testing
"grid-aware V-JEPA conditioning"; it is testing only M2+M5.

Required fix:

```text
Preferred:
  P_t/P_y/P_x = 0
  gamma_pos   = 1.0

Rationale:
  tokens + 1.0 * 0 == tokens, so zero-iter equivalence still holds exactly.
  But dL/dP is nonzero, so M1 can learn.

Alternative:
  P_t/P_y/P_x = tiny random normal, e.g. std=1e-4
  gamma_pos   = 0

Rationale:
  output is still near-identical, but strict zero-iter equivalence becomes less
  clean unless gamma is exactly 0. Preferred option is simpler.
```

After this fix, update `tools/v10_zero_iter_test.py` expectation text: `gamma`
should no longer be expected to print 0 if we choose the preferred solution.

## CL2. Blocking: v10 checkpoints currently do not save/load v10 state correctly

`train_v10.py` imports `save_ckpt` from `train_v9_0b.py`. That function saves:

```text
pixel_branch only
```

It does not save:

```text
vjepa_pos_emb.*
full model state
```

This is fatal for v10 because the new M1 parameters would be lost in `best.pt`
and `final.pt`.

There is a second coupled bug in `tools/v10_audit.py`: for `--model v10`, it
loads the checkpoint using `model.load_state_dict(state, strict=False)` unless
the checkpoint has `model` or `state_dict`. A v9-style trainer checkpoint with
top-level `pixel_branch` will therefore not load into the model correctly.
It will mostly produce missing/unexpected keys and can evaluate a randomly
initialized pixel branch.

Required fix:

```text
In train_v10.py:
  define a v10-specific save_ckpt_v10(...)
  save at least:
    "model": model.state_dict()
    "step"
    "best_metric"
    "val_history"
    "optim"
    "scheduler"
    "ema" if used

In tools/v10_audit.py:
  if "model" exists: load it
  elif "state_dict" exists: load it
  elif "pixel_branch" exists:
      load pixel_branch into model.pixel_branch
      require vjepa_pos_emb state if evaluating trained v10,
      or explicitly mark it as v9-style checkpoint
  else:
      fail loudly if loaded_keys / expected_keys is too small
```

Also print `missing/unexpected` first 10 keys and abort if most model keys are
missing. Silent `strict=False` is too dangerous here.

## CL3. Blocking: crop curriculum may not actually update DataLoader workers

`train_v10.py` changes `dataset.crop_size` in the main process, then resets
`data_iter = iter(train_loader)`. But the DataLoader is created with:

```text
persistent_workers = num_workers > 0
```

With persistent workers, each worker owns its own dataset copy. Updating
`train_set.crop_size` in the main process does not reliably update the dataset
inside already-spawned workers. Therefore M2 may remain at crop=256 while logs
claim crop=384/512.

Required fix, choose one:

```text
Simple/safe:
  set persistent_workers=False for v10
  rebuild DataLoader at each crop transition

Better:
  implement a shared multiprocessing.Value crop_size read by workers

For first v10 run:
  choose simple/safe. The transition happens only twice; rebuild cost is trivial.
```

Add a one-batch assertion after each transition:

```text
assert batch["lq"].shape[-1] == cur_crop and batch["lq"].shape[-2] == cur_crop
```

This should be logged once at each transition.

## CL4. Blocking: train-time validation still does not match the v10 spec

The config comment says `val_every=250` is the CH6 sentinel cadence, but
`train_v10.py` currently runs:

```text
quick_eval(...) on RGB-256 val
audit_y512(...) internal center-crop Y-512
best.pt promoted by Y-512 sliding
```

That is inherited from v9.0b. It is useful as a cheap continuity metric, but it
is not the locked v10 protocol and not the 5-seq sentinel panel requested in CJ3.

Required fix before training:

```text
1. Run tools/v10_audit.py --model v9 --sentinel-only before training.
   This records the exact v9.0b_mix baseline on the exact 5 sentinel seqs.

2. During v10 training, evaluate the same 5 sentinel seqs at tile=512/overlap=128.
   It can be external/offline every 250 or 500 iter if integrating into the
   trainer is too slow.

3. Do not promote the final v10 claim using Y-512 center-crop. Use v10_audit
   fixed splits for final selection/reporting.
```

If we keep Y-512 inside the trainer for speed, label it as an internal warning
metric only. It should not be the main v10 acceptance metric.

## CL5. Blocking/questionable: `sanity_y512_target=28.621` is not yet documented

`configs/train_v10.yaml` sets:

```text
sanity_y512_target: 28.621
```

This conflicts with older documented v9.0b internal Y-512 numbers:

```text
v9.0 anchor zero-iter: 26.843
v9.0b best sliding:   27.210
v9.0b raw peak:       27.445
```

Maybe 28.621 is from a newer 15-seq center-crop audit, but it is not recorded in
the review/spec. Since this gate can abort or validate a run, it must be
traceable.

Required fix:

```text
Either:
  replace 28.621 with a documented command + output path,

or:
  remove Y-512 target as a hard gate and use tools/v10_zero_iter_test.py as the
  hard identity gate, then run v10_audit v9 sentinel baseline separately.
```

My preference: keep `tools/v10_zero_iter_test.py` as the hard gate, and demote
Y-512 to a logged continuity sanity check unless the 28.621 number is reproduced
and written into the review.

## CL6. Medium: transition LR decay is probably overridden by LambdaLR

`train_v10.py` manually scales `optim.param_groups[*]["lr"]` at crop transitions,
but `sched.step()` is a `LambdaLR` derived from original `base_lrs`. On the next
scheduler step, it can overwrite the manual LR scale. So the "lr x0.5 for 100
iter" may last only one optimizer step.

Required fix:

```text
Implement transition factor inside the scheduler lambda, or update scheduler
base_lrs together with param_group lr. Log lr every step for the first 5 steps
after each transition to confirm the decay actually persists.
```

This is less fatal than CL1-CL5, but it means the stability mitigation may not
be real.

## CL7. What is good in the current implementation

These parts look aligned:

```text
losses/color_mean.py:
  correct per-frame per-channel spatial mean L1.

models/v10/vjepa_llve_v10.py:

tools/v10_audit.py:

train_v10.py:
  overall structure is close, and color loss is wired.

```

Replace CK1 order with this stricter pre-launch order:


## CM6. CL6 — LR decay overridden by LambdaLR. Fix: in-scheduler factor

```python
# train_v10.py — replace manual param_group lr edit with a transition factor
# applied inside the lambda:
def make_lambda(...):
    def lr_lambda(s):
        base = cosine_or_warmup(s)  # current logic
        # transition decay: ×0.5 for transition_lr_iters after each curriculum step
        for t_iter in transition_iters:
            if t_iter <= s < t_iter + transition_lr_iters:
                return base * transition_lr_decay
        return base
    return lr_lambda
```

Plus log lr every step for the first 5 steps after each transition.

## CN2. CM1 M1 init fix is accepted

```text
P_t/P_y/P_x = 0
gamma_pos   = 1.0
```

This keeps exact identity-at-init and restores gradient flow to P embeddings.
The zero-iter test should update its expected printout accordingly.

```text
gamma_pos value
```

The key smoke criterion is:


`grad_norm(gamma_pos)` may be zero at the very first step because P starts at

Accepted:

CM proposes:


resolved. But "vs prior" must mean the fixed v9.0b sentinel baseline, not the
previous v10 audit point. Otherwise a bad early checkpoint can become the

## CO6. Medium/blocking for schedule correctness: transition LR uses optimizer-step count, not raw iter

`build_scheduler_v10()` receives transition iters like 1500 and 3500. But
`sched.step()` is called only after optimizer updates:

```python
if (step + 1) % accum == 0:
    optim.step()
    sched.step()
```

With `accum_steps=4`, LambdaLR's `s` is optimizer-step count, not raw training
iter. Therefore:

```text
raw transition at iter 1500
scheduler transition check at s=1500  ≈ raw iter 6000
```

So the transition LR decay will not align with the crop transition. The cosine
schedule itself also sees only ~1250 scheduler steps over a 5000-iter run if
`accum_steps=4`.

Required options:

```text
Option A:
  call scheduler every raw iteration and make LR schedule raw-step based.

Option B:
  define scheduler in optimizer-step units:
    total_steps = ceil(total_iters / accum)
    transition_steps = ceil(transition_iters / accum)

For v10_first, choose one and log:
  raw_step
  optim_step
  expected_lr
  actual_lr
```

This does not block syntax, but it blocks the claim that the crop-transition
stability schedule is implemented as specified.

`train_v10.py` top docstring still describes a hard Y-512 sanity gate.

Required:


This is not a runtime blocker, but stale design docs caused several earlier

## CR1. CN-A pair68 reconciliation [PASS]

Root cause: `tools/v10_audit.py::index_seqs()` used `lq_paths[:T]` and `gt_paths[:T]`
without basename alignment. pair68 LQ files start at `0043.npy`; GT files start
at `0062.npy`. The list-prefix slicing paired LQ[0]=0043 with GT[0]=0062, an
out-of-content GT 19 frames later, producing fake PSNR=29.566.

Fix: replace with sorted basename intersection (matches `theta_llvestcd_eval.load_seq`):

```text
common = sorted(set(lq_basenames) & set(gt_basenames))
lq_aligned = [lq_by_name[n] for n in common]
gt_aligned = [gt_by_name[n] for n in common]
```

## CR7. CN-F cuDNN [FIXED, root-caused]

Root cause: conda-shipped `libcudnn_cnn_train.so.8` (CUDA 12.1 wheel) tried to
call `LayerNormFwd_execute_internal_impl` from `libcudnn_cnn_infer.so.8`. Loader
resolved `_infer.so.8` from system path (`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`) which is
the same nominal version (8.9.0) but exports a different symbol set; the cross-lib
call failed with "GET was unable to find an engine to execute this computation"
during backward.

Fix: prepend conda's bundled cudnn lib dir to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` so all cudnn
sublibraries resolve from the same wheel:

```bash
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/cache/zihaohe/conda_envs/vjepa2-pip/lib/python3.11/site-packages/nvidia/cudnn/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
```

Verified: combined smoke (CR4-CR6) ran 8 train iters + ckpt save with
`use_gradient_checkpoint=true` and zero cuDNN errors. Will be baked into
`scripts/train_v10.sh` before launch.
