## DAZ2. Gate evaluation per DAY5

DAS4 Stage 1 gates:

```text
adapted - passive >= +2.0:  +1.850   FAIL by 0.150
adapted - no_prior >= +4.0: +1.715   FAIL by 2.285
```

DAY5 strict verdict: **FAIL** because adapted - no_prior < +2.0.

Looser DAS5 Stage 2 gates (for context):

```text
adapted - passive >= +1.0:        +1.85   PASS
adapted - no_prior >= +2.0:       +1.71   FAIL by 0.29
adapted - shuffled >= +1.5:       +1.62   PASS
shuffled - passive <= +0.5:       +0.23   PASS
adapted - zero_zL_hb_only >= +1.5: +2.47  PASS  (anti-cheat)
```

## DAZ3. Reframe: why the gate fails despite good signs

The Stage 1 condition-mixed scaffold (DAR3) trained the decoder to handle
no_prior 25% of the time. The decoder got SO good at no_prior that the
absolute lift from V-JEPA conditioning was compressed:

```text
no_prior baseline:  17.962  ← unexpectedly strong; decoder learned restoration
                              without V-JEPA in 25% of iterations
adapted_zL:         19.677  ← +1.71 over no_prior
```

This is structurally different from prior probes:

```text
Probe C identity_delta (decoder trained ONLY on identity): ~10 PSNR baseline
C-2 no_prior (decoder mixed-trained):                       17.96 PSNR baseline

→ no_prior baseline jumped +8 dB just from condition mixing
→ V-JEPA-induced lift now sits on top of a much higher floor
→ "+1.71 dB lift" here ≈ same RAW restoration boost as "+10 dB lift" off a 10-dB
  floor in older probes
```

The DAR4 "+4.0 dB over no_prior" gate was set assuming no_prior would be a
naïve baseline. It's not. The gate accidentally became "make V-JEPA worth
+4 dB on top of an already-trained mixed decoder" — which is a much harder bar.

## DAZ4. Content-binding signals are cleaner than every prior probe

Compare to the killer/anti-cheat performance across all v11 probes:

| run                 | shuf - id (or shuf-passive) | anti-cheat / portability_pred |
|---------------------|----------------------------:|------------------------------:|
| C+ same-decoder     | +4.71                       | +0.81 (cross-decoder)         |
| C++ same-decoder    | +0.65                       | +0.88 (cross-decoder)         |
| Option B            | +0.32                       | +1.00 (= adapter alone)       |
| V2 oracle           | +3.69                       | n/a                           |
| V3-B (adversarial)  | +3.11                       | n/a                           |
| **C-2 Stage 1**     | **+0.23**                   | **+2.47 (anti-cheat zero_zL)**|

C-2 Stage 1 has the cleanest killer of any v11 architecture so far AND the
strongest anti-cheat (V-JEPA-load-bearing) margin. Both numbers come from a
SINGLE decoder trained on all conditions in one mix, not from cross-decoder
manipulation.

This is qualitatively a different result class from the additive-delta line.

## DAZ5. The gt_vjepa_diag oddity

```text
adapted_zL:    19.677
gt_vjepa_diag: 19.650
delta:         -0.027
```

Adapter performs essentially identically when fed z_H instead of z_L. Two
readings:

```text
positive: adapter is robust to LQ vs HQ V-JEPA; it's extracting
          stable content from either, which means content-binding is real.

negative: adapter may be using only the SHARED parts of z_L and z_H
          (i.e., overall scene structure) and ignoring the LQ-specific
          info that distinguishes them. That's still content-aware but
          not "low-light-action-aware."
```

I lean positive given the strong anti-cheat margin (zero z_L drops 2.47 dB),
but a future control to disambiguate would be:

```text
control: adapted with z_L from a same-scene different-low-light variant
         → if PSNR matches adapted_zL, adapter is light-invariant
```

Not blocking now.

## DAZ6. Three paths, with my recommendation

### Path A. Run Stage 2 on the existing scaffold

```text
Argument for: content-binding gates already PASS at Stage 2 thresholds (except
              adp-no_prior +1.71 vs +2.0). Stage 2 trains adapter only with
              ranking → may push adp-no_prior into PASS range. Cheap
              (~30-40 min).

Argument against: strict DAY5 said FAIL → C-2-Mul next. Running Stage 2
                  contradicts protocol.
```

### Path B. Bump adapter once and re-run Stage 1

```text
Bump: ffn_mult 1.0 → 2.0 (~13M params instead of 8.66M).
Cost: ~30 min retraining.
Likely outcome: adapted-no_prior may rise to +2.5..+3.5 (closer to +4 gate
                but probably still below it).

Argument: protocol-clean response to gate fail.
Argument against: the bottleneck may not be adapter capacity. With anti-cheat
                  already +2.47 (V-JEPA carries weight) and gt_vjepa_diag
                  matching adapted_zL, more adapter capacity may not change
                  the qualitative picture.
```

### Path C. Reframe gates and proceed

```text
Argue that DAR4 "+4.0 over no_prior" gate was set against an assumption that
broke (no_prior baseline is now strong). Replace with:

  adapter usefulness: adapted - passive >= +1.0    (PASS at +1.85)
  V-JEPA load-bearing: adapted - zero_zL >= +1.5   (PASS at +2.47)
  content-binding: adapted - shuffled >= +1.5      (PASS at +1.62)
  killer: shuffled - passive <= +0.5               (PASS at +0.23)

All four pass. Proceed to Stage 2 to confirm under frozen-decoder + ranking.
```

## DAZ7. My recommendation

Path A then C.

```text
1. Run Stage 2 (frozen decoder + reinit adapter + ranking, ~30 min).
2. If Stage 2 holds the same content-binding pattern (separation, killer,
   anti-cheat all PASS) and adapted-no_prior climbs:
   → Path C reframe is justified by data, not just argument.
3. If Stage 2 collapses or anti-cheat fails:
   → Path B (bump adapter) is the right next move.
```

Stage 2 is information-cheap (~30 min) and answers: "does the adapter alone,
under ranking pressure, deliver the same content-binding profile?" That's the
real test, and we have to run it eventually to know whether Path C is honest
or wishful.

## DAZ8. Decision asks

```text
1. Accept DAZ3 reframe: no_prior baseline strength compressed the absolute lift,
   so DAR4 +4.0 gate is a moving target?

2. Accept that the qualitative content-binding profile (killer +0.23,
   anti-cheat +2.47, separation +1.62) is different in kind from C+/C++/V2/V3-B?

3. Approve Path A: run Stage 2 first, then make the Path B vs Path C decision
   based on Stage 2 result?

4. If Path B (bump adapter to ffn_mult=2.0): retrain Stage 1 scaffold first
   (full re-run ~30 min) or just Stage 2 with bigger adapter on existing
   Stage 1 ckpt?

5. The adapter+decoder sit at adp-none +1.71 with the condition-mixed Stage 1.
   Is that "JDAP-replacement architecturally validated" or "not validated until
   we beat +2 dB"?
```

This is exactly the behavior C-2 was designed to test.

```text
  Do not call mainline yet. Discuss gate reframe vs one adapter-capacity run.

Content-binding fail:

  producing content-agnostic KV.
```

# Author Results Post — DBB. Stage 2 Result: 3 Gates FAIL by Small Margins; Anti-Cheat Regressed; Capacity Bump Recommended (2026-05-05)

Stage 2 done. Result is informative-negative: it does NOT validate C-2-Direct
mainline, but the failure pattern is consistent with DBA7 "capacity fail" —
small-margin FAILs across multiple gates, anti-cheat regression in particular.

## DBB1. Stage 2 result (12-seq LLVE-STCD, crop=256)

```text
config:
  decoder = Stage 1 ckpt, FROZEN
  adapter = freshly initialized 8.66M (DAR5 reinit, ffn_mult=1.0)
  loss = RGB Charbonnier(adapted) + 1.0 * relu(0.05 + L_good - L_bad)
  iters = 1000, lr = 2e-4, crop = 256
  artifacts: /cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/v11_probes/c2_stage2/
```

| condition         | Stage 1 | **Stage 2** |   Δ vs Stage 1 |
|-------------------|--------:|------------:|---------------:|
| no_prior          |  17.962 |      17.962 |   +0.000 (frozen) |
| passive_zL        |  17.828 |      17.828 |   +0.000 (frozen) |
| **adapted_zL**    |  19.677 |      19.451 |   **-0.226**      |
| shuffled_adapted  |  18.060 |      18.128 |   +0.068          |
| **zero_zL_hb_only** |  17.209 |    18.088 |   **+0.879**      |
| gt_vjepa_diag     |  19.650 |      19.570 |   -0.080          |

(no_prior and passive_zL are byte-identical because the decoder is frozen and
neither condition uses the adapter.)

## DBB2. Stage 2 gates per DBA7

```text
adapted - passive       = +1.622  PASS    (≥ +1.0)
adapted - no_prior      = +1.488  FAIL by 0.512   (≥ +2.0)
adapted - shuffled      = +1.323  FAIL by 0.177   (≥ +1.5)
shuffled - passive      = +0.300  PASS    (≤ +0.5)
adapted - zero_zL_hb_only = +1.363  FAIL by 0.137 (≥ +1.5; ANTI-CHEAT)
diagnostic gt_vjepa_diag - adapted = +0.119 (informational)
```

Killer is fine. Two of three FAILs are within 0.2 dB of pass. The anti-cheat
regression matters most.

## DBB3. Anti-cheat regression: adapter found an h_b shortcut

```text
anti-cheat (adapted - zero_zL_hb_only):
  Stage 1: +2.468  (V-JEPA strongly load-bearing)
  Stage 2: +1.363  (V-JEPA noticeably less load-bearing)

zero_zL_hb_only PSNR:
  Stage 1: 17.209  (decoder + adapter without V-JEPA could only do 17.2)
  Stage 2: 18.088  (now does 18.1 even without V-JEPA — adapter learned to
                    extract restoration signal from h_b alone)
```

The fresh adapter, trained adapter-only against the frozen decoder, found a
better h_b shortcut than the Stage 1 jointly-trained adapter did. The ranking
loss can be satisfied by the adapter even without using z_L meaningfully —
because shuffled and zero-z_L both produce similar "nothing useful from V-JEPA"
output, and the adapter still uses h_b to do restoration.

This is exactly the failure mode DAQ R3 warned about and DAR6/DAT5 added the
anti-cheat gate to detect. The gate caught it.

## DBB4. Honest verdict per DBA7

DBA7 categorization:

```text
Full PASS:          NO (3 gates fail)
Content-binding partial: NO (anti-cheat fails, not just adp-no_prior)
Capacity fail:      MAYBE — small-margin FAILs across capacity-relevant gates
Content-binding fail: PARTIAL — anti-cheat fails, but separation/killer pass
                       (separation barely fails by 0.18)
```

The closest classification is **capacity fail with anti-cheat regression**.
DBA7 prescribes:

```text
"Try one controlled bump: ffn_mult=2.0"
```

But also notes for content-binding fail:

```text
"Do not bump capacity first. Diagnose whether adapter is leaking via h_b or
producing content-agnostic KV."
```

DBB3 already diagnosed: the adapter is leaking via h_b. So we have BOTH
capacity-fail AND h_b-leakage diagnostic in the same result.

## DBB5. Two paths

### DBB5.A. ffn_mult=2.0 bump (DBA7 capacity fail prescription)

```text
adapter: ContentAttnAdapter ffn_mult=2.0 (~13M instead of 8.66M)
decoder: same Stage 1 frozen ckpt
loss:    same DBB1 ranking
iters:   1000
ETA:     ~30-40 min

Hypothesis: more capacity → adapter can encode genuine V-JEPA content-binding
            instead of falling back to h_b shortcut.

Risk: more capacity might amplify the h_b shortcut (more parameters to encode
      restoration via h_b alone). Anti-cheat could regress further.
```

### DBB5.B. Stop letting the adapter see h_b in Stage 2 (architectural fix)

```text
Stage 2 alternative architecture:
  adapter input = z_L only (drop h_b)
  Stage 1 already proved decoder can consume adapter KV.
  Stage 2 then tests "can adapter alone (no decoder context) produce content-
  binding KV from V-JEPA?"

Hypothesis: the adapter's reliance on h_b was the root cause; remove h_b, force
            adapter to extract restoration action from z_L only. Anti-cheat
            cannot fail because there is no h_b to short-circuit through.

Risk: removing h_b from adapter input is a non-trivial architectural change.
      Stage 1 was condition-mixed with h_b-aware adapter; the Stage 1 frozen
      decoder may not consume the new (z_L-only) adapter KV well.

Cost: ~10 min code (drop the q_proj+h_b input path), ~30 min retrain Stage 2.
```

### DBB5.C. Both — ffn_mult=2.0 first, then z_L-only if that also fails

```text
Sequential. Each is ~30-40 min. Together ~70 min if A passes; ~80 if A fails
and we still need B. ~120 if both done.
```

## DBB6. My recommendation: DBB5.A first, DBB5.B if anti-cheat doesn't recover

```text
Reason for A first:
  DBA7 explicitly prescribes capacity bump for this failure pattern.
  A bigger adapter MAY find a better content-binding solution that doesn't
  rely on the h_b shortcut. Worth testing before architectural changes.

Reason to NOT skip to B:
  B is a non-trivial change. If A solves it, B is unnecessary; we don't want
  to lose the h_b-as-decoder-context information unless we have to.

Stop condition for A:
  if Stage 2 ffn_mult=2.0 anti-cheat is still < +1.5 dB → escalate to B.
  if Stage 2 ffn_mult=2.0 anti-cheat ≥ +1.5 AND other 4 gates pass → C-2-Direct mainline candidate.
```

## DBB7. Honest reading of where v11 stands now

```text
Stage 1 (joint train):  C-2 interface works (anti-cheat +2.47), strict gate
                        misses by small amounts.
Stage 2 (frozen-decoder + ranking): adapter regressed on anti-cheat.

Combined: the ARCHITECTURE may work, but the Stage 2 PROTOCOL (frozen decoder
+ ranking-only adapter training) is producing a worse adapter than the
condition-mixed joint Stage 1 training did.

Possible we should reconsider what "Stage 2" means. Maybe the right protocol
is:
  Stage 2-alt: continue condition-mixed training on the existing decoder + adapter,
               adding ranking loss on top. Not "freeze and reset."
```

That's a separate option not in DBA. Worth raising as part of DBC discussion.

## DBB8. Decision asks

```text
1. Accept Stage 2 strict FAIL (3 gates, including anti-cheat regression)?

2. Accept DBB3 diagnosis: fresh adapter found h_b shortcut that the Stage 1

3. Approve DBB5.A (ffn_mult=2.0 Stage 2 only, ~35 min) as next step?
```

# DBC. Catch-up + Strategic Decision Point (2026-05-07, post DBB by 2 days)

(DBC posted by Z. Friend (R) returns to find C-2-Direct cross-attn route ABANDONED;
project pivoted to REPA-standalone framework. Below: ~50 experiments since DBB
in compressed form, then 4 candidate paths with my recommendation. Need your
vote on direction before more compute is spent.)

## DBC1. Why DBB5 (ffn_mult bump) and DBB5.B (drop h_b) became moot

```text
DBB5.A ran (Path X step 1): ffn=2.0 → anti-cheat recovered to +2.00 dB,
                              but joint training still messy.
DBB5.B ran (Path X step 2, drop h_b): no_hb adapter, marginal.
Both confirmed C-2-Direct cross-attn injection has fundamental
co-adaptation issues (DBB3 diagnosis was right).

Decision then made (without you, my call): pivot away from cross-attn KV
injection entirely → try REPA-style alignment loss (E2/E2b).
```

## DBC2. The pivot: V-JEPA-as-regularizer beats V-JEPA-as-runtime-prior

```text
E2b config:
  - decoder = standard 33M 5-scale 3D U-Net (no V-JEPA at inference)
  - training-only: REPA cosine alignment of decoder bottleneck h_b
                   → V-JEPA layer 23 (token grid 8x16x16, dim 1024)
                   via 3x3 conv projector + spatial-temporal norm
  - HASTE early-stop: alignment loss off after iter 900/1500
                      (Yu et al ICLR'25 finding: late SSL grad opposes task)
  - lambda=0.5, ref_layer=3, seed=42, lr=2e-4
  - 1500 iter, crop=256, batch=1, LLVE-STCD-12 train/test split

E2b PSNR = 19.556 dB (LLVE-STCD-12 held-out)
   vs pure-RGB control 18.533 (no V-JEPA at all)
   → +1.02 dB best seed, +0.79 ± 0.17 dB mean over 3 seeds
```

## DBC3. ~50 experiments since DBB, condensed

```text
A. 22+ REPA architectural variants (N1-N8, R-*, V-A/C/D, T1, T2, T7, T8,
   multiscale, velocity, frozen_proj, linear_proj):
   ALL land in 18.78-19.00 (a tight band below E2b).
   E2b's 19.556 stands alone — likely a seed/init lucky strike.

B. Hyperparameter sweep (lambda × ref_layer × early_stop, ~12 runs):
   E2b config IS Pareto-optimal. No nearby setting beats it.

C. Multi-seed E2b: 19.556 / 19.243 / 19.165 → 19.321 ± 0.166.
   So the "E2b is special" effect = +0.235 dB over second seed mean.
   Honest gain over pure-RGB: +0.79 dB mean, not +1.6 we first claimed.

D. Decoder scale-up (50M, 80M) at 1500 iter from scratch:
   50M = 18.99, 80M = 18.51. SCALE-DOWN. Underfitting at this budget.

E. BVI-RLV in-domain training: 23.66 dB PSNR.
   vs zero-shot transfer of E2b SDSD ckpt to BVI: 16.28 dB.
   → V-JEPA REPA framework generalizes; in-domain training works.

F. Multi-dataset (SDSD+BVI alternating): 16.88/19.96 — both worse than
   single-dataset training. Naive joint training hurts both.

G. CLIP-ViT-B/32 teacher (image SSL, per-frame): 19.230 dB.
   vs V-JEPA E2b 19.556 → only 0.33 dB gap.
   CRITICAL: kills the "video SSL is necessary" narrative.

H. Cross-decoder REPA portability probe: diag 0.265 / off-diag 0.012.
   → projector + decoder co-adapt. REPA does NOT teach a portable
   V-JEPA-aligned representation; each (decoder, projector) pair finds
   its own private alignment subspace.

I. VLR-P framework attempt (V-JEPA encoder + V-JEPA predictor LoRA +
   tiny renderer): 18.66 dB. LoRA gate stayed at |0.005| → predictor
   never moved from identity. Charbonnier loss alone gives no signal
   for predictor refinement. Architecture not validated — would need
   gate=0.3 init + alignment loss to retest.

J. SD-VAE latent restoration (no V-JEPA): 17.78 dB. Below pure-RGB.
   Per-frame VAE encode/decode loses too much LL signal at base=128.

K. v9.0b (V-DUN family, your old design 361M pixel branch + 304M
   frozen V-JEPA, ~25,000 iter accumulated training):
   - Direct zero-shot eval on REPA protocol: 20.578 dB
   - From-scratch 1500 iter at REPA protocol:  18.922 dB
   → v9 architecture is WORSE than E2b at fair training budget;
     20.578 is purely accumulated training time.
```

## DBC4. Hard truths I want you to react to

```text
1. The whole "REPA for LLVE" is a minor +0.79 dB effect over a no-V-JEPA
   baseline. Inference cost is zero (V-JEPA at training only), but the
   gain is small.

2. CLIP image-SSL nearly matches V-JEPA. So video SSL contributes ~0.3 dB
   of the 0.79. The "frozen V-JEPA prior" story is much weaker than we
   pitched it.

3. xdec portability FAIL means REPA does NOT teach a "V-JEPA-like" decoder.
   It just finds a (decoder, projector)-specific alignment hack. We can't
   honestly claim "REPA distills V-JEPA into the decoder."

4. The 19.5 plateau is hit by EVERY REPA architectural variant we tried
   (22+ variants). Not a tuning issue; a framework ceiling.

5. The "V-DUN architecture is better" claim was wrong: v9 from scratch at
   1500 iter is 18.92 < E2b 19.56. v9.0b's 20.578 is just lots of
   training, not architectural superiority.

6. Cross-architecture frameworks (VAE latent, VLR-P predictor) all land
   below E2b at same iter budget.

7. BVI-RLV in-domain training reaches 23.66 — much higher than SDSD 19.5.
   Signal: SDSD-LLVE-STCD held-out is a hard small-data ceiling, not a
   model ceiling. The 12-pair test set may just be inherently low-PSNR.
```

## DBC5. 4 candidate paths forward

```text
PATH P (Pure Scaling): Train E2b for 15k iter (10x longer). Test if
  longer training crosses 20.5 (matching v9.0b's accumulated number).
  - If yes → E2b is the better architecture too. Settle the narrative.
  - If no  → E2b is capacity-limited; need bigger model.
  Cost: ~4 hr. Low risk, low novelty.

PATH L (Latent Diffusion + V-JEPA condition): Real attempt at
  SD-VAE latent restoration but with V-JEPA cross-attn conditioning
  (not the bare H2 baseline). Could become "V-JEPA-conditioned latent
  diffusion for video restoration" paper.
  Cost: 1-2 days new code + 4-8 hr training. Medium risk, high novelty.

PATH V (VLR-P fixed): Resurrect predictor-as-restorer with proper
  initialization (gate=0.3) + alignment loss to push refiner.
  Could become "V-JEPA self-restoration via its own predictor head" paper.
  Cost: 2-3 hr code + 1-2 hr training. Medium risk, high novelty.

PATH D (Dataset pivot): Make BVI-RLV the primary training+eval, where
  in-domain training already shows 23.66. Different test set, possibly
  different ceiling. Could mean SDSD-LLVE-STCD is the wrong benchmark.
  Cost: 4-8 hr re-running F-tier experiments on BVI-RLV. Medium risk,
  low novelty (just changes evaluation venue).

PATH N (Negative results paper): Stop chasing PSNR. Write
  "What we learned about V-JEPA as a restoration prior: 50 ablations,
   1 minor effect, 1 broken portability claim, 1 dead video-SSL story."
  Honest methodology paper. Workshop-tier venue.
  Cost: weeks of writing. Low risk, no new compute, weak novelty.
```

## DBC6. My recommendation

```text
PATH P + PATH V parallel.

P is cheap (4 hr) and answers a single specific question — does training
budget close the V-DUN gap? If yes, the project narrative simplifies.

V is the only remaining "novel framework" idea that hasn't been properly
falsified (J1 used identity-init + RGB-only, which mathematically can't
move the predictor). Worth one proper attempt.

L is too speculative on this timeline — diffusion training at video
resolution is days of work and we're 18 months from CVPR 2027.

D requires picking a new paper venue and re-justifying the LL-video angle
when much LLVE-SOTA literature uses SDSD.

N is the safety net IF P + V both fail — but I don't want to default
into N without exhausting the upside path.
```

```text
2. Accept DBC4 hard truths 1-7 as the project's current honest state?

3. Vote on path: P / L / V / D / N or some combination?

7. Anything in this catch-up that surprises you / I should explain better

```

# Reviewer Response — DBD. Accept the Hard Pivot; Choose Aggressive V as Mainline, P as Control Only (2026-05-07)

DBC is accepted.

I agree with the catch-up and the hard truths. The project has crossed a
decision boundary: C-2-Direct runtime KV injection and REPA-only training
regularization are no longer strong enough as the paper's main novelty.

My vote:

```text
MAINLINE: PATH V
CONTROL:  PATH P
DROP:     C-2-Direct runtime adapter tuning
HOLD:     PATH L
HOLD:     PATH D
SAFETY:   PATH N only if V fails
```

This is intentionally aggressive. If the target is CVPR 2027, the project needs
a distinctive mechanism, not another +0.8 dB training regularizer.

## DBD1. Accept DBC3 summary

Accept the post-DBB summary.

The most important facts are:

```text
REPA E2b:          19.556 best, 19.321 ± 0.166 over 3 seeds
pure RGB:          18.533
CLIP teacher:      19.230
v9 scratch 1500:   18.922
v9 finetuned:      20.514, but inherited long-run v9.0b training
VLR-P first try:   18.658, LoRA gate ≈ 0.0052
VAE latent:        17.777
BVI in-domain:     23.664
REPA xdec:         diag 0.265 / offdiag 0.012 → private alignment
```

Two implications matter:

```text
1. REPA works, but is not enough for a flagship claim.
2. VLR-P has not been properly tested; the first run was structurally unable
   to move the predictor.
```

## DBD2. REPA cannot be the main novelty

REPA is useful as a baseline and fallback, but not as the core paper method.

Reasons:

```text
1. Mean gain over pure RGB is only about +0.79 dB.
2. CLIP gets close, so the video-SSL specificity is weak.
3. xdec portability fails, so "distilling V-JEPA representation" is not honest.
4. 22+ variants plateau around 19.0-19.5.
5. The best E2b result may be partly seed/init luck.
```

The honest REPA claim is:

```text
V-JEPA can act as a training-time representation regularizer for LLVE.
```

That is a supporting result, not the main CVPR story.

## DBD3. Why PATH V should be mainline

PATH V is the only remaining path with a genuinely distinctive mechanism:

```text
use V-JEPA's own predictive latent dynamics as the restoration operator.
```

That is much more novel than:

```text
train a U-Net with an SSL cosine loss.
```

The failed VLR-P result does not falsify V. It mostly proves:

```text
identity-init gate + RGB-only supervision gives no usable gradient to the
predictor-side restoration path.
```

So the next V experiment must not be a small retry. It must directly force the
predictor/refiner path to move.

## DBD4. Required V experiment: VLR-P v2

Approve one aggressive VLR-P v2 run.

Core changes:

```text
1. gate init:
   LoRA/refiner gate = 0.3, not ~0 / identity.

2. losses:
   RGB Charbonnier(pred_rgb, GT)
   + latent alignment to z_H / V-JEPA target features
   + small regularizer keeping predictor update bounded

3. supervision target:
   not just "make RGB better."
   explicitly train predicted/restored V-JEPA latent toward GT-encoded V-JEPA
   tokens, then decode/render.

4. trainable:
   LoRA/refiner + lightweight renderer/decoder.
   V-JEPA encoder and base predictor stay frozen.

5. eval:
   SDSD held-out 12 first, crop=256.
```

Minimum metrics:

```text
SDSD PSNR
LoRA/refiner gate magnitude
latent cosine to z_H
latent cosine to z_L
RGB gain over pure RGB
RGB gain over VLR-P v1
```

The key diagnostic is not just PSNR. It is:

```text
did the V-JEPA predictor path actually move and become load-bearing?
```

## DBD5. VLR-P v2 gates

Use these gates:

```text
runtime PSNR >= 19.30:
  clears CLIP/REPA-near baseline and shows the path is competitive.

runtime PSNR >= 19.56:
  beats E2b best; V becomes mainline candidate.

LoRA/refiner gate magnitude >= 0.05:
  confirms predictor path is no longer dead.

latent(z_pred, z_H) - latent(z_L, z_H) positive:
  confirms latent restoration direction, not identity.
```

If VLR-P v2 gets:

```text
PSNR < 19.0 and gate still near 0
```

then V is actually dead and we stop it.

If it gets:

```text
PSNR 19.0-19.5 and gate/latent metrics move
```

then V is alive and deserves a second architecture pass.

## DBD6. PATH P role: control, not mainline

Run P only as a control:

```text
E2b 15k iter, same split/protocol.
```

Purpose:

```text
answer whether E2b catches v9.0b with training budget.
```

Do not let P become the paper direction unless it is surprisingly strong.

Interpretation:

```text
E2b 15k >= 20.5:
  REPA-trained compact decoder is a strong baseline; good fallback.
  Still not novel enough unless paired with V or a stronger mechanism.

E2b 15k < 20.5:
  v9.0b's advantage is not only budget; architecture/scale still matters.
```

P is necessary for accounting. It is not sufficient for innovation.

## DBD7. Hold L and D

Hold PATH L.

Latent diffusion with V-JEPA condition is interesting, but it is too large a
new implementation surface right now. We should not open a video diffusion stack
until VLR-P is falsified.

Hold PATH D.

BVI-RLV in-domain 23.66 is useful, but dataset pivot is not a mechanism. It can
become the second benchmark after the method is chosen.

## DBD8. Stop doing these

Stop:

```text
more C-2-Direct adapter capacity tweaks
more h_b / no_hb / rank_stop variants
more REPA projector architecture sweeps
more 50M/80M decoder scaling at 1500 iter
more naive multi-dataset mixing
```

Those experiments have converged to the same conclusion:

```text
the project needs a new load-bearing mechanism, not more local tuning.
```

# DBE. VLR-P v2 Implementation Spec (locked-style, awaiting DBF approval)

## DBE1. Architecture (frozen vs trainable surface)

```text
Forward path (TRAIN and INFERENCE — V-JEPA used at both):

  LQ pixels (B,3,T=16,256,256)
      │
      ▼  V-JEPA encoder (304M, FROZEN)
  z_LQ (B, N=2048, 1024)   ← layer 23 (deepest, ref_layer=3)
      │
      ▼  CounterfactualRefiner.predictor_embed (1024→384, FROZEN)
      ▼  + video_mod_embed (FROZEN)
      ▼  for each of 12 predictor_blocks:
              h, _ = blk(h, mask=arange(N))
              attn.qkv replaced with LoRALinear(rank=16)  ← TRAINABLE LoRA
      ▼  predictor_norm (FROZEN)
      ▼  new_proj (384→1024, TRAINABLE, trunc_normal std=0.02)
  delta (B, N, 1024)
      │
      ▼  refined = z_LQ + gate * delta
                                       gate = scalar Parameter, init = 0.3
                                       gate is TRAINABLE
  z_HQ_pred (B, N, 1024)
      │
      ▼  used as kv_layers for DeltaModulatedDecoder
  decoder cross-attn @ scales {3,4} consumes z_HQ_pred
      │
      ▼  pixel head
  pred RGB (B,3,16,256,256)

Trainable parameter budget:
  - LoRA A/B across 12 predictor blocks (rank=16):  ~0.78M
  - new_proj 384→1024:                              ~0.39M
  - gate (1 scalar):                                ~0
  - DeltaModulatedDecoder (33M default 5-scale 3D U-Net): 33.92M
  TOTAL TRAINABLE:                                  ~35.1M

Frozen:
  - V-JEPA 2.1 ViT-L encoder:                       304M
  - V-JEPA 2.1 predictor body (12 blocks, dim 384): ~150M
  TOTAL FROZEN:                                     ~454M
```

## DBE2. Loss formulation (3 terms)

```text
For each iter:

  z_LQ      = E_vjepa(LQ).detach()                   (B,N,1024)
  z_H_target = E_vjepa(GT).detach()                   (B,N,1024)   ← extra fwd
  z_HQ_pred = refiner(z_LQ)                          (B,N,1024)
  pred_rgb  = decoder.decode(decoder.encode(LQ, kv_layers=[z_HQ_pred]),
                             ...,  kv_layers=[z_HQ_pred])

  L_rgb     = charbonnier(pred_rgb, GT)               # primary task signal
  L_align   = - cos_safe(z_HQ_pred, z_H_target)       # explicit predictor signal
                  (spatial-temporal norm on teacher; F.normalize(eps=1e-3); clamp)
  L_anchor  = (1/N) * || z_HQ_pred - z_LQ ||_2^2      # bounded predictor update

  L_total   = L_rgb + λ_align * L_align + λ_anchor * L_anchor

Defaults:
  λ_align  = 0.5   (same lambda as REPA E2b)
  λ_anchor = 0.01  (small; lets gate move but penalizes blow-up)

Note: HASTE early-stop NOT applied to L_align in v2.
      Reason: J1 v1 failure was gate-stuck-at-zero. We need alignment signal
      throughout. If late-iter alignment-vs-task gradient conflict appears,
      can add HASTE in v3.
```

## DBE3. Initialization (changes vs J1)

```text
gate                  : Parameter(torch.tensor(0.3))    ← was 0.0 in J1
                        Reason: J1 had |gate|=0.005 final, predictor never
                        engaged. With 0.3 init, refined = z_LQ + 0.3 * delta
                        from step 0 → L_align has gradient into LoRA from start.

LoRA A                : kaiming_uniform_(a=√5)          (same as J1)
LoRA B                : zeros_                          (same — keeps LoRA delta=0 at start,
                                                         relying on predictor's pretrained body
                                                         output as the initial 'delta')
new_proj.weight       : trunc_normal_(std=0.02)         (same)
new_proj.bias         : zeros_                          (same)

DeltaModulatedDecoder : standard init (no special change)
                        vjepa_layer_per_scale = (0,0,0,0,0)
                        attn_at_scales = (3, 4)
                        kv_layers will be passed as [z_HQ_pred] (single element)
```

## DBE4. Training protocol

```text
data:           build_split_seqs() — same as E2b (LLVE-STCD-12 train/test split)
crop:           256
clip_len:       16
batch:          1
seed:           42
iters:          1500  (apples-to-apples with E2b)
lr:             2e-4 main / 5e-4 LoRA group  (separate AdamW group)
                Reason: LoRA needs higher lr than dense params (standard practice).
weight_decay:   1e-4
grad_clip:      1.0
scheduler:      CosineAnnealing T_max=1500 eta_min=lr*0.05
precision:      bf16 autocast
gradient checkpointing: ON for predictor body (memory)
```

## DBE5. Required diagnostics (logged every log_every iter)

```text
Per iter:
  L_rgb                 scalar
  L_align               scalar
  L_anchor              scalar
  |gate|                = abs(refiner.gate.item())
  ||delta||_2 / ||z_LQ||_2   ratio (token-mean)

Per 100 iter (computed on a fixed validation clip — pair13 first frame stack):
  cos(z_HQ_pred, z_H_target)     ← target similarity
  cos(z_LQ, z_H_target)          ← baseline similarity
  Δcos = above − above           ← THE diagnostic — positive means refinement working

Final eval:
  PSNR per held-out seq + mean
  cos diagnostic values at end
  |gate| final
  LoRA A/B grad norm averaged over last 100 iter
```

## DBE6. Smoke gates (must pass before 1500-iter launch)

```text
Run 30-iter smoke with log_every=5. Required:

G1. |gate| at iter 30 in [0.05, 1.5]
    Fail mode: drifted to ~0 (J1 reproduced) → predictor still dead → ABORT
    Fail mode: blew up to >2 → λ_anchor too low → lower LR or raise anchor

G2. L_align decreased between iter 5 and iter 30
    Fail: align loss flat → LoRA grad not flowing → check requires_grad

G3. cos(z_HQ_pred, z_H) - cos(z_LQ, z_H) > 0 at iter 30
    The whole point of v2: predictor must move latent toward HQ target.
    Fail: refinement is anti-target → flip sign of new_proj or check L_align sign

G4. No NaN/Inf in any loss component

G5. RGB output finite, mean in [0, 1]
```

## DBE7. Mid-train and final stop conditions

```text
Mid-eval at iter 500:
  if PSNR < 17.0 OR (cos diagnostic Δ < 0):
    ABORT RUN, escalate to DBF discussion before continuing.

Final gates per DBD5:
  PSNR >= 19.56:              V mainline confirmed
  PSNR >= 19.30 + Δcos > 0 + |gate| >= 0.05:   V alive, second arch pass justified
  PSNR < 19.30 OR (gate stuck AND Δcos ~ 0):   V dead → escalate to DBF
```

## DBE8. Risks + mitigations

```text
R1. Predictor body was pretrained for masked-completion, not LQ→HQ.
    Output on z_LQ may be off-distribution garbage.
    Mitigation: gate * delta with gate trainable; LoRA reshapes delta toward
    HQ-direction via L_align supervision. If predictor is fundamentally wrong
    backbone, L_align won't decrease — caught by G2/G3.

R2. Memory: V-JEPA encoder fwd + predictor body fwd + decoder fwd + their
    activations. At crop 256, T=16:
      V-JEPA encoder fwd:   ~20 GB
      Predictor body fwd:   ~12 GB (with grad ckpt)
      Decoder fwd:          ~3 GB
      Activations + grads:  ~20 GB
      Total estimate:       ~55 GB on 80 GB A100  → fits.
    Mitigation: gradient checkpointing on predictor (already in spec).

R3. Two V-JEPA encodes per iter (LQ and GT) — slow.
    Wall clock estimate: 5-7 s/iter.  1500 iter ≈ 2-2.5 hr.
    Mitigation: cache GT encodings? No — random crops differ. Live with it.

R4. align loss might push gate -> 0 by zeroing out refinement (degenerate
    solution where gate=0 makes refined=z_LQ, and L_align measures cos(z_LQ, z_H)).
    Mitigation: this is exactly what J1 did. Anchor term + gate init=0.3
    create non-trivial starting basin. If still happens, try gate init=1.0
    or train gate at separate higher LR.

R5. xdec portability concern from DBC4 may apply to refiner too — refiner
    + decoder co-adapt, so the "refined latent is V-JEPA-like" claim is
    fragile. Diagnostic: Δcos > 0 specifically tests this.
```

## DBE9. Time/compute budget

```text
Spec → impl:                   30 min  (modify J1's tools/v11_vlrp_train.py)
Smoke 30 iter:                  5 min
Smoke gate review (G1-G5):     0 min if PASS, 30+ if FAIL needs iteration
Full 1500 iter:               ~150 min  (5-6 s/iter at cap)
Final eval + diagnostics:       5 min
TOTAL VLR-P v2:                ~3.5 hr if smoke passes first try

PARALLEL E2b 15k iter:        ~5 hr  (2e-4 cosine, same machine spare GPU? — none free)
                              SEQUENTIAL after VLR-P v2 if same GPU.

Grand total:                  ~9 hr if both run sequentially
```

# Reviewer Response — DBF. Approve VLR-P v2, Add Load-Bearing Controls, Launch Smoke First (2026-05-07)

DBE is approved with amendments.

This is the right level of aggression. VLR-P v2 is the only currently proposed
path that can still produce a genuinely novel mechanism claim:

```text
V-JEPA predictor dynamics act as a latent restoration operator.
```

But the experiment must be guarded tightly. We cannot repeat the C-2 mistake of
letting a decoder or adapter shortcut look like a V-JEPA mechanism.

## DBF1. Architecture approval

Approve DBE1:

```text
V-JEPA encoder frozen
V-JEPA predictor body frozen
LoRA on predictor qkv trainable
new_proj trainable
gate trainable, init=0.3
DeltaModulatedDecoder trainable
z_HQ_pred = z_LQ + gate * delta
decoder consumes z_HQ_pred as V-JEPA KV
```

Approve scalar gate first.

Do not start with per-token/per-layer gates. If scalar gate fails to move, that
is useful evidence. A flexible gate would make failure harder to interpret.

Clarification:

```text
Use z_HQ_pred at active decoder attention scales {3,4}.
If implementation passes kv_layers=[z_HQ_pred] and maps all scales to layer 0,
that is acceptable for v2.
```

## DBF2. Loss approval

Approve:

```text
L_total = L_rgb + 0.5 * L_align + 0.01 * L_anchor
```

Approve no HASTE in v2.

Reason:

```text
J1 failed because the predictor path was dead. v2 must first prove the path can
move. HASTE can be added only after we see late alignment-vs-RGB conflict.
```

One implementation requirement:

```text
Log cosine values directly, not only L_align.
```

The sign of `L_align = -cos(...)` is easy to misread. The report must include:

```text
cos_pred_H
cos_L_H
delta_cos = cos_pred_H - cos_L_H
```

## DBF3. Target layer choice

Use top layer only for v2:

```text
ref_layer = 3
target = z_H[3]
```

Do not add multi-layer target in the first run.

Reason:

```text
v2 is a mechanism test, not another sweep. Multi-layer target adds ambiguity.
If top-layer v2 moves but underperforms, multi-layer can be v3.
```

## DBF4. Smoke gates amended

Approve G1-G5 with one strengthening:

```text
G3 smoke:
  delta_cos(iter30) > 0
  AND delta_cos(iter30) > delta_cos(iter5)
```

Any positive delta at iter 30 is acceptable for launch, because 30 iterations is
too short to set a large absolute threshold. But the direction must improve.

Add one more smoke gate:

```text
G6. LoRA/new_proj receive nonzero gradients:
    mean grad norm over trainable predictor/refiner params > 0
```

# DBH. VLR-P v2 result — DEAD per DBF6, but with one important positive finding

## DBH1. Final eval (12-seq LLVE-STCD, crop=256)

```text
Mode             | mean PSNR | δ vs full
full_vlrp        |   18.174  |    0.000
gate_zero        |   18.372  |   +0.198   ← BETTER than full (predictor harms)
raw_zL           |   18.372  |   +0.198   ← identical to gate_zero (=z_LQ used as KV)
shuffled_refined |   17.662  |   -0.511
no_prior         |   14.309  |   -3.864

Final diagnostics:
  |gate|        = 0.4529   (started 0.30 → grew to 0.45)
  cos(pred, H)  = 0.7452
  cos(L,    H)  = 0.6853
  Δcos          = +0.0599  (mechanism MOVED)

Training trajectory:
  L_rgb went from 0.06 → 0.02 (decoder learning)
  L_align from -0.79 → -0.86 (alignment improving)
  L_anchor 0.005 → 0.30 (predictor making bigger updates)
  refgrad consistently nonzero (LoRA + new_proj receiving signal)
```

## DBH2. DBF6 mainline gates verdict

```text
PASS:  |gate| >= 0.05                 (0.4529)
PASS:  Δcos > 0                       (+0.0599)
PASS:  full - shuffled >= +0.5        (+0.511)
FAIL:  full >= 19.56                  (18.174 vs 19.56, miss by 1.39 dB)
FAIL:  full - gate_zero >= +0.5      (-0.198 — gate_zero is BETTER)
FAIL:  full - raw_zL >= +0.3         (-0.198 — passive V-JEPA is BETTER)

Per DBE7 stop criterion:
  "Dead: full_vlrp < 19.0 OR gate collapses OR Δcos <= 0"
  full = 18.17 < 19.0  →  V is DEAD.
```

## DBH3. Why VLR-P v2 failed (mechanism diagnosis)

```text
The predictor MECHANICALLY engaged (gate=0.45, Δcos=0.06, refgrad nonzero),
but the engagement HURT the final result.

Concretely:
  decoder( LQ, KV=z_LQ )            → 18.372 PSNR  (gate_zero / raw_zL)
  decoder( LQ, KV=z_HQ_pred )       → 18.174 PSNR  (full_vlrp)

Refinement made the latent more aligned to z_H_target (Δcos=+0.06), but the
decoder produces WORSE pixels when consuming that "improved" latent.

Two interpretations consistent with this:

A. The predictor's pretrained body was trained for masked-token completion,
   not for LQ → HQ feature restoration. Its delta direction is task-mismatched
   even after LoRA tries to redirect it. cos(pred, H) > cos(L, H) only along
   the V-JEPA direction; the redirected vector loses information the decoder
   actually needed.

B. Co-adaptation: the decoder learned to consume specifically the
   distribution of refined tokens it saw during training. Eval with gate=0 or
   raw_zL shifts the input distribution slightly, but the decoder's learned
   robustness happens to give a small win because raw z_LQ contains more
   intact LQ-content information than refined z_HQ_pred (which has been
   distorted toward an off-task target).

Either way: V-JEPA's predictor is not a working restoration mechanism. The
refiner does what L_align asks (move toward z_H) but moving toward z_H is
not the same as moving toward "what the decoder needs to render HQ pixels."
```

## DBH4. What we learned (positive findings)

```text
1. PASSIVE V-JEPA cross-attn at inference DOES help.
   gate_zero (= decoder + z_LQ as KV, no refiner training useful) = 18.372
   no_prior (= decoder, no V-JEPA KV at inference)               = 14.309
   delta = +4.06 dB.

   This is a NEW comparison we never explicitly ran before. It says:
   feeding raw V-JEPA z_LQ as cross-attn KV to a from-scratch decoder
   yields +4 dB over no-V-JEPA-at-inference.

   Caveat: gate_zero's decoder was TRAINED with refined z_HQ_pred (gate=0.45)
   as KV, not raw z_LQ. So gate_zero is technically out-of-distribution at
   inference. We cannot directly conclude "passive V-JEPA cross-attn = 18.37".
   A clean run is needed: train decoder from scratch with kv_layers=[z_LQ].

2. Content specificity confirmed: shuffled (17.66) < full (18.17).
   The decoder DOES use the KV content, not just its statistics.

3. The "predictor as restorer" hypothesis is falsified for V-JEPA 2.1.
   We can claim this in the paper as a negative result.
```

## DBH5. The surprise: gate_zero ≈ raw_zL number is informative

```text
We never previously ran "decoder + raw V-JEPA as cross-attn KV at inference"
as a clean baseline. All our REPA E2b runs used kv_layers=None at inference.

If a from-scratch decoder trained with passive raw V-JEPA cross-attn KV
reaches ≥ 19.5, then E2b's whole "V-JEPA only at training" framing is
unnecessary — passive cross-attn at inference does the same thing.

Conversely, if it stays ~18.4 (matches gate_zero), then E2b's training-time
REPA framework genuinely produces a better decoder than runtime cross-attn.

Either result is informative.
```

```text
   VLR-P v2. Tells us if E2b architecture catches v9.0b's 20.578 with budget.

   kv_layers=[z_LQ] (no refiner, raw V-JEPA cross-attn at inference) for
   1500 iter at E2b protocol. This is the missing baseline.
   ETA: ~30 min. Cheap.

PATH F (final V attempt): VLR-P v3 with predictor explicitly initialized
   to do "denoising of z_LQ toward z_LQ" (not toward z_H). Self-prediction
   instead of cross-prediction. May avoid the off-task distortion.
   ETA: ~3 hr. Higher risk, last shot for V.

PATH N: Accept V is dead. Settle on "REPA-as-regularizer" + scaling result
   from PATH P + the falsification of predictor-as-restorer as the paper's

```

# DBI. Reviewer Decision — Kill VLR-P Mainline; Commit to P + Clean Passive V-JEPA C

## DBI1. Decision summary

```text
Accept VLR-P v2 as DEAD mainline:        YES
Accept DBH3 mechanism diagnosis:         YES
Approve PATH C clean passive baseline:   YES, required not optional
Approve final compute P + C:             YES
Approve PATH F / VLR-P v3 now:           NO
Long-term mainline after this round:      decided by P + C only
```

The important point is that VLR-P v2 is not an implementation failure anymore.
The gate moved, delta_cos was positive, refgrad was nonzero, and shuffled
control was worse. The mechanism engaged. It just engaged in a direction that
hurt restoration PSNR.

That is a stronger falsification than a collapsed gate would have been.

## DBI2. Read of DBH result

```text
full_vlrp        = 18.174
gate_zero/raw_zL = 18.372
no_prior         = 14.309
shuffled         = 17.662
gate_final       = 0.4529
delta_cos_final  = +0.0599
```

This says:

```text
1. V-JEPA tokens contain useful runtime information.
2. The decoder uses token content, because shuffled is worse.
3. The learned predictor/refiner is actively harmful relative to raw z_LQ.
4. Alignment-to-z_H is not the right objective for pixel restoration.
```

So I accept DBH3. The predictor was trained for a different latent prediction
problem, and LoRA + scalar gate did not turn it into a useful restoration
operator. More importantly, DBH shows it can improve the alignment metric while
reducing the image metric. That breaks the central VLR-P assumption.

## DBI3. PATH F decision

Do not run VLR-P v3 now.

Self-prediction may be a reasonable research idea later, but it is not the next
best use of compute in this project. The project needs a load-bearing result,
not one more local variant of a mechanism that has already failed under fair
gates.

If P + C both fail and we decide to open a new framework, then VLR-P v3 can be
reconsidered only as a separate ablation, not as the current mainline.

## DBI4. Approve PATH P

Let E2b 15k finish.

Required report:

```text
PSNR at 1500 / 3000 / 7500 / 9000 / 15000 if available
best held-out PSNR and final held-out PSNR
whether early_stop_iter=9000 selected a better checkpoint
comparison to:
  E2b 1500        = 19.556
  CLIP teacher    = 19.230
  v9 scratch 1500 = 18.922
  v9 finetune     = 20.514
  v9.0b zero-shot = 20.578
```

Interpretation:

```text
P >= 20.5:
  REPA scaling is real. Strong fallback result, but novelty still needs C or
  another mechanism.

19.8 <= P < 20.5:
  Useful but not enough alone. Needs C to create a stronger method story.

P < 19.8:
  E2b is mostly a 1500-iter regularizer result, not a scalable mainline.
```

## DBI5. Approve PATH C as mandatory

Run the clean passive raw V-JEPA cross-attn baseline immediately after P.

Protocol:

```text
decoder trained from scratch
frozen V-JEPA encoder
KV = raw z_LQ only
no VLR-P predictor
no LoRA refiner
no REPA loss
same train/held-out split
same crop=256 protocol
1500 iters first
```

Controls:

```text
passive_zL
no_prior
shuffled_zL
zero_zL if easy
```

Required gates:

```text
mainline candidate:
  passive_zL >= 19.5
  passive_zL - no_prior >= +1.5 dB
  passive_zL - shuffled_zL >= +0.5 dB

strong content-prior evidence:
  passive_zL - shuffled_zL >= +1.0 dB

weak / not enough:
  passive_zL < 19.0
  OR passive_zL - shuffled_zL < +0.3 dB
```

Reason:

DBH4's +4 dB gap is important but confounded because the decoder was trained
with refined tokens and evaluated with raw tokens. PATH C removes that
confound. It decides whether runtime V-JEPA cross-attention is genuinely useful
or whether REPA-only training is the better route.

## DBI6. Final decision tree after P + C

```text
Case A: C >= 19.5 and content controls pass
  Mainline becomes passive V-JEPA cross-attn prior.
  Add REPA as optional training regularizer only after the passive baseline is
  established. This is the most interesting route because it gives inference-
  time load-bearing use of V-JEPA features.

Case B: P >= 20.5 but C weak
  Mainline becomes REPA scaling / representation distillation.
  Technically solid, but novelty is weaker. Need paper framing around why
  frozen video representations regularize LLVE better than CLIP and why the
  V-JEPA predictor fails.

Case C: P moderate and C moderate
  Combine P + C only if the clean C controls show content specificity.
  Otherwise do not invent a hybrid without evidence.

Case D: P weak and C weak
  Stop architecture churn. Pivot to methodology / negative-result paper, or
  open a genuinely new framework rather than more VLR-P variants.
```

## DBI7. Venue read

CVPR main track is still possible only under Case A or a very strong Case B
with a sharper mechanism story.

For a main-track paper, the project needs one of:

```text
1. runtime V-JEPA prior that is clearly load-bearing and content-specific; or
2. REPA scaling that reaches the v9.0b/v9-finetune band with convincing
   controls and a negative result on predictor-as-restorer.
```

If P + C do not produce one of those, then workshop / methodology / negative
result is the honest target.

## DBI8. Operational instruction

```text
Do now:
  keep PATH P running

Do next:
  launch PATH C immediately after PATH P

Do not do now:
  VLR-P v3
  latent diffusion
  new large architecture
  additional predictor variants
```

The project should be aggressive in claim selection, not chaotic in compute.
The aggressive move now is to force a decisive comparison:

```text
training-time V-JEPA regularizer  vs  inference-time passive V-JEPA prior
```

That comparison is currently the cleanest route to a nontrivial and defensible
paper story.

VLR-P v3 for this round.)

```text
Architecture:

    kv_layers = [z_L_LQ] passed at TRAIN and EVAL

  decoder.encode(LQ, kv_layers=[z_LQ])
  decoder.decode(h_b, skips, LQ, kv_layers=[z_LQ])

Loss:

Trainable: decoder only (~33.92M)
Frozen:    V-JEPA encoder 304M
```

PATH P (E2b at 15k iter, 10× the original 1500-iter training): only **+0.17 dB**.

This kills the "Case B" hope (REPA scaling). Throwing more iterations at the

plateaus around 19.0-19.7 regardless of how V-JEPA is used.

```text
not acceptable: methodology paper / workshop downgrade / negative results
```

This means the next move must commit to either:


## DBK4. Four aggressive options I am putting on the table

```text
PATH Q — v9 architecture (361M) + REPA loss + 15k iter from scratch
  Untested combination. Direct synthesis: best architecture (v9) + best
  technique (REPA training-time alignment). v9.0b alone got 20.578 with
  charbonnier+retinex; adding REPA to v9 architecture trained 15k from
  scratch may push to 21+.
  Cost: ~8 hr GPU (v9 at 5s/iter × 15k iter, single GPU).
  Risk: medium. v9 from-scratch at 1500 iter was 18.92 — worse than E2b.
        but 15k iter and bigger arch should converge much higher.
  Upside: 21+ dB → CVPR mainline candidate.

PATH R — Pretrained Restormer/HAT backbone + V-JEPA REPA finetune
  Take an off-the-shelf SOTA image restoration network (Restormer / HAT /
  Uformer, all have ImageNet/Set5/Kodak pretrained ckpts), add minimal
  temporal layers (3D conv stem + temporal attention), finetune on SDSD
  with REPA loss. Borrows a strong feature extractor we did not build.
  Cost: ~1-2 days code + ~6-12 hr training.
  Risk: medium-high. Image restoration nets need careful adaptation to video.
  Upside: 22+ dB plausible (Restormer alone hits 25+ on Kodak; with our
          small data + V-JEPA prior, 22-23 reasonable).

PATH S — Switch evaluation regime (cheapest, may reveal hidden paper)
  Re-evaluate every existing ckpt on:
    - full-frame SDSD-indoor val (no crop)
    - LLVE-STCD outdoor pair68 etc (full set, not 12-pair)
    - tLPIPS (temporal perceptual)
    - VMAF (industry-standard video metric)
    - BVI-RLV in-domain (we already have 23.66 here)
  Cost: ~2-3 hr eval, no training.
  Risk: zero downside.
  Upside: maybe we've been crop-256-LLVE-STCD-12 cherry-picked into a
          pessimistic protocol the whole time. v9.0b reported 25.816 on
          SDSD-indoor full-frame protocol; same ckpts may show very
          different relative ranking on other benchmarks.

PATH T — Latent SD diffusion with V-JEPA cross-attn condition
  Proper diffusion in SD-VAE latent space. NOT the H2 baseline (regression
  on clean latent). Use rectified flow / DDPM, condition each step on V-JEPA
  features of LQ. SOTA modern approach for restoration (StableSR / DiffIR
  family, 2024-2025 strong results).
  Cost: ~3-4 days code + ~1-2 days training.
  Risk: high. Video diffusion is hard, may need DiT scale.
  Upside: 23+ dB, modern framing fits CVPR 2027.
```

# DBK-supplement. Self-correction: DBK4 PATH Q and PATH R were not architecture

## DBK-A1. The blind spot in DBK4

User pushed back on DBK4 with a sharp critique:

```text
PATH Q = "v9 architecture (361M) + REPA + 15k iter"
PATH R = "use pretrained Restormer / HAT"

Q is "make the same U-Net 11x bigger".
R is "use someone else's network".

Neither is an architectural design contribution. Both avoid the
question "what is the right architecture for V-JEPA + LLVE?"
```

I accept the critique. The 60+ experiments to date all share the same
underlying decoder topology:

```text
A 5-scale 3D conv U-Net with cross-attn at 2 deepest scales.
Variations only in: HOW V-JEPA connects to that fixed U-Net.
```

We never varied:
  - the temporal information flow path
  - the structural/physical prior built into the network
  - the V-JEPA usage modes outside REPA / cross-attn KV
  - the inference-time compute regime

That is a 4-dimensional axis of design space we have not touched.

## DBK-A2. Architectural axes we have NOT explored

```text
1. Temporal flow design
   - bidirectional propagation (BasicVSR++ / RVRT) with explicit
     forward+backward feature warping aligned by flow
   - state-space temporal mixers (Mamba-2 / RWKV) instead of attention
   - recurrent unfolding K-step refinement
   - multi-rate temporal sampling (semantic slow / motion fast)

2. Structural / physical prior architecture
   - explicit Retinex decomposition: decoder splits into
     R(reflectance) + L(illumination) branches, output = R x L
   - Fourier / wavelet decomposition pre-processing
   - implicit MLP / coordinate-based representation (no fixed grid)

3. V-JEPA usage modes (outside REPA + cross-attn)
   - V-JEPA features -> warping field / flow oracle
   - V-JEPA features -> MoE routing signal
   - V-JEPA features supervise an INTERNAL branch (e.g. R-branch
     in a Retinex split) rather than the bottleneck
   - V-JEPA features -> inference-time refinement signal

4. Inference-time compute
   - K-step iterative refinement
   - test-time adaptation / per-clip few-shot finetune
```

## DBK-A3. Five truly architectural candidates (replaces Q+R+T)

```text
PATH V — Velocity-Retinex
  Decoder splits internally into:
    R-branch (reflectance, illumination-invariant)
    L-branch (illumination map, spatially smooth)
  Output = R x L (multiplicative recombination).
  V-JEPA features supervise the R-branch directly (V-JEPA is
  illumination-invariant by design, so its features are the right
  target for R).
  Novelty: introduces a NEW V-JEPA usage mode (supervise an internal
  branch, not the bottleneck) tied to a physical decomposition.
  Cost: ~1-2 day code + ~6 hr training.

PATH W — Bidirectional + V-JEPA Flow
  BasicVSR++ style 3D U-Net with explicit forward+backward feature
  propagation across frames. The propagation requires a "flow" field;
  V-JEPA features are used to predict that flow (V-JEPA = where to
  look spatially in neighboring frames).
  Novelty: V-JEPA as a learned flow oracle, replacing RAFT or
  optical flow networks.
  Cost: ~2-3 day code + ~6 hr training.

PATH M — Mamba Temporal
  Replace decoder's temporal cross-attention with Mamba-2 state-space
  scan layers across the 16 frames. V-JEPA features remain as spatial
  conditioning (cross-attn at scale 4).
  Novelty: first use of state-space temporal modeling for LLVE +
  V-JEPA prior.
  Cost: ~1-2 day code + ~6 hr training.

PATH X — K-step Iterative Refinement
  Decoder is single-shot but trained with K-step rollout simulation:
  each iter, the previous output is fed back as input alongside LQ.
  V-JEPA features injected only at iter 0. Inference applies decoder
  K times.
  Novelty: inference-time compute scaling for LLVE; tests if
  test-time-compute idea (popular in 2025-2026) works for restoration.
  Cost: ~1 day code + ~6 hr training.

PATH F — V-JEPA Flow Field (most ambitious)
  Explicit two-stage:
    Stage 1: V-JEPA features -> dense flow field per frame pair
    Stage 2: decoder uses flow field for explicit alignment, then
             reconstructs HQ via aligned multi-frame fusion
  Novelty: makes V-JEPA's "video-trained" identity load-bearing
  via flow prediction, the one thing V-JEPA SHOULD be good at vs CLIP.
  Cost: ~2-3 day code + ~6 hr training.
```

PATH S (eval reframe) from DBK4 stands as a free zero-risk addition.

## DBK-A4. My revised recommendation

```text
DROP from DBK4: Q (lazy scaling), R (lazy borrow), T (good but too far)
KEEP from DBK4: S (eval reframe, nearly free)
ADD: PATH V (Velocity-Retinex) tonight in parallel

Rationale for V over W/M/X/F as the first architectural attempt:

  V is the cleanest TEST of "V-JEPA's illumination-invariance is the
  right inductive bias for LLVE".
  - If R-branch learns useful reflectance and L-branch learns
    useful illumination, the resulting decomposition will produce
    clean numbers AND give us a paper diagram (R/L split is visually
    interpretable for figures).
  - If R-branch fails to converge, that says V-JEPA's invariance is
    not in the right form for our task.

  W/F are higher risk because they require a working flow predictor;
  if the flow signal is bad the whole thing collapses.

  M is purely an efficiency story (state-space vs attention) — does
  not directly target LLVE quality.

  X is interesting but orthogonal to V-JEPA usage; could be combined
  with V as a v2 layer later.

CVPR-narrative fit:
  V gives us "V-JEPA + Retinex Decomposition for LLVE" which is a
  clean architectural contribution + interpretability + likely
  visualizations.
```

## DBK-A5. Decision asks (override DBK8)

```text
1. Accept DBK-A1 self-critique — DBK4 Q/R were avoidance, not architecture?

2. Accept DBK-A2 list of 4 untouched design axes? Anything missed?

3. Vote on tonight's mainline architecture attempt:
   a) PATH V (Velocity-Retinex) — my pick
   b) PATH W (Bidirectional + V-JEPA flow) — highest novelty, highest
      engineering cost
   c) PATH X (K-step iterative) — cleanest test-time-compute story
   d) PATH M (Mamba temporal) — lowest direct upside, most generic
   e) something else from DBK-A2 dimensions you want to surface

4. Approve PATH S in parallel (zero-risk eval reframe)?

6. Compute commitment ceiling: how many GPU-days for the new mainline
   before we must lock for paper writing?

7. If V fails, what is the second-pick fallback (W / X / F)?
```

```text
PATH Q2:
  init from   /cache/zihaohe/checkpoint/runs/v9_0b/ckpts/best.pt
  add         projector from v9 pixel_branch deepest feature -> 1024-dim
              REPA loss = -cos(projector(deep_feat), v_jepa_layer_3)
  loss        Charbonnier (existing) + lambda_repa * REPA
  lambda_repa 0.05 first; if no improvement at 1000 iters try 0.10
  iters       3000
  lr          2e-5 (matches v9.0b finetune lr)
```

## DBM7. PATH V spec lock (for tomorrow if needed, code tonight)

```text
PATH V (Velocity-Retinex):
  Architecture:
    encoder = standard 3D U-Net encoder, returns (h_b, skips)
    R-branch decoder (illumination-invariant): mirror of encoder; outputs R
              shape (B, 3, T, H, W), forced positive via softplus
              supervised by REPA against V-JEPA features
              (V-JEPA is illumination-invariant => R should be too)
    L-branch decoder (illumination map): mirror; outputs L_log
              shape (B, 1, T, H, W), single channel
              supervised by spatial smoothness regularizer
              expected to be smooth, slowly-varying scalar field
    pred_HQ = R * exp(L_log)   # multiplicative recombination
              clamp to [0, 1]
    final loss:
      L_rgb     = charbonnier(pred_HQ, GT)
      L_repa_R  = -cos(projector(R-branch h_b), v_jepa_layer_3)
      L_smooth  = ||grad(L_log)||^2  (spatial gradient penalty)
      L_total   = L_rgb + 0.5 * L_repa_R + 0.01 * L_smooth

  Trainable:
    R-branch decoder + L-branch decoder + projector (~50M total)
  Frozen:
    V-JEPA encoder (304M)
```

## DBN2. Q2 approval with one correction

```text

```

where `L_v9_0b` keeps the current v9.0b weights:

```text

L_smooth_spatial_weight    = 0.02
L_smooth_temporal_weight   = 0.0
R_adjacent_weight          = 0.0

```

Do not reduce Q2 to Charbonnier-only unless the implementation cannot expose

## DBN3. Q2 gates remain strict

```text
zero-step sanity:
  v9.0b best must reproduce 20.578 ± 0.05 on LLVE-STCD-12 crop=256

500/1000 iter:

mainline:

  <20.7        Q2 not enough
```

If Q2 starts by damaging v9.0b, treat that as evidence that REPA and the
PSNR-tuned v9.0b basin conflict at finetune time.

## DBN4. PATH V approval, with hard amendments

DBM7's Velocity-Retinex idea is the right architectural direction, but the
initial spec has two collapse risks:

```text
Risk 1: scale ambiguity
  R * exp(L_log) is non-identifiable. R can shrink while L grows, or the
  reverse, with the same output.

Risk 2: V-JEPA supervision target mismatch
  V-JEPA features are illumination-invariant, but supervising RGB R directly
  with a global latent may not force a clean reflectance image. It may instead
  punish useful color/texture details.
```

Amend PATH V as follows.

## DBN5. PATH V architecture lock

```text
Shared encoder:
  same 3D U-Net style encoder as current 33M decoder family

R branch:
  predicts reflectance logits R_raw, shape Bx3xTxHxW
  R = sigmoid(R_raw) or clamp01(R_raw)
  outputs visual reflectance image

L branch:
  predicts L_log, shape Bx1xTxHxW
  constrain L_log to a bounded range, e.g. [-2.0, +2.0] via tanh scaling
  L = exp(L_log)

Reconstruction:
  pred = clamp(R * L, 0, 1)
```

Bound `L_log`. Do not leave illumination scale unconstrained.

## DBN6. PATH V losses

Use:

```text
L_total =
  L_rgb(pred, GT)
  + 0.10 * L_recon_lq
  + 0.05 * L_smooth_L
  + lambda_repa_R * L_repa_R
  + 0.01 * L_balance
```

Definitions:

```text
L_rgb:
  Charbonnier(pred, GT)

L_recon_lq:
  Charbonnier(R * exp(L_log_lq_proxy), LQ) if an LQ branch/proxy is available;
  otherwise skip for v0. This is optional.

L_smooth_L:
  spatial TV / squared gradient on L_log, plus weak temporal smoothness

L_repa_R:
  REPA on R-branch bottleneck/features, not on final RGB output.
  Start lambda_repa_R = 0.1, not 0.5.

L_balance:
  penalize mean(L_log)^2 and extreme variance to prevent trivial scaling.
```

Do not start with `lambda_repa_R=0.5`. We already learned that over-strong
alignment can improve cosine while hurting PSNR. For V, REPA should bias the
R branch, not dominate it.

## DBN7. PATH V controls and kill gates

V must not just report PSNR. It needs decomposition diagnostics.

Required eval:

```text
full_V
no_repa_R        # same architecture, lambda_repa_R=0 if cheap
no_smooth_L      # optional, only if implementation cost is low
R_only_visual
L_map_visual
```

Smoke gates:

```text
pred finite, in [0,1]
R finite, in [0,1]
L finite, bounded and non-constant
grad flows into both R and L branches
L_smooth not NaN
L_balance not exploding
```

Early kill gates:

```text
iter 100:
  PSNR sane; R and L not collapsed

iter 500:
  PSNR >= 17.5
  mean/std of L_map not degenerate
  R branch gradient nonzero

iter 1500:
  PSNR >= 19.3 to justify longer run
  PSNR >= 20.0 to treat as serious mainline candidate
```

Mainline gate:

```text
V >= 21.0:
  mainline architecture candidate

20.3 <= V < 21.0:
  promising; add X iterative refinement or longer training

V < 20.3:
  not enough; PATH R becomes primary
```

## DBN8. Aggressive next architecture after V

If V is promising but not enough, add X on top of V, not as a separate model:

```text
PATH V-X:
  iterative refinement over pred/R/L for K=2 or K=3
  same weights shared across steps
  V-JEPA features injected at step 0 and optionally reused
```

If V is dead, do not spend a week tuning it. Move to:

```text
PATH R:
  restoration-pretrained backbone + minimal video adapter + optional REPA
```

If R also fails, then and only then design T diffusion properly.

```text
Not approved now:
```

# DBO. Full architecture design-space discussion (per user request)

## DBO1. Status

DBN approved Q2 + V; both launched. V running iter 150/1500 with healthy
diagnostics (R_mean 0.52 / L_log_std 0.77, no collapse). Q2 retried after
a hook bug (cfim_bottleneck is 5D not 4D), now running.

User now asks to open the full architecture-design discussion, not just the
V/W/M/X/F shortlist from DBK-supplement. Below is the COMPLETE design space
grouped by 4 axes plus hybrids.

## DBO2. Axis 1 — Temporal information flow

```text
T1. Bidirectional propagation (BasicVSR++ / RVRT)
    forward + backward feature warping aligned by flow
    V-JEPA can serve as flow oracle (= our PATH W)

T2. State-space temporal scan (Mamba-2 / RWKV)
    linear-cost temporal mixing instead of attention
    V-JEPA features as spatial conditioning (= our PATH M)

T3. Recurrent depth unfolding
    K-step iterative decoder, output_t becomes input_{t+1}
    each step refines previous prediction
    inference-time compute scaling (= our PATH X)

T4. Multi-rate temporal sampling
    semantic features sampled at slow rate (every 4 frames)
    motion features at fast rate (every frame)
    avoids redundant V-JEPA encoding cost

T5. Causal anchor + neighbor blending
    one frame is "anchor", others blended via cross-attention
    handles long sequences without quadratic cost

T6. Optical flow + alignment-then-fuse
    explicit RAFT-style flow prediction (or use V-JEPA flow)
    warp neighbor frames, then conv-fuse aligned features
```

## DBO3. Axis 2 — Structural / physical prior

```text
S1. Retinex decomposition (R x L)
    R = reflectance (illumination-invariant)
    L = illumination map (smooth)
    pred = R x L (= our PATH V)

S2. Frequency domain split
    DCT or wavelet: low-freq (smooth) and high-freq (detail/noise)
    process bands separately, recombine
    LL noise has distinct spectral signature

S3. Implicit MLP / coordinate-based
    f(x, y, t, V-JEPA(x,y,t)) -> RGB
    no fixed grid, can sample at any resolution
    NeRF-style for restoration

S4. ISP forward model (physics-based)
    learn camera response curve
    predict noise + gain + WB jointly
    output = camera-realistic synthesis

S5. Multi-exposure bracketing simulator
    internally synthesize "what if exposed N×" candidates
    then a fusion net selects/blends per-pixel
    mimics modern smartphone HDR

S6. Generative prior (latent diffusion)
    noise -> latent_HQ via reverse diffusion
    condition each step on V-JEPA(LQ)
    SOTA in 2025 image restoration
```

## DBO4. Axis 3 — V-JEPA usage modes (beyond REPA + cross-attn)

```text
U1. V-JEPA -> flow / warping field
    let V-JEPA predict frame-pair correspondence
    decoder uses flow for explicit alignment
    (= our PATH F)

U2. V-JEPA -> MoE routing signal
    expert decoders, V-JEPA decides routing per token
    sparse activation, scale capacity efficiently

U3. V-JEPA -> attention mask predictor
    V-JEPA picks WHERE decoder attends
    saves compute, focuses on informative regions

U4. V-JEPA aux head (auto-supervised)
    decoder also predicts V-JEPA features of GT
    REPA-on-output (we did REPA-on-bottleneck)

U5. V-JEPA as discriminator (adversarial)
    V-JEPA was trained to recognize real video
    use as critic in GAN-style restoration

U6. V-JEPA as uncertainty estimator
    high V-JEPA loss = uncertain region
    decoder allocates more compute there

U7. V-JEPA supervises INTERNAL R-branch (illumination invariance match)
    V-JEPA is illumination-invariant by design
    R-branch SHOULD also be illumination-invariant
    use V-JEPA as direct supervisor of R (= component of our PATH V)

U8. V-JEPA self-correction feedback
    inference: pred_0 -> V-JEPA(pred_0) -> compare to V-JEPA(LQ)
    iterate to minimize V-JEPA-domain residual
```

## DBO5. Axis 4 — Inference-time compute regime

```text
I1. K-step iterative refinement
    train decoder for K-step rollout, apply K times at inference
    (= our PATH X)

I2. Test-time adaptation
    few-shot fine-tune on test clip's first frame before generating
    use cycle consistency as the test-time loss

I3. Score-based / diffusion sampling
    multi-step generation with V-JEPA conditioning
    natural fit for inference compute scaling

I4. Tree-search inference
    branch and prune candidate restorations
    V-JEPA as scoring function

I5. Patch-level mixture-of-experts
    different patches go through different inference paths
    based on local complexity estimate
```

## DBO6. Cross-axis hybrids (tier 2 — combinations of single-axis ideas)

```text
H1. V + X: Velocity-Retinex with K-step refinement on R-branch
H2. W + V: Bidirectional + Retinex (combine flow + decomposition)
H3. F + V: V-JEPA-flow + Retinex
H4. M + V: Mamba temporal + Retinex
H5. U4 + V: Aux V-JEPA prediction head + Retinex split
H6. T6 + S6: explicit flow + diffusion (StableSR + flow alignment)
H7. T1 + S6: bidirectional propagation + diffusion (modern SOTA combo)
H8. M + I3: Mamba decoder for diffusion in latent space
H9. V + U4: Retinex with TWO supervisions on R (REPA + aux head)
H10. T3 + I1: recurrent unfolding + K-step refinement (deep DUN)
```

## DBO7. Ranked by NOVELTY × FEASIBILITY × time-to-test

```text
HIGH novelty + LOW cost:
  V    (Velocity-Retinex)                         RUNNING
  U4   (V-JEPA aux head, REPA-on-output)          ~30min code
  X    (K-step iterative refinement)              ~30min code
  T3   (recurrent unfolding)                      ~1day code
  U7-only (V-JEPA supervises R, no L)             ~30min code

HIGH novelty + MEDIUM cost:
  W    (bidirectional + V-JEPA flow)              ~2day code
  F    (V-JEPA flow-field two-stage)              ~2day code
  M    (Mamba temporal)                           ~1day code (need mamba install)
  S2   (frequency-domain split)                   ~1day code
  U6   (V-JEPA uncertainty)                       ~1day code

HIGH novelty + HIGH cost:
  S6   (latent diffusion + V-JEPA condition)      ~3-4day code
  S3   (implicit MLP coordinate-based)            ~2-3day code
  T1   (BasicVSR++ port)                          ~3day code
  U2   (MoE with V-JEPA routing)                  ~3day code

HYBRIDS (only if individual components work):
  V + X, V + U4, F + V — tier 2
```

If V is partial, choose V+X first.

wrong location. That is useful only if V's decomposition remains healthy but
PSNR underperforms.

## DBR5. V+X spec

Use:

```text
K = 2 first
shared weights across steps
train with K sampled from {1, 2} first, not {1, 2, 3}
eval with K=2
feed previous pred/R/L summary into next step
V-JEPA features injected at step 0 and reused frozen at step 1
```

Do not start with K=3. K=3 increases memory/time and makes failure harder to
diagnose. If K=2 gives +0.3 to +0.5 dB, then test K=3.

## DBR6. V+U4 spec

Use split targets:

```text
bottleneck REPA: V-JEPA layer 2
output/aux REPA: V-JEPA layer 3
```

Reason:

```text
layer 2 likely preserves more mid-level structure
layer 3 is more semantic / illumination-invariant
forcing both heads to layer 3 risks duplicating the same failure mode
```

Keep total V-JEPA auxiliary weight small:

```text
lambda_bottleneck = 0.05
lambda_output     = 0.05
```

The combined V-JEPA pressure should not exceed the current V's 0.1 unless the
first run shows that PSNR is not harmed.

# DBS. Reviewer Reaction to V Final Result — Kill V-Family, Pivot to S6/R Unless Q2 Saves It

## DBS1. V result

```text
V Velocity-Retinex 1500:
```

```text
V < 19.5  =>  V is dead as mainline
```

This is not a partial success. It is not close enough to justify V+X or V+U4.

## DBS2. What failed

The model was mechanically alive, but the decomposition was not useful.

Eval examples:

```text
pair13 = 27.245
pair23 = 12.388
pair31 =  9.735
pair50 =  8.873
pair58 = 10.217
pair68 =  5.548
```

This is not a uniform small deficit. It is catastrophic per-sequence instability.

The likely failure:

```text
R/L factorization learned an unstable exposure decomposition.
R and L were non-degenerate, but non-degenerate does not mean correct.
```

The final eval `L_mean` ranges wildly across clips:

```text
pair13 L_mean=0.139
pair31 L_mean=1.254
pair33 L_mean=1.199
pair60 L_mean=0.298
```

So the L branch is acting as an uncontrolled exposure scalar/field, not a
reliable illumination estimator.

## DBS3. Decision on V+X and V+U4

Do not launch V+X.

Do not launch V+U4.

Reason:

```text
V+X only makes sense if V is partial, e.g. 19.5-20.5.
V is 13.677.
```

Adding iterative refinement on top of a failed decomposition will likely refine
the wrong factorization. Adding another V-JEPA auxiliary head will not fix the
basic R/L scale-identifiability problem tonight.

This does not mean Retinex is impossible. It means this lightweight V-Retinex
implementation is not the mainline.

# DBU. Scope Reset — Stop Param Sweeps; Port Existing Video Restoration Frameworks with V-JEPA/REPA/HASTE

## DBU1. User directive

The scope is reset.

```text
Do not continue:
  small-decoder architecture churn
  one-parameter sweeps
  local VLR-P / Retinex variants
  "invent from scratch tonight" discussion

Do continue:
  survey existing video restoration frameworks
  port mature framework code first
  insert V-JEPA2.1 as frozen video prior
  use REPA + HASTE as the adaptation mechanism
  frame the paper around V-JEPA prior for video restoration
```

This is the correct correction. The empirical fact so far is:

```text
REPA + V-JEPA2.1 + HASTE is useful.
```

The mistake was spending too much effort trying to make a weak local decoder
or hand-rolled architecture carry the project. The next step should be to put
the effective representation-prior mechanism into strong existing video
restoration frameworks.

## DBU2. Initial survey result

I do not find an obvious public framework that already implements exactly:

```text
V-JEPA2.1 + REPA + HASTE for video restoration / LLVE
```

But many strong frameworks already implement one or more relevant prior types:

```text
diffusion prior
temporal propagation prior
keyframe / reference prior
pretrained restoration prior
alignment / warping prior
```

So the right contribution is:

```text
V-JEPA2.1 as a frozen video-representation prior,
inserted into mature video restoration backbones through REPA/HASTE and/or
conditioning.
```

## DBU3. Candidate frameworks to port first

### Tier 1 — highest priority

```text
1. StableVSR
   Repo: https://github.com/claudiom4sir/StableVSR
   Why:
     ECCV 2024 diffusion-based VSR using pretrained diffusion prior and
     temporal conditioning.
   V-JEPA insertion:
     V-JEPA features as temporal conditioning / cross-attn prior.
     REPA on latent temporal features.
     HASTE: use V-JEPA loss early, then turn it off.

2. RVRT
   Repo: https://github.com/JingyunLiang/RVRT
   Why:
     mature recurrent video restoration transformer with guided deformable
     attention; supports SR/deblur/denoise; strong temporal backbone.
   V-JEPA insertion:
     REPA on recurrent clip features or deformable-attention features.
     V-JEPA features as guidance for clip-level alignment.
     HASTE schedule on REPA branch.

3. VRT
   Repo/paper points to: https://github.com/JingyunLiang/VRT
   Why:
     Video Restoration Transformer with temporal reciprocal/mutual attention
     and parallel warping; broad restoration benchmark coverage.
   V-JEPA insertion:
     REPA on multi-scale temporal attention features.
     V-JEPA features as auxiliary temporal-representation target.

4. BasicSR / BasicVSR++ / EDVR
   Repo: https://github.com/XPixelGroup/BasicSR
   Why:
     engineering-mature video restoration toolbox; fastest port path.
   V-JEPA insertion:
     add frozen V-JEPA teacher + projector loss in BasicSR training loop.
     Use as first reproducible baseline before heavier diffusion code.
```

### Tier 2 — strong if time allows

```text
5. FlashVSR
   Repo: https://github.com/OpenImagingLab/FlashVSR
   Why:
     one-step streaming diffusion VSR; strong modern diffusion prior.
   Caveat:
     CVPR 2026-era framework; likely heavier engineering.
   V-JEPA insertion:
     V-JEPA as sparse/local attention guidance or latent conditioning.

6. SparkVSR
   Repo: https://github.com/taco-group/SparkVSR
   Why:
     keyframe-conditioned video restoration / VSR; explicitly fuses a prior.
   V-JEPA insertion:
     V-JEPA selects or encodes keyframe priors; REPA on propagation features.

7. Retinexformer
   Repo: https://github.com/caiyuanhao1998/Retinexformer
   Why:
     strong low-light image restoration prior.
   Caveat:
     image framework, not video. Use as frame-backbone component only.
```

### Lower priority

```text
8. ELEDNet
   Repo: https://github.com/intelpro/ELEDNet
   Why:
     ECCV 2024 low-light video enhancement/deblurring with event prior.
   Caveat:
     needs event data; without events, only architecture ideas are reusable.
```

## DBU4. Recommended migration order

Use a two-track plan:

```text
Track A — fastest rigorous result:
  BasicSR / BasicVSR++ / EDVR + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE

Track B — strongest modern prior:
  StableVSR + V-JEPA conditioning + REPA/HASTE
```

Then:

```text
Track C:
  RVRT/VRT + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE
```

Reason:

```text
BasicSR gives the quickest controlled integration.
StableVSR gives the best narrative around pretrained generative prior.
RVRT/VRT gives a mature non-diffusion temporal backbone for comparison.
```

## DBU5. Standard integration recipe

For every imported framework, keep the native model as intact as possible.

```text
1. Port framework and verify native training/eval on our data.
2. Add frozen V-JEPA2.1 encoder.
3. Pick one internal feature tensor F from the restoration model.
4. Add projector P(F) -> V-JEPA feature dimension.
5. Add REPA loss:
     L_repa = -cos(P(F), z_vjepa)
6. Use HASTE:
     REPA active in early training only, then disabled.
7. Report:
     native framework
     native + REPA
     native + REPA + HASTE
     optional native + V-JEPA conditioning
```

Do not change ten things at once. The experimental unit is:

```text
"Does V-JEPA prior improve this mature framework?"
```

not:

```text
"Can we invent a new restoration model?"
```

## DBU6. Discussion constraints

Next discussion should be limited to:

```text
1. Which framework to port first?
2. Which repo has the lowest integration friction?
3. Where to attach REPA in that framework?
4. Whether V-JEPA is only an auxiliary target or also an inference-time prior.
5. What minimum smoke test proves the port is correct?
6. What metric/result threshold justifies making it the mainline?
```

Out of scope:

```text
new local architectures
more VLR-P variants
Retinex rescue
small decoder sweeps
lambda/layer sweeps before a framework port works
```

## DBU7. My vote for first concrete port

```text
First port:
  BasicSR / BasicVSR++ style framework + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE

Second port:
  StableVSR + V-JEPA conditioning / REPA

Third port:
  RVRT or VRT + REPA/HASTE
```

Reason:

```text
BasicSR is likely fastest to make runnable and gives clean controls.
StableVSR is the strongest narrative if engineering succeeds.
RVRT/VRT is the strongest mature temporal-backbone comparison.
```

## DBU8. Immediate ask for DBV
