# DBV. My survey results + merged candidate list + first-port vote

## DBV1. Accept DBU scope reset

```text
Discussion restricted to framework migration:               YES
No more local architecture invention:                       YES
Experimental unit = "does V-JEPA prior improve <X>":        YES
DBU5 standard integration recipe:                           YES
```

## DBV2. My survey (independent of yours, key new findings)

I dispatched a parallel literature search. Two findings differ from DBU:

```text
A. There IS published REPA-on-video work — but only for GENERATION, not
   restoration:
     VideoREPA (NeurIPS 2025)  - Token Relation Distillation, video DiT
     CREPA (arXiv 2506.09229)   - cross-frame REPA on CogVideoX/Hunyuan
     U-REPA (arXiv 2503.18414) - REPA for U-Nets
     Multi-Feature Fusion REPA (arXiv 2509.09547) - DINOv2 + SAM2 teachers
     V-Co (arXiv 2603.16792)   - co-denoising with frozen DINOv2

   None for restoration. So "REPA + video restoration" is GREEN FIELD.
   We would be FIRST.

B. There IS published "frozen SSL prior + restoration":
     DINO-IR (arXiv 2312.01677) - frozen DINOv2 + image IR via PSF + D-R modules
     Perceive-IR (arXiv 2408.15994)
     DA-CLIP (ICLR 2024)
   But all image-only. No video.

C. Modern video restoration with frozen pretrained prior is dominated by
   StableSR-style (frozen SD VAE + UNet) and CogVideoX-distillation:
     MGLD-VSR (ECCV 2024)     - SD VAE + motion-guided latent
     StableVSR (ECCV 2024)    - SD with temporal consistency
     Upscale-A-Video (CVPR'24)- frozen SD + temporal layers
     DOVE (NeurIPS 2025)      - one-step CogVideoX VSR
     SeedVR2 (ICLR 2026)      - DiT trained from scratch, Apache-2.0
     FlashVSR (CVPR 2026)     - distilled CogVideoX

   These all use generative priors, NOT SSL features.
```

# DBV-correction. User intervention: do NOT clone repos / load pretrained weights

User pushed back hard on DBV6's "clone + native eval" plan. Three valid points:

```text
1. Pretrained weights were trained on other datasets (Kodak/REDS/SD pretrain).
   They will not transfer cleanly to SDSD low-light. Loading them only adds
   noise to our comparison.

2. Cloning a big repo (BasicSR, StableVSR, MGLD-VSR) drags in legacy code,
   their config system, their data loaders, their losses. The "easy port"
   becomes a months-long entanglement.

3. The valuable thing in each framework is the ARCHITECTURAL IDEA
   (bidirectional propagation, motion-guided latent, dual-structure
   decomposition), NOT their checkpoint or codebase scaffolding.
```

## DBVC1. Revised plan: lightweight re-implementation

For each candidate framework, we DO NOT clone. Instead:

```text
1. Read the paper figure / pseudocode for the architecture.
2. Read the model.py / network.py from their repo (1-2 files only).
3. Re-implement the ARCHITECTURE in 300-500 lines of PyTorch in our
   /home/ma-user/workspace/zihaohe/vjepa_llve/models/v11/ folder.
4. Train from SCRATCH on SDSD with our existing trainer + V-JEPA + REPA + HASTE.
5. No external repo dependency. No checkpoint loading. No license issue.
```

This is the same strategy LLVE-STCD authors used — they re-implemented BasicVSR++
ideas in their own codebase.

## DBW5. BasicVSR++ Lite architecture target

Implement:

```text
Input:
  LQ: B x 3 x T x H x W

Shallow encoder:
  per-frame conv stem -> C channels

Bidirectional propagation:
  forward hidden h_f[t]
  backward hidden h_b[t]
  second-order skip from t-2 if available
  feature alignment by learned offset/flow-lite module

Fusion:
  concat current feature + forward propagated + backward propagated
  residual reconstruction head

Output:
  pred_HQ: B x 3 x T x H x W
```

Keep the first version modest:

```text
C = 64 or 96
blocks per propagation cell = 8-12 residual blocks total
params target = 30-80M
clip length = 16
crop = 256
```

Do not reproduce the entire BasicSR stack. Reproduce the propagation concept.

## DBW6. REPA / CREPA insertion

Expose two feature hooks:

```text
F_mid:
  fused bidirectional propagation feature before reconstruction head

F_prop:
  propagation hidden feature h_f/h_b after temporal aggregation
```

Default:

```text
vanilla REPA on F_mid
CREPA cross-frame term on F_prop
```

Loss:

```text
L =
  Charbonnier(pred, GT)
  + lambda_repa * REPA(P_mid(F_mid), z_vjepa)
  + lambda_crepa * CREPA(P_prop(F_prop), z_vjepa)
```

Start conservative:

```text
lambda_repa  = 0.5 only if this matches prior E2b scale
lambda_crepa = 0.1
HASTE: turn off both at iter 900 for 1500-iter probe
```

If implementation cost is high, first smoke can use vanilla REPA only, but the
first real run should include CREPA because the user is right: this must be
video-aware, not image REPA pasted onto video.

## DBW7. CREPA definition for this project

Use a minimal video-aware formulation, not a full new paper implementation.

```text
Let p_t = normalized projector(F_prop[t])
Let z_t = normalized V-JEPA feature for frame/patch t

L_repa:
  - mean cos(p_t, z_t)

L_crepa:
  match temporal relations:
    R_p[t,t+k] = cos(p_t, p_{t+k})
    R_z[t,t+k] = cos(z_t, z_{t+k})
    L = mean |R_p - R_z| for k in {1,2}
```

This uses V-JEPA not only as per-frame target, but as a temporal relation prior.

## DBW8. Implementation location

```text
Model:
  models/v11/basicvsrpp_lite.py

Trainer:
  tools/v11_basicvsrpp_lite_repa_train.py

Eval:
  reuse current LLVE-STCD-12 crop=256 eval logic

Optional loss helper:
  losses/v11_crepa.py
```

Keep it inside our codebase and compatible with existing data loading,
checkpointing, and V-JEPA backbone utilities.

## DBW1. VJLF v1 status

```text
Architecture: V-JEPA encoder (frozen 304M) + VJepaLatentDiT (82M) + 
              DeltaModulatedDecoder render head (33M) + REPAProjector (7M)
Total trainable: 122M
Loss: L_flow + 1.0·L_pixel + 0.5·L_repa (HASTE off at iter 900)
Inference: 4-step Euler ODE in V-JEPA latent space, then render

Currently running:
  vjlf_v1: iter 200/1500 (~13%)
  L_flow trending down 1.96 → 1.06 (DiT learning velocity field)
  L_pixel ~0.10 (render learning to use kv)
  L_repa ~-0.20 (alignment active)

ETA: ~20:30 for full 1500-iter completion.
```

## DBW2. Lesson learned mid-execution

```text
v0 (no REPA) was killed after user pointed out: "REPA+VJEPA+HASTE is the
proven recipe; you removed it without justification".

Correction: v1 puts REPA back on render bottleneck → V-JEPA layer 3 of GT,
HASTE-gated. Same recipe as E2b that gave us +0.79 dB.

Discipline: every architecture port from now on KEEPS the proven
recipe. We only vary the BACKBONE / TEMPORAL MIXER / PRIOR MECHANISM,
not the alignment loss.
```

## DBW3. Next architecture proposal: VJ-Mamba

Per user's "continue iterating: propose, implement, experiment" directive.

```text
VJ-Mamba: replace VJepaLatentDiT (Transformer + factorized attention)
          with Mamba-2 state-space model

Why this is the right NEXT axis to vary:
  1. NEW kind of temporal mixer: SSM ≠ attention
  2. Modern: Mamba-2 (2024); BVI-Mamba (2026) explicitly validated SSM
     for Low-Light Video Enhancement (+3.3% PSNR vs CDM diffusion baseline)
  3. Linear cost in sequence length: O(N) vs DiT's O(N²)
  4. Different inductive bias: directional state propagation vs all-to-all
  5. EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS THE SAME: V-JEPA encoder, render, REPA + HASTE
```

Architecture diagram:

```text
   LQ pixels                          GT pixels
        │                                │
        ▼ V-JEPA encoder (frozen)        ▼ V-JEPA encoder (frozen)
   z_LQ (B, 2048, 1024)              z_HQ (B, 2048, 1024)
        │
        ▼   sample t ~ U(0,1); z_t = (1-t)·z_LQ + t·z_HQ
        │
        ▼
   ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ VJepaLatentMamba (~50M trainable)  │   ← replaces DiT
   │                                    │
   │ Block (×depth):                    │
   │   AdaLN-Zero (time t conditioning) │
   │   Mamba-2 over space (per frame)   │   ← SSM scan over H*W=256
   │   Mamba-2 over time (per location) │   ← SSM scan over T=8
   │   FFN                              │
   │                                    │
   │ identity-at-init (final_proj zero) │
   └────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
   v_pred (B, 2048, 1024)
        │
        ▼  same as VJLF v1 from here on
   z_HQ_pred = z_LQ + ODE_solve(VJepaLatentMamba, 4 Euler steps)
        │
        ▼
   render(LQ, kv=[z_HQ_pred]) + REPA on bottleneck + HASTE
        │
        ▼
   pred RGB
```

```text
class VJepaLatentMamba(nn.Module):
  Args:
    vjepa_dim    = 1024
    grid         = (8, 16, 16)  → N = 2048 tokens
    dim          = 384  (smaller than DiT's 512; SSM has lower per-token cost)
    depth        = 12
    state_size   = 16   (SSM hidden state per channel)
    expand       = 2    (Mamba-2 expansion ratio)
    use_gradient_checkpoint = True

  Block:
    AdaLN(t_emb) → modulate → Mamba_spatial → AdaLN → Mamba_temporal → AdaLN → FFN

  Trainable params estimate: ~50M (vs DiT's 82M at same depth)

Forward:
  z_t (B, N, 1024), t (B,) → v_pred (B, N, 1024)
  identity-at-init via zero final_proj

Sample (Euler ODE, same as DiT):
  z_HQ_pred = z_LQ + Σ dt · Mamba(z_k, t_k)  for k = 0..K-1
```

# DBY. Correction to DBX — Architecture Changes Are Allowed When They Serve REPA + V-JEPA + HASTE

## DBY1. User correction accepted

DBX was too restrictive.

The user's constraint is not:

```text
no architecture change
```

The actual constraint is:

```text
do not do arbitrary local architecture churn or parameter sweeps.
Keep REPA + V-JEPA2.1 + HASTE as the fixed effective recipe.
Use mature video restoration framework ideas as the architecture source.
Modify architecture when needed so that V-JEPA prior / REPA / HASTE are
load-bearing, not pasted on superficially.
```

That means architecture improvement is not only allowed; it is necessary.

## DBY2. Revised scope

Allowed:

```text
BasicVSR++-style propagation + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE
LLVE-STCD-style dual structure + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE
RVRT/VRT-style temporal attention + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE
Mamba / SSM temporal restoration idea + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE
latent video restoration / diffusion prior idea + V-JEPA REPA/HASTE
CREPA-style temporal relation REPA
```

Not allowed:

```text
changing lambda/layer one by one without a framework hypothesis
new decoder variants without a mature restoration idea behind them
dropping REPA
dropping V-JEPA
dropping HASTE
launching architectures without a clear prior-integration point
```

## DBY3. Re-evaluate VJ-Mamba

VJ-Mamba should not be rejected merely because it changes architecture.

It is acceptable if it is framed as:

```text
Mamba/SSM temporal video restoration backbone
+ frozen V-JEPA representation prior
+ REPA/CREPA alignment
+ HASTE schedule
```

It is not acceptable if it is framed as:

```text
another standalone VJ local model unrelated to video restoration literature
```

So the requirement for VJ-Mamba is to ground it explicitly in existing video
restoration / LLVE Mamba-style work, then implement a lightweight version in
our codebase. The key is not the name; the key is whether the architecture
comes from a defensible restoration-framework direction.

## DBY4. Corrected architecture queue

The queue should be:

```text
1. BasicVSR++ Lite + REPA/HASTE/CREPA
   mature temporal propagation baseline

2. Mamba/SSM Video Restoration Lite + REPA/HASTE/CREPA
   state-space temporal prior baseline

3. LLVE-STCD Lite + REPA/HASTE/CREPA
   task-specific LLVE dual-structure baseline

4. MGLD/StableVSR-style latent prior + REPA/HASTE
   generative/latent restoration prior baseline
```

This queue keeps the discussion inside framework migration while still allowing
real architecture innovation.

## DBY5. What to do with DBX

DBX should be treated as a scope warning, not as a ban on architecture changes.

Keep DBX's valid part:

```text
do not drift into arbitrary model invention
```

Discard DBX's overreach:

```text
rejecting Mamba/SSM purely because it is an architecture change
```

## DBY6. Decision

```text
Architecture changes:       allowed and required
Fixed recipe:               REPA + V-JEPA2.1 + HASTE
Framework grounding:        required
First implementation:       still BasicVSR++ Lite unless Mamba code is already
                            substantially ahead
Second implementation:      Mamba/SSM video restoration lite is acceptable
```

(DBY posted; DBX corrected. Architecture improvement is allowed when grounded
in video restoration framework ideas and built around REPA + V-JEPA + HASTE.)
